                 HR – SUBSTANCE FREE WORKPLACE – POLICY

Document Control

Title: HR – Substance Free Workplace – Procedure – Philippines
Description: Procedure addressing substance-free workplace requirements, mandatory
substance testing, disciplinary action, treatment, rehabilitation, and referral for RealPage
Philippines employees.
Document Type: Procedure
Document Code: HR-POL-15
Owner: HR
Audience: All RealPage Philippines employees
Country: Philippines
System of Record: UKG People Articles
Version Number: 1.1
Last Review Date: 01 May 2024
Effective Date: 01 June 2024
Approval Date: 01 June 2024
Approver: Ivy De Borja
Classification: Internal Use
Document Status: Final
Next Review Date: 17 August 2027

I. Overview & Objective

RealPage is committed to providing a safe and productive work environment. Alcohol and
drug abuse pose a threat to the health and safety of employees and to the security of our
equipment and facilities. For these reasons, RealPage is committed to the elimination of
drug and/or alcohol use and abuse in the workplace.

The presence of any detectable amount of dangerous drugs or alcohol in the employee's
system while at work, while on the premises of RealPage, or while on official business.
“Dangerous Drugs” include those listed in the Schedules annexed to the 1961 Single
Convention on Narcotic Drugs, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, and in the Schedules
annexed to the 1971 Single Convention on Psychotropic Substances as enumerated in the
attached annex of R.A. 9165.

II. Scope

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

This process applies to all RealPage Philippines employees.

III. Responsibilities

1. Employer’s Responsibility

RealPage prohibits the use, possession, distribution, solicitation for, or sale of dangerous
drugs and alcohol on company premises or while performing an assignment.

2. Employee’s Responsibility

All employees are expected to properly represent the company at all times, even when
alcohol may be present during business events or activities. All employees are not allowed
to use, be in possession of, distribute, solicit for, or sell dangerous drugs and alcohol on
company premises or while performing an assignment.

3. Assessment Team

The Assessment Team is comprised of the OSH-certified committee, including designated
OSH Officers, Senior HRBP and/or HRBPs, who will address all aspects of drug abuse
prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation.

IV. Definition of Terms

N.A.

V. Process Details

1. Mandatory Substance Test

To ensure that only those qualified shall be screened and recruited to prevent the
detrimental effects which drug and alcohol use and abuse may cause in the workplace, the
conduct of mandatory drug test shall be required for pre-employment.

RealPage shall designate a duly accredited drug testing center by the Department of Health
(DOH) as its authorized drug testing laboratory.

RealPage may also conduct drug and alcohol testing under any of the following
circumstances:

a. Random Testing

Employees may be selected at random for drug testing at any interval determined by
RealPage.

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                             Internal Use

The company has the prerogative to determine the sample size for its random drug testing
yearly, unless there is a mandate coming from pertinent government offices on the sample
size.

b. For-Cause Testing

        i. RealPage may ask an employee to submit to a drug or alcohol test at any time it
feels that the employee may be under the influence of drugs or alcohol, including, but not
limited to, the following circumstances: evidence of drugs on or about the employee's
person or in the employee's vicinity, unusual conduct on the employee's part that suggests
impairment or influence of drugs or alcohol, negative performance patterns, or excessive
and unexplained absenteeism or tardiness.

       ii. All drug and alcohol tests shall employ, among others, two (2) testing methods, the
screening test which will determine the positive result as well as the type of the drug used
and the confirmatory test which will confirm a positive screening test. Where the
confirmatory test turns positive, the Assessment Team shall evaluate the results and
determine the level of care and administrative interventions that can be extended to the
concerned employee.

        iii. RealPage shall inform the employee who was subjected to a drug or alcohol test
of the test results, whether positive or negative.

      iv. A drug test shall be valid for one (1) year. All costs of drug and alcohol testing shall
be borne by RealPage.

2. Disciplinary Action

The employee shall not be terminated from employment based solely on having tested
positive for drug or alcohol use but shall be suspended from work at such number of days as
may be warranted. The employee found to have tested positive for drug is required to take
specified treatment and rehabilitation measures.

However, an employee may be terminated from employment if he refuses to give his consent
to the mandatory drug test, has rejected or failed to complete the required rehabilitation,
has tested positive for drug or alcohol use for the second time, or has been caught in
possession of, buying, selling, or distributing drugs in violation of this Policy.

3. Treatment, Rehabilitation, and Referral

        a. An employee who, for the first time, is found positive of drug use, may be referred
for treatment and/or rehabilitation in a DOH-accredited center.

                                   For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

       b. Following rehabilitation, the Assessment Team, in consultation with the head of
the rehabilitation center, shall evaluate the status of the drug-dependent employee and
recommend the resumption of the employee’s job if he poses no serious danger to his co-
employees and/or the workplace.

       c. All costs for the treatment and rehabilitation of the drug-dependent employee shall
be charged to his account. The period during which the employee is under treatment or
rehabilitation shall be considered as leave of absence.

VI. Guidelines

N.A.

Title: HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines

Document Control

Description: Deﬁnes attendance and punctuality requirements, absence notiﬁcation procedures,
attendance violations, disciplinary consequences, and related employee, supervisor, and HR
responsibilities for RealPage employees in the Philippines.

Document Type: Policy

Owner: Human Resources Business Partner Team

Audience: RealPage employees, trainees, supervisors/managers, and applicable HR teams in the
Philippines

Country: Philippines

System of Record: UKG People Articles

Version Number: 3.0

Last Review Date: July 26, 2024

E ective Date: September 1, 2024

Approval Date: [TO BE CONFIRMED]

Approver: Ivy Paraluman De Borja

Classiﬁcation: Internal Use

Document Status: Final

Next Review Date: [TO BE CONFIRMED]

Reason for Change: Version 3.0 created two major absence categories—Planned and
Unplanned—and deﬁned conditions for excused and unexcused unplanned absences; clariﬁed
employee responsibility for supporting documentation; reduced the tardiness/undertime grace
period; and revised NCNS disciplinary consequences.

Contents

   1. Purpose

   2. Scope

   3. Deﬁnitions

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

    4. Policy
       4.1 Responsible Parties
       4.2 Attendance Requirements
       4.3 Absence Notiﬁcation Procedure

    5. Consequences for Attendance Policy Violations

    6. Policy Administration and Progressive Disciplinary Action Process

    7. Impact to Compensation

    8. Related Policies

    9. Repealing Clause

    10. Document History

1. Purpose

Regular attendance and punctuality are essential for RealPage to provide excellent customer
service and meet deﬁned Service Level Speciﬁcations. Timely and regular attendance is an
expectation of performance for all RealPage employees.

To ensure adequate sta ing, positive employee morale, and to meet expected productivity
standards throughout the covered groups, employees will be held accountable for adhering to their
workplace schedule.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees at all job levels, including trainees of RealPage located in the
Philippines across all business units and departments e ective September 1, 2024.

3. Deﬁnitions

Employee – Refers to all types and levels of employees, including trainees and contractors if
directly employed by the Company.

Supervisor – Any employee who is responsible for supervising the performance of another
employee or trainee.

Present at Work – Means that the employee has logged in and is ready to perform duties, such as
but not limited to accepting calls, on or before the assigned/scheduled working hours at the
beginning of the employee's shift at the prescribed workplace.

For purposes of clarity, “workplace” can be in the o ice or in an approved remote location.

                Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Prescribed Workplace – The place where an employee is expected to work at a particular time, i.e.,
in the o ice assigned for Work-in-the-O ice Days, and at home or an approved alternative work
location when remote.

Absence – The state of being away from work.

a. Planned Absence

Occurs when an employee will not be available for work due to a pre-arranged commitment or
event properly approved by management. Planned absence may be paid or unpaid.

To be classiﬁed as Leave Without Pay (LWOP), a valid reason must be presented and approved by
the immediate Supervisor in advance.

b. Unplanned Absence

Occurs when an employee is not present at work without prior authorization. This type of absence
may be excused or unexcused.

Unexcused Absence – Occurs when an employee is absent from work without a valid reason and
permission from management.

An employee is absent and unexcused when the employee:

      Fails to report to work for the scheduled shift or working hours.

      Fails to notify properly. For the avoidance of doubt, proper notiﬁcation is deﬁned in this
       policy under “Absence Notiﬁcation Procedure.”

      Goes on unplanned absence despite having accrued paid time o (PTO) credits.

      Has no accrued leave credit and borrowed leave privileges.

      Fails to comply with all other requirements cited in related policies, including parental
       leave, maternity leave, and similar policies.

Excused Absence – Arises when an employee did not plan to be away from work but is absent for a
valid reason. Notiﬁcation process and documentation are required for an unplanned absence to be
sub-classiﬁed as excused. See Section 4 for applicable conditions.

Tardy – Occurs when an employee fails to report for work at the assigned/scheduled work time.

Undertime – Occurs when an employee leaves work prior to the end of the assigned working hours,
regardless of supervisor approval, and is treated in the same manner as tardiness.

Abandonment of Post – Occurs when an employee leaves at any point during the shift before the
end of the shift without approval from the immediate supervisor or an authorized representative of
the supervisor.

No Call No Show (NCNS) – A situation where an employee is absent without proper notice.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Absence Without O icial Leave (AWOL) – Occurs when an employee who has notiﬁed the
Company about the absence does not receive proper approval but still chooses to be away from
work.

Critical Workday – Workdays when attendance has been determined by management to be critical
to support the needs of the business.

Critical Workday Absences – Absences incurred during a Critical Workday.

4. Policy

4.1 Responsible Parties

Employee Responsibilities

Employees, including trainees as deﬁned above, are personally responsible for understanding
expectations and following rules around attendance, including but not limited to:

a. Notifying the supervisor when unable to come to work on time or unable to come to work, while
strictly following the call-in procedures articulated in this policy.

b. Articulating the reason or reasons for tardiness, absence, and other related requests.

c. Gathering and submitting supporting documents to support the reason for absence, tardiness,
and other related requests.

Supervisor Responsibilities

The Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that:

a. Their respective employees are aware of and follow this policy. A Supervisor is expected to
emphasize the Company's Attendance Policy to remind employees of the rules around absences
and tardiness.

b. This policy is implemented, including but not limited to sanctioning employees who violate the
policy following the appropriate procedure for issuing corrective actions and providing due process.

c. Employee notiﬁcations regarding tardiness and/or absence are appropriately addressed.

d. Absence and/or tardiness is reported to the appropriate parties, including but not limited to
Workforce Management, Operations Management Team, Payroll Team, and HRBP, as appropriate.

e. Maximum productive hours are maintained in the team by implementing consequence
management as detailed in this Policy.

HR Business Partner Responsibilities

The HR Business Partner ensures that they:

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

a. Support the Supervisor in situations requiring consequence management.

b. Function as a consultant to Supervisors and other parties in implementing this policy, in
conjunction with other relevant policies and statutory requirements.

c. Supports Supervisors in ensuring proper documentation of absences, tardiness, and all
processes articulated in this policy and related policies.

4.2 Attendance Requirements

Employees must schedule their time o in advance. However, recognizing that unforeseen
circumstances may arise, this policy outlines regulations regarding absences.

Planned Absences

Employees accrue Planned Time O (PTO) credits that they can use to take time o for vacations or
other personal business. Employees with accrued vacation leave credits are eligible for excused
absences by requesting approval for time o as outlined below.

Requested Number of Vacation Days —
                                                      Required Number of Days Prior to Approval
Business Days

                                                      At least one (1) week notice, except for
One (1) to six (6) days
                                                      emergency cases

Seven (7) to twenty-nine (29) days                    At least two (2) weeks prior notice

One (1) month or more                                 At least one (1) month prior notice

Similarly, government-mandated leaves, if processed prior to availment, are considered planned
and therefore authorized or excused.

Typical leaves availed of with advance notice include:

      Maternity Leave

      Paternity Leave

      Magna Carta for Women

      Solo Parent Leave

      Leave of Absence due to Medical Reasons

Each type of leave has requirements that employees must comply with.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Unplanned Absence

The burden of proof that the absence is valid lies with the employee.

Even in cases when an employee claims absence due to sickness, management reserves the right
to seek a formal explanation and full documentation from the employee in case of failure to notify,
when documentation is missing to justify the employee's absence within the timeframe prescribed
by this policy, and/or as reasonably demanded by the Company.

Furthermore, an employee who applies for both PTO and unpaid leave due to sickness agrees to be
examined by the Company physician, the HMO provider, a public health provider, or any other
medical professional at the sole discretion and satisfaction of the Company.

The employee waives all privacy to Personal and Sensitive Personal Information about such illness
and grants the Company authority to validate such illness or medical condition, including
requesting documents from the employee.

Although unplanned, some leaves may be considered excused if the absence is caused by events
authorized by the local government or a prevailing Company beneﬁt. In all cases, the employee
must meet the requirements for each type of leave below:

      Bereavement/Funeral Leave

      Leave for Victims of Violence Against Women and Their Children Act (VAW-C)

Similarly, an unscheduled absence due to sickness or emergency may be excused if the following
criteria are met:

      The employee must contact the immediate Supervisor and Workforce hotline a minimum of
       two (2) hours prior to the scheduled time of work.

      If an unplanned absence due to employee sickness occurs for two (2) consecutive days, the
       medical certiﬁcate requirement strictly applies.

      If an emergency situation prevents the employee from providing two-hour advance notice,
       the employee must submit applicable documentation, such as a certiﬁed police report,
       medical documentation, or other emergency documentation that justiﬁes the lack of
       advance notice, within ﬁve (5) business days of the absence.

Failure to provide required documentation may result in the Company treating the absence as
unexcused, depending on the requirement or documentation failure.

Tardiness and Undertime

Every day, the Company requires an employee to be on time at the beginning of the shift and after
every break, as well as to complete all required working hours for the day.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Understanding that unforeseen circumstances may arise, the Company gives an employee a total
of ten (10) minutes of grace period or two (2) instances of tardiness/undertime every month, where
the two incidents combined do not exceed ten (10) minutes.

When an employee has used all allowable time or instances of tardiness/undertime in a month, any
succeeding tardiness/undertime will be considered an infraction and will be subject to disciplinary
action depending on the number of instances outlined in the Attendance Policy consequences
stated in this policy.

Unexcused Absences While on Training

For trainee absences due to illness that are classiﬁed as either excused or unexcused, the trainee
will be subject to termination as speciﬁed in the voluntary training agreement.

However, subject to management discretion, a trainee may be recommended to complete the
current training course or be reassigned to a future training course, if one is available.

Critical Workday Absence

On Critical Workdays, workload volume is expected to be high.

Management reserves the right to reclassify a previously determined workday, whether critical or
non-critical. If a workday is reclassiﬁed, an announcement will be made one (1) day in advance.

Any unexcused absence incurred during a Critical Workday schedule shall be counted as two (2)
instances and sanctioned according to this policy.

No Call No Show (NCNS) and Absence Without O icial Leave (AWOL)

One (1) incident of NCNS or AWOL will not only be considered unexcused but shall also be counted
as three (3) instances, subject to the disciplinary sanction stated in the table of consequences for
Attendance Policy violations.

Progressive disciplinary action applies.

4.3 Absence Notiﬁcation Procedure

The Company expects employees to follow departmental notiﬁcation procedures if:

a. They will be late for work.
b. They need to leave work early.
c. They will not be at work.
d. They are requesting planned time away from work.

Employees must make the request in advance directly to their immediate superior and in
accordance with departmental procedure.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                             Internal Use

Employees should notify their immediate Supervisor or Manager at least two (2) hours before their
scheduled shift.

Notiﬁcation to a fellow employee is not su icient. The employee must make every attempt to talk
directly with the immediate superior concerning the reason for the absence.

When applying for planned time o , an employee must refer to available accrued leave credits.

All pertinent requirements for the particular type of leave for which the employee is seeking
approval must be complied with. This ensures appropriate implementation, including tracking of
leave utilization.

In case of a long leave due to medical reasons, management has the discretion to require or order
the employee to engage in a video call or conduct random house visits at the employee's place of
residence.

The employee is expected to communicate in advance the covered days of absence based on the
Medical Certiﬁcate issued to the employee.

The Medical Certiﬁcate must be sent to the employee's direct Supervisor/Manager via email or
other means of communication.

5. Consequences for Attendance Policy Violations

An employee who allegedly incurs unexcused absence, tardiness, or undertime will be served with
a Notice to Explain detailing the facts and circumstances of the violation related to this policy.

Instance                                                            Consequence

                                                                    Disciplinary Action: Written
1st Instance within a rolling 6-month period
                                                                    Warning

                                                                    Disciplinary Action: Second
2nd Instance within a rolling 6-month period
                                                                    Written Warning

3rd Instance within a rolling 6-month period or 1st instance of Disciplinary Action: Final
NCNS/AWOL                                                       Written Warning

4th Instance within a rolling 6-month period or 2nd incident of Disciplinary Action:
NCNS/AWOL within a 6-month period                               Termination

6. Policy Administration and Progressive Disciplinary Action Process

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                   For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

The RealPage Human Resources (HR) Department and line management of the employees
concerned are responsible for the administration of this policy.

The procedure below speciﬁes the steps each responsible party must take in implementing this
policy.

The immediate superior should monitor employee attendance on a regular basis and address
unsatisfactory attendance in a timely and consistent manner.

If the immediate superior notices a pattern of unscheduled absences, the immediate superior
should promptly discuss the concern with the employee.

The immediate superior is responsible for verifying and investigating employee absences before
disciplinary action is recommended.

a. All perceived violations must be formally reported to the immediate superior, who will review,
study, and validate the report.

b. In case of NCNS, a Return-to-Work Order (RTW) shall be sent to the employee's last known
address. Whether the employee returns or not, the employee will be subject to the due process
outlined in this policy. See the Return-to-Work Order Notice Template.

c. After establishing the validity of the report, and where the penalty is a Final Warning or
Termination, the immediate Supervisor, in coordination with the Human Resource Department
(HRD), shall issue a memo to the employee stating clearly the charges and requesting a written
explanation as to why disciplinary action should not be taken.

The memo shall be prepared in three (3) copies and distributed as follows:

      Original: Employee

      Duplicate: HRD / 201 File

      Triplicate: Immediate Superior ﬁle copy

d. The employee shall be given:

      Five (5) calendar days for o enses that may be punishable by termination or dismissal; or

      Three (3) calendar days for other o enses, from receipt of the memo to submit a written
       explanation.

e. If no written explanation is received after the applicable period has elapsed, this shall be
construed as a waiver on the part of the employee to be heard and present the employee's side. In
such instances, the Company will decide based on the facts on hand.

f. Upon the employee's submission of a written explanation, the immediate superior and HRD shall
conduct a thorough investigation and evaluation of the case.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

g. After the investigation and evidence have been gathered, the immediate superior shall
recommend the disciplinary action to be imposed on the employee, with the concurrence of HRD.

h. After a decision has been made, HRD shall prepare the Notice of Disciplinary Action, which shall
be subject to review and approval by the Philippine Legal Department. After approval, the Notice of
Disciplinary Action shall be immediately served on the employee.

Timely and regular attendance is a performance expectation of all RealPage employees.

Consequently, employees who have exhibited unsatisfactory attendance and have been subject to
disciplinary action, whether written or ﬁnal, during the course of the year may have the incident or
infraction documented in their annual performance evaluation.

7. Impact to Compensation

For clarity, the e ects of absence, tardiness, and undertime will be as follows:

      All unexcused absences, even when an employee has leave credits, shall be unpaid and will
       therefore be deducted from the employee's pay.

      All excused absences without PTO credits, or without pay as speciﬁed by local laws, shall
       be unpaid leave and will therefore be deducted from the employee's pay.

      For non-exempt employees, all time resulting from being late, including over breaks, early
       breaks, and unauthorized log-o s, will also be deducted from the employee's pay.

8. Related Policies

The Attendance Policy will be implemented alongside other relevant public and Company policies,
including but not limited to:

      Labor Code of the Philippines and its Implementing Rules and Regulations

      Employee Handbook

      Philippines Code of Conduct

      Zero Tolerance Policy

      Leave Policy

Business Unit/Group-Speciﬁc Policies and Processes

Groups such as Contact Center operations, including but not limited to RPCC, Insurance,
Screening, and others, may have supplemental policies and procedures that shall be implemented
to ensure sta ing for critical intervals, including but not limited to a Schedule Adherence Policy.

              Internal Use | HR – Attendance – Policy – Philippines | Version 3.0
                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                             Internal Use

9. Repealing Clause

This policy and the consequences for violating the Attendance Policy stated herein supersede the
rules in Version 2 of the Company's Code of Conduct.

hr_employee_code_of_conduct_policy_phili.text:
Internal Use

                                EMPLOYEE CODE OF CONDUCT

DOCUMENT METADATA:
  • Title: HR – Employee Code of Conduct – Policy – Philippines
  • Description: Employee Code of Conduct
  • Document Type: Policy
  • Owner: HR Employee Relations – Philippines
  • Audience: Employees of RealPage (Philippines), Inc.
  • Country: Philippines
  • System of Record: UKG People Articles
  • Version Number: V2
  • Last Review Date: 15 October 2024
  • Effective Date: 15 November 2024
  • Approval Date: 26 October 2024
  • Approver: Ivy De Borja, VP Employee Relations
  • Classification: Internal Use
  • Document Status: Final

1. SCOPE

      Their Policy establishes the rules and regulations of RealPage (Philippines), Inc. and shall
be known as the Company’s Employee Code of Conduct.

2. OBJECTIVE

        To lay down the policies, rules and regulations of the Company in order to ensure efficient,
effective and orderly operations within the organization.

3. DEFINITION OF TERMS

The following words and phrases as used in their Code shall have the meaning indicated herein.

       3.1 COMPANY – RealPage (Philippines), Inc.

       3.2 COMPANY PREMISES – means all lease holdings as well as vehicles rented by
       RealPage (Philippines), Inc., alternative work locations of employees and any other location
       where Company-related activities are conducted.

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

       3.3 DISCIPLINARY ACTION – appropriate and reasonable action taken to enforce the
       Company’s rules, regulations and prescribed standards, the purpose of such action will be
       to prevent any employee from:

               (a) unfairly taking advantage of their fellow workers,
               (b) failing to meet their obligation to the Company, or
               (c) impairing the efficiency of the Company

       3.4 DUE PROCESS – providing the employee with sufficient notice apprising them of the
       charges against them and affording the employee ample opportunity to be heard and
       defend themselves.

       3.5 EMPLOYEE – refers to all personnel of RealPage (Philippines), Inc.

4. COVERAGE

       The provisions of their Code shall apply to all employees of RealPage (Philippines), Inc.
regardless of rank or position in the table of organization and employment status.

5. GENERAL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES - INTERNAL ADMINISTRATIVE CASES ON
EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINARY MATTERS

5.1 POLICIES

1. All employees of RealPage (Philippines), Inc. (“Company”) must familiarize themselves and
comply with their Disciplinary Procedure.

Acknowledge Receipt: The HR Department Head (“HR Head”) and Department Heads or their
respective deputized representative will collaborate to ensure that all employees acknowledge
receipt of their procedure in any format deemed appropriate by the Company which must be
practical and efficient for safekeeping and retrieval. The HR Head or deputized HR representative
will be responsible for securely storing the acknowledgments of receipt for these procedures,
along with any amendments or modifications, for all employees in a central repository.

Leadership’s Role: The Country Manager, HR Head, Department Heads, and Senior Leaders
(Senior Managers and above) are responsible for ensuring compliance with their procedure and
promoting its observance.

Updates and Clarification: The Country Manager and HR Head, in consultation with the Legal
Head, may issue updates and guidelines (referred to as “Implementing Memoranda”) to clarify and
support their procedure. In addition, the Legal Head may, as the need arise, issue the appropriate
legal standards for the handling and disposition of internal cases on employee discipline and
termination and may conduct the pertinent information session in partnership with Human
Resources.

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

No Excuses: Unawareness of their Disciplinary Procedure and its Implementing Memos does not
excuse any employee from compliance.

2. The HR Head, in collaboration with Department Heads, or their respective deputized
representatives will conduct the administrative proceedings outlined in their Disciplinary
Procedure and implement appropriate disciplinary actions as defined in Chapter VI of the
Employee Code of Conduct. Any reported violations will be promptly investigated and addressed
by the HR Head or their appointed HR Business Partner and Department Heads or their appointed
Managers. The Committee on Disciplinary Investigation (“Committee”) for each specific case will
be promptly constituted and authorized by the HR Head or their appointed deputy from the
escalation of the Incident Report accompanied by sufficient evidence to the HR Department which
must ensure the equitable participation of all the relevant Departments or Teams from the
beginning to the conclusion of the investigation and disciplinary action process. All proceedings
will adhere to the timeframe and procedural steps outlined in the Internal Case Management
Manual of Human Resources.

3. For alleged offenses where the imposable penalty (or one of the imposable penalties) as charged
under the Notice to Explain (NTE) and the recommendation of Human Resources based on the
results of the investigation and pieces of evidence reviewed is Termination, the HR Head and the
Department Heads must confer with the Legal Head for the evaluation and approval of the
disposition of the case in the Notice of Decision (NOD). In addition, the Legal Head or their
deputized representative may be consulted in any part of the investigation, as well as participate
in the investigation including administrative hearing on a need basis. The Legal Head or their
representative may also audit observance of the substantive and procedural due process and/or
any documents related thereto to ensure consistent and quality implementation of due process.

4. In the rare instance that the opinion of the Legal Head on the proper disposition of a case is
different from the position of the Committee’s majority, the Legal Head will explain the basis of
their position and if after the explanation, the Committee is still convinced of its original position,
the majority with the concurrence of the HR Head will proceed. In rare cases when no agreement
is reached between and among the Committee members, Department, HR and Legal Heads may
be escalated to the Country Head who will then make the final decision on the case. All members
of the Committee will support the final outcome.

5. An employee who commits an alleged major offense may be placed under Preventive
Suspension without pay for a period not exceeding thirty (30) days pending result of the
investigation if the employee’s continued presence will pose a serious and imminent threat to the
life or property of the Company and/or the Company’s employees. The HRBP is responsible for
monitoring the proper implementation of the Preventive Suspension, including reverting the
suspended employee to the payroll after the 30th day limitation.

6. Any employee who has been charged and proven to have committed more than two (2) violations
of the same or different kind under the Employee Code of Conduct within a period of one (1) year
may, depending on the circumstances of the case and at the discretion of the Company, aggravate

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

the violation committed and impose the penalty next higher in severity for the third (3rd) and
succeeding violations.
7. For fair and reasonable circumstances, the Company, at its discretion, may mitigate the violation
and impose a penalty less in severity than that prescribed under the Employee Code of Conduct.

5.2 GUIDELINES FOR IMPLEMENTATION

To ensure that the Employee Code of Code is justly, fairly and orderly administered by the HR Head
and the Department Heads:

5.2.1 The HR Department shall be responsible for:

       1. Providing regular refresher courses for employees on the Employee Code of Conduct;
       and
       2. Conducting an annual review and if necessary, updating the Employee Code of Conduct
       to align with the Company’s requirements and the needs of all departments, teams, and
       business units.
       3. Ensuring compliance with the Disciplinary Procedure outlined in the Employee Code of
       Conduct, in accordance with the roles and responsibilities of leaders and team members
       across the organization.
       4. Accomplishing proper documentations - for offenses that warrant Final Written Warning
       and Termination, the HR Business Partner is responsible for writing the documentations
       such as Notice to Explain and Notice of Decision.
       5. Tracking of all disciplinary action records and safekeeping all documents related to the
       case.

5.2.2 The Department heads shall be responsible for:

       1. Enforcement of disciplinary actions imposed to employees under the Employee Code of
       Conduct; and
       2. Preparing and submitting the required reports, documentation, or recommendations to
       the HR Department on past and present cases involving Disciplinary Procedure in their
       respective Departments, Teams and Business Units.
       3. Ensuring compliance with the Disciplinary Procedure of the Employee Code of Conduct
       based on the function of the Department and the roles and responsibilities of its leaders
       and its team members.
       4. Accomplishing proper documentations - for offenses that warrant Level 1 and 2
       sanction, the manager/supervisor of the employee concerned shall write the
       documentations, such as the Notice to Explain and Notice of Decision in consultation with
       the HR Business Partner.

5.3 PROCESS

5.3.1 Report of Violations

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

All information pertaining to the violation of the Company’s Employee Code of Conduct where the
imposable penalty is Final Written Warning or Termination must be promptly reported to the HR
Department and to the Department Head who will jointly review, validate, and evaluate the merit
of the report. The leader who has personal knowledge of the facts and circumstances of the matter
will initiate their process through the submission of an Incident Report to the HR Department and
to the Department Head promptly, no later than 60 days from the date of the incident. The Incident
Report will state all relevant matters of facts and must enclose/attach the evidence that supports
each allegation in the report. Alternatively, the HR Department may also opt to investigate the
matter on its own initiative by requiring the pertinent leaders to submit the Incident Report.

5.3.2 Preliminary Evaluation
After establishing the preliminary facts and evidence that support the basis for the Incident Report,
the HR Department, in consultation with the Department Head or their delegated Leader, shall
determine based on a preliminary evaluation if the allegations and the initial evidence are sufficient
to support the issuance of a Notice to Explain.

       • If the allegations and the initial evidence are sufficient, a Notice to Explain (“NTE”) will be
       issued.
       • If they are not sufficient, the HR Department, in consultation with the Department Head
       or their delegated Leader will determine if the allegations and the initial evidence may be
       rectified or strengthened to support the issuance of an NTE or otherwise, the matter will be
       dismissed.
       • When issued, an NTE must clearly state the charge or charges against the employee in a
       manner and substance that would enable the employee to understand and defend
       themselves. against the allegations of facts against them, the law or regulation and the
       company policy, procedure, instruction, directive, or memo supposedly violated, and the
       imposable penalties for the alleged violation, if proven. The NTE must also specify the date,
       time and venue of the administrative hearing if such is deemed necessary by HR.

       The NTE will also direct the employee to submit a Written Explanation within the
       appropriate period stated in the notice why no disciplinary action should be taken against
       them. The NTE shall be prepared in three (3) copies and distributed as follows:

       Original : Employee
       1st Copy : Department Head (or their authorized deputies) *
       2nd Copy : HR Department / 201 File

       *Note: There may be instances when the Department Head and their authorized deputies
       may not be copy-furnished of the documentation of cases that demand the highest level of
       confidentiality due to the sensitivity of the information involved, such as but not limited to
       complaints falling under the Company’s Anti-Sexual Harassment Policy, Violence Against
       Women and Children and the likes.

5.3.3 Conduct of an Employee Pending an Investigation

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

Any behavior or conduct that obstructs, impedes, or impairs the business must immediately cease
while the disciplinary process is pending or in progress.

5.3.4 Written Explanation and Right to be Heard
For alleged offenses where the imposable penalty as charged under the NTE is Termination, the
employee shall be given five (5) calendar days from receipt of the NTE to submit their Written
Explanation. Except in cases where an Administrative Hearing of Conference is mandatory (e.g.,
the employee asked for an Administrative Hearing or Conference), the opportunity given to an
employee to submit a Written Explanation constitutes the employee’s right to be heard.

       • For alleged offenses where the imposable penalty as charged under the NTE is Final
       Written Warning without risk of termination, which must be explicitly stated in the NTE, the
       employee shall be given three (3) calendar days from receipt of the NTE to submit their
       Written Explanation.

       • For alleged offenses where the imposable penalty as charged under the NTE is Any Other
       Warning (without risk of termination), the employee shall be given one (1) working day from
       receipt of the NTE to submit their Written Explanation.

5.3.5 Waiver of the Written Explanation
If no Written Explanation is received after the lapse of the aforesaid period, the same shall be
construed as a waiver on the part of the employee to submit the Written Explanation and/or its
supporting evidence and that the Company may proceed to decide the matter based on the facts
and evidence gathered during the preliminary evaluation and the results of any subsequent
investigation or evidence duly received, without any Written Explanation on the employee’s part.

5.3.6 Administrative Hearing or Conference when mandatory
A formal Administrative Hearing or Conference is not mandatory in the Disciplinary Procedure
except when it is requested by the employee in writing, or when there is substantial dispute of
evidence that will justify a deeper probe of the matter. In such circumstances when Administrative
Hearing is conducted, the respondent has the right to attend with the help of their counsel,
however, the latter is not allowed to engage in a discussion with the facilitator of the Administrative
Hearing during the said conference.

5.3.7 Preventive Suspension
If the employee’s continued presence in the company poses a serious and imminent threat to the
life or property of the Company or of the Company’s employees, the HR Department may place the
employee under Preventive Suspension without pay for a period not exceeding thirty (30) days.
Should the HR Department in consultation with the employee’s Department Head and the Legal
Head decide to extend the Preventive Suspension beyond thirty (30) days, the employees must be
paid usual full compensation and other benefits during the period of the extended Preventive
Suspension. Also, employees who were fully exonerated after investigation will be paid back for
the days they were on Preventive Suspension. It must be highlighted that Preventive Suspension is

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

not a penalty, but a measure allowed by law in order to prevent such a serious and imminent threat
to the life or property of the Company or of the Company’s employees.

5.3.8 Case Evaluation when Legal Head’s participation is mandatory
Upon the employee’s submission of the Written Explanation, the HR Department and the
Department Head shall conduct a thorough evaluation of the case to ascertain the facts, to
determine the fair and just disposition of the case, and to ascertain the appropriate penalty, if any.
The Legal Head must be involved in the decision-making process if HR’s recommendation is to
dismiss the erring employee. For other cases, the Legal Head may be consulted particularly on
difficult questions of law, policy or evidence.

5.3.9 Deliberation and Preparation of the Notice of Decision
The HR Department shall consult with the Department Head to deliberate the outcome of the case.
The HR Business Partner (HRBP) or a deputized representative will draft the Notice of Decision for
disciplinary actions that warrant Final Written Warning or Dismissal as penalty, while the
Department Manager is responsible for writing Decisions for offenses with Level 1 to Level 2
sanction.

5.3.10 Review and Approval of the Notice of Decision
The HR Department shall prepare the Notice of Decision which shall be subject to the review and
approval of the Vice President for HR (or her deputized representative) and Philippine Legal
Department Head. The approved Notice of Decision shall be immediately served to the employee
by the HR Department.

5.3.11 Zero Tolerance, Red Flags, and Critical Error Cases
Employee acts and conducts which under their Code or in other company policies are categorized
as Zero Tolerance Cases, Red Flag Cases, or Critical Error Cases must be resolved promptly and
expeditiously if the facts gathered during the investigation process are sufficient to decide on the
case.

5.3.12 Signatures
All leaders and employees of the Company accept, ratify, and approve that in view of the modern
way of doing business and of facilitating workplace operations, and in light of their acceptability
under Philippine laws, rules, regulations, and jurisprudence, any electronic or digital signature
under any document, evidence, written matter, or proceedings in the context of their Code of
Conduct shall be equally valid and binding as an ink-written signature.

5.4 SANCTION AND SCHEDULE
Penalty: Level 1
Code: (L1)
Prescription Period: 3 months

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

Penalty: Level 2
Code: (L2)
Prescription Period: 6 months

Penalty: Final Written Warning
Code: (FWW)
Prescription Period: 12 months

Penalty: Dismissal
Code: (D)
Prescription Period: NA

6. OFFENSES AND PENALTIES

6.1 OFFENSES AGAINST COMPANY AND BUSINESS INTEREST

A. ATTENDANCE
Sec. 1.1: Committing an act of No Call No Show (NCNS). NCNS occurs when an employee
absents without proper notice.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 1.2: Absence despite disapproval of leave application by the Line Manager also known as
AWOL, unless (1) employee can prove that their absence was for a valid reason other than the
original reason for which the leave application was denied and (2) such valid reason could not
have been communicated to the office before incurring the absence.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 1.3: Unexcused absence/s, tardiness/ undertime within six (6) months rolling period.
Penalty: L1 (also referred to as “First Warning” in the Attendance Policy) to D

B. DISHONESTY AND BREACH OF TRUST AND CONFIDENCE
Sec. 2.1: Revelation of confidential matters, data, or other information relative to official
transactions.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 2.2: Revelation of confidential business information and/or trade secrets.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.3: Manipulation of funds, misappropriation, malversation, diversion of company funds
including company credit card or other commercial documents for personal benefits or

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

withholding of company funds or being an accomplice or accessory in said offenses.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.4: Committing any act of forgery, faking of documents, and/or fraud against the company
or its business. When a fraudulent transaction is committed using the employee’s device, the
fraud is presumed to be committed by the employee, and they bear the responsibility to present
evidence proving otherwise.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.5: Committing any act of dishonesty in any company transactions including but not limited
to coaching, administrative investigations and official functions.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.6: Committing any act of deceit such as but not limited to swindling, unpaid debts to
colleagues for an unreasonable period, and the other synonymous behaviors that may, among
others cause work disruption.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.7: Causing any fraud in timekeeping such as but not limited to tailgating.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 2.8: Removing any office file, document or without authority or with the intention of using the
same for pecuniary gain or to dispose of evidence relative to any subject under administrative
investigation or to cover up for any irregularity or offense committed by themselves or others.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.9: Unauthorized access, copying, alteration, removal, or destruction of any electronic
data, software, or program.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.10: Unauthorized copying, distribution of copyrighted, licensed, patented, software, video,
audio, photo, literary materials, etc.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.11: Access to prohibited sites during work or while using company devices such as but not
limited to porn, hacking, gaming, software downloads, proxy-avoidance/filter-bypass, and other
questionable or suspicious sites which may introduce risks to the company’s technical
infrastructure.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.12: Downloading, installation, or use of unauthorized software (software which is not
approved for business use, improperly licensed, improperly licensed software or software which
is infected with malware).
Penalty: FWW to D

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Sec. 2.13: Abuse of company resources including, but not limited to, transfer of excessive
amount of non-work-related data (e.g. streaming or download of movies or of large files, etc.),
accessing of nonwork related sites for extended period of time affecting the employee’s
productivity, or heavy use of internet resulting to slow response time for work-related access.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 2.14: Bypassing of existing security controls.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 2.15: Unauthorized modification or tampering of company information, including but not
limited to, logs, email, conversation history, report, etc.).
Penalty: D
Sec. 2.16: Unauthorized modification of company infrastructure (network, servers, computers,
voice/messaging systems, Security systems, etc.).
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.17: Leakage or loss of confidential information or asset (unauthorized copying, recording
or reproduction of sensitive or confidential information, loss or unauthorized access of device
used to store company information including but not limited to, emails, files, data, etc.). Device
may refer to every type of media such as but not limited to mobile phone, tablet, personal
computer (laptop or desktop) storage device (USB flash drive, mobile hard disk, memory cards
etc.), breach of online storage affecting sensitive or confidential information (cloud storage, web
e-mail, etc.), loss or unauthorized access to company device.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.18: Unauthorized use of privileged access (e.g. administrator/root/sa/dba/etc.) including
but not limited to, changing of computer settings without authority, giving access to unauthorized
individuals, unauthorized modification or deletion of information or data.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.19: Unauthorized use of another person’s login account. All persons involved shall be
liable.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.20: Any act that introduces risks or impacts operations including but not limited to,
spreading of malware, enables the entry of hackers into the network or gain access to company
information, or illegal or fraudulent activities or transactions.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.21: Willful non-observance of standard operating procedures in the handling of any official
transaction or work assignment.
Penalty: D

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

Sec. 2.22: Engaging in criminal conduct whether or not related to job performance or even if such
act happened outside of work hours. Their offense may be proved by substantial evidence in an
internal investigation and need not rely on a conviction in a court of law.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.23: Copying, storing and sharing personally identifiable information in a manner that
violates the Data Privacy Act of the Philippines.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.24: Unauthorized collection or receiving of gifts of substantial value, fees, charges, from
clients, suppliers, collectors, solicitors, or receiving the same in consideration of patronizing their
products or services or for services rendered, in connection with any Company transaction.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.25: Unauthorized collection or receiving any amount of kickbacks and/or commission
from clients or suppliers or receiving the same in consideration of patronizing their products or
services or for preferential treatment, in connection with any Company transaction.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.26: Unauthorized collection or fees and/or charges, from clients, suppliers, collectors,
solicitors, or receiving the same in representation of the company.
Penalty: D
Sec. 2.27: Misrepresentation as to qualifications, experience, certification/s, skills, and
ability/ies.
Penalty: D

Sec. 2.28: Giving false testimony, whether verbal or written, during Company-conducted
investigations.
Penalty: D

C. NEGLIGENCE OF DUTY, INEFFICIENCY, UNSATISFACTORY WORK PERFORMANCE,
INCOMPETENCE

Sec. 3.1: Unauthorized absence from workplace including loitering, and loafing, abuse of break
periods, etc.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 3.2: Failure to report violations of the Company’s Code of Conduct and relevant policies
promptly by any leader in charge of the enforcement of their Code of Conduct and/or the policy
concerned.
Penalty: L1 to FWW

Sec. 3.3: Insubordination or disobedience.
Penalty: FWW to D

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Sec. 3.4: Negligence or inefficiency including delayed completion of work assignments, failure to
meet deadlines, improper discharge of instructions, inaccurate reports, frequent errors, failure to
follow or observe standard operating procedures, mislabeling or misrouting documents and the
likes.
Penalty: L2 to D

Sec. 3.5: Failure of the employee who has been placed under Performance Improvement Plan
(PIP) to meet goals after a second opportunity is given to improve performance.
Penalty: D

Sec. 3.6: Gross negligence causing company damage or loss to the company.
Penalty: L2 to D

Sec. 3.7: Failure to follow written or oral instruction made by superior, as well as memoranda
and circulars or failure to perform assigned work due to simple negligence.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 3.8: Attending to personal matters during work hours.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 3.9: Malingering or feigning sickness.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 3.10: Sleeping on the job during working hours.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 3.11: Engaging in unlawful work stoppage, slowdowns or strikes.
Penalty: D

D. OFFENSES AGAINST BUSINESS INTEREST

Sec. 4.1: Theft or robbery of property of the Company or co-employees.
Penalty: D

Sec. 4.2: Improper conduct or behavior towards a customer or a client.
Penalty: FWW – D

Sec. 4.3: Demonstrating hostile, arrogant or rude behavior towards the customer/client
irrespective of the actual economic consequence to the business.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 4.4: Failure to adhere to any standard customer service level requirement/expectation
including but not limited to call avoidance irrespective of the actual economic consequence to

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

the business.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 4.5: Encouraging, coercing or inducing others to violate Company rules and regulations.
Penalty: FWW - D

E. OFFENSES AGAINST THE NAME AND REPUTATION OF THE COMPANY AND ITS
EMPLOYEES /PERSONS

Sec. 5.1: Making malicious, derogatory, or false statements regarding the good name of the
Company or its services using any means including but not limited to social media, internet
postings and comments, etc.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 5.2: Act of insult, spreading untrue and/or malicious gossip, calumny or otherwise damaging
the good name and reputation of any employee using any means, in the context of work, provided
that, if the acts are perceived to be in violation of the Safe Spaces Act and/or Anti-Sexual
Harassment then the company reserves the right to investigate and act of the perceived violation.
Penalty: FWW - D

6.2 OFFENSES AGAINST THE COMPANY’S EMPLOYEES AND OTHER PERSONS

Sec. 1: Quarrelling with a co-employee while at work, whether inside or outside company
premises and work hours in the context of work (heated exchange of fighting or violent words,
name calling, belligerent and aggressive conduct towards another employee).
Penalty: L2 - D

Sec. 2: Committing acts of threat, intimidation, coercion, harassment, and/or bullying upon
another employee, officer, including third-party service staff assigned to the company, guests,
etc.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 3: Committing acts of disrespectful, discourteous, insulting, upon another employee,
officer, including third-party service staff assigned to the company, guest/s, etc.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 4: Committing acts inflicting bodily harm upon another employee, officer, including third-
party service staff assigned to the company, guest/s, etc.
Penalty: D

Sec. 5: Committing acts of discrimination against a fellow employee, a company officer,
including third-party service staff assigned to the company, guest/s, etc.
Penalty: D

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Sec. 6: Engaging in any form of behavior or action that sexually harasses a fellow employee and
undermines their dignity, and/or any act that violates the Anti-Sexual Harassment Law of the
Philippines and/or the Safe Spaces Act of the Philippines.
Penalty: D

6.3 OFFENSES AGAINST COMPANY PROPERTIES

Sec. 1: Committing any act of sabotage on company property, equipment or facilities.
Penalty: D (Plus restitution of value of property/equipment thru salary deduction and/or from
whatever benefits due to the employee them/her)

Sec. 2: Unauthorized removal of company property from its designated location, or bringing out
from the company premises, without authority or prior approval.
Penalty: FWW to D

Sec. 3: Robbery or Theft (including attempt) of company property whether involving funds,
equipment, supplies, company valued data and/or non-public information, etc.
Penalty: D

Sec. 4: Excessive, inappropriate, or unauthorized use of Company time, materials, facilities, or
equipment, including telephones, e-mail, internet access, or instant messaging, etc.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 5: Unauthorized disclosure of trade secrets, or trade processes or any valuable information
acquired on the account of the employee’s position.
Penalty: D

Sec. 6: Causing damage to company property willfully, negligently or through improper use.
Penalty: L1 - D Plus restitution of value of damage or cost of repairs

6.4 OFFENSES AGAINST SECURITY AND ORDER

Sec. 1: Carrying of licensed firearm or other licensed weapons inside company premises
including company event/s whether inside or outside company premises, and/or insisting to enter
company premises and/or event while carrying such firearm and/or weapon.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 2: Carrying of unlicensed firearm or other unlicensed weapons inside company premises.
Penalty: D

Sec. 3: Final conviction of any employee charged with the commission of any criminal act
brought to court by any offended party.
Penalty: D

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

Sec. 4: Being charged with the commission of any illegal act in court which casts a serious doubt
on the credibility and fitness of the employee to perform their role effectively.
Penalty: D

Sec. 5: Any act that exhibits indecent or immoral conduct within Company premises or during
Company time or using Company property in the course thereof, including but not limited to the
exhibition or distribution of pornographic literature and/or materials.
Penalty: D

Sec. 6: Possession, distribution, sale, transfer, use, or working while under the influence of
alcohol (except in an authorized company event), or illegal drugs while at work regardless of
location.
Penalty: D

Sec. 7: Taking part in any game of chance including solicitation (except in an authorized company
event), gambling, and/or collection of bets inside the company.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 8: Causing public alarm and or scandal e.g. bomb scare, fire, earthquake jokes, or
synonymous events, or enabling a guest to do the same.
Penalty: FWW - D

Sec. 9: Smoking tobacco cigarette or e-cigarette, chewing tobacco or usage of any other tobacco
or nicotine products in restricted areas.
Penalty: L2 to D

Sec. 10: Failure to submit any and every medical document/s as directed, or report for scheduled
medical checkup/physical examination or procedure, or to comply and/or cooperate with the
Company Clinic in completing processes and programs (such as but not limited to Health
Improvement Plans) when instructed by the immediate supervisor and or Management.
Penalty: L1 to D

Sec. 11: Failure to observe the Company’s safety rules and regulations.
Penalty: L2 to D

Sec. 12: Unauthorized sale or promotion of products, services, or goods within the workplace
premises without proper authorization or permission.
Penalty: L1 to D

HR – Employee Termination and Clearance – Policy V3.0 – Philippines
Document Metadata:

   •   Title: HR – Employee Termination and Clearance – Policy V3.0– Philippines
   •   Description: Policy governing employee offboarding/separation/termination and
       employee exit clearance for RealPage Philippines
   •   Type: Policy
   •   Owner: HR Employee Relation – Philippines
   •   Audience: RealPage Philippines exiting employees and applicable stakeholders
   •   Country: Philippines
   •   System of Record: Approved SharePoint document library associated with the
       designated HR Team
   •   Version Number: 3.0
   •   Effective Date: June 1, 2026
   •   Approval Date: April 20, 2026
   •   Approver: Ivy Paraluman De Borja, VP – HR Employee Relations
   •   Last Review Date: March 20, 2026
   •   Next Review Date: March 20, 2027
   •   Document Status: Final
   •   Classification: Internal Use

1 Purpose
       RealPage Offboarding/Separation/Termination is the process where an employee is
deactivated and reported inactive in the system. Employee Exit Clearance is a process and
validation to ensure exiting employees have no outstanding obligations upon separation
from the company, including deprovisioning of electronic services on the last day of
employment. This policy aims to standardize the offboarding process across all types of
employment and separation to manage records of the exiting employee and minimize, if
not completely block, security threats through the return of all company-issued properties
and disablement of system access.

2 Scope
       The guidelines of this procedure cover all exiting employees of the entire RealPage
Philippines regardless of employment status (regular, probationary, contractual), job
grade, or nature of separation (voluntary or involuntary) and all stakeholders.

3 Definition of Terms
      Employee – Refers to the exiting employee who is in the process of terminating
      his/her employment with the district. Such termination/separation may be
      voluntary (resignation or retirement) or involuntary.
      Company – Refers to RealPage (Philippines), Inc
      Employment Status – Refers to the type of employment which includes, but not
      limited to, Probationary, Regular, and Project based employment.
      Nature of Separation – Refers to the Voluntary and Involuntary separation.
      Voluntary Separation – Refers to a type of termination initiated by the employee,
      wherein the employee submits a resignation through the Company’s designated HR
      system (currently People Assist), with an attached resignation letter.
      Involuntary Separation – Refers to a type of termination initiated by the employer.
      This includes separation due to just causes (such as policy violations, misconduct,
      or breach of company rules) or authorized causes under applicable labor laws,
      such as Redundancy or Retrenchment.
      Immediate Superior – Refers to the leader with direct supervisory authority over the
      employee, to whom the employee directly reports.
      HR Business Partner – Refers to the Human Resources Business Partner assigned
      to the employee’s Line of Business (LOB), responsible for providing HR guidance,
      support, and partnership to the employee and management.
      HR Talent Services Associate – Refers to the employee assigned to provide
      centralized administrative and operational support for HR-related processes,
      transactions, and employee services.
      Desktop Support – Refers to the employee under IT department, responsible for
      ensuring that all company-issued assets returned by the employee are thoroughly
      checked and validated to confirm completeness and acceptable condition in
      accordance with Company standards.
      Payroll – Refers to the employee under Payroll team responsible checking and
      validating approved deductions for any uncleared accountabilities based on
      validated and endorsed offboarding results and processes the employee’s final pay
      computation in accordance with Company policy and applicable regulations.
      Finance – Refers to the employee under Finance department responsible checking
      and validating approved deductions for any uncleared accountabilities based on
      validated and endorsed offboarding results, and requests and ensures the
      disbursement of the employee’s final pay.

       People Assist – Refers to the Company’s designated HR system used to facilitate
       employee lifecycle transactions, including the filing and processing of resignations,
       initiation of offboarding and clearance activities, documentation tracking, and
       coordination of approvals among relevant stakeholders.
       Document Manager – Refers to the Company’s designated system or repository
       used to securely store, manage, track, and retrieve employee-related documents,
       including but not limited to resignation letters, clearance records, final pay
       documents, and other HR-related files.
       Company Properties – Refer to all company-issued assets that were assigned to or
       in the possession of the employee during the course of employment. These typically
       include, but are not limited to, IT equipment (e.g., laptop, headset, computer or
       laptop accessories, docking station), company ID or badge, pedestal and keys, and
       HMO cards.
       Certificate of Clearance (COC) – A formal document issued by the Company to a
       separated employee confirming that all clearance requirements have been fully
       completed, including the return of Company-issued assets, settlement of
       accountabilities, and fulfillment of all employment obligations.

4 Policy
       4.1 Employee Separation
       4.1.1 Voluntary
       All resigning employees are governed by the Labor Code of the Philippines and the
       applicable rules and regulations enforced by the Department of Labor and
       Employment (DOLE). An employee who intends to resign without just cause is
       required to submit a written notice of resignation to the employer at least thirty (30)
       calendar days or one (1) month in advance, unless a shorter period is approved by
       the Company. Eligibility for re-employment of former employees shall be solely at
       the discretion of the Company, subject to applicable policies and business
       requirements. A resigning employee must remain active in the system to receive
       their final payout.
       A resignation shall be deemed effective upon the occurrence of either of the
       following, whichever comes first:

   •   Completion of the required thirty (30)-day notice period; or
   •   An earlier effective date expressly approved or waived by the Company.

    4.1.2 Immediate Resignation
          Requests for immediate resignation may be subject to Company review. The
    Company may require the submission of reasonable supporting documentation,
    when applicable, to validate the basis cited.
    In accordance with the Labor Code and DOLE regulations, an employee may resign
    without serving the thirty (30)-day notice period under justifiable circumstances,
    including but not limited to the following:

•   When the employee’s honor and dignity have been gravely insulted by the employer
    or the employer’s duly authorized representative;
•   When the employee is subjected to inhuman, harsh, or abusive treatment by the
    employer or the employer’s representative;
•   When the employer has committed a crime or offense against the employee or any
    of the employee’s immediate family members; and
•   Other analogous causes of a similar nature that render continued employment
    unreasonable or untenable.

    4.1.3 Withdrawal of Resignation
    Any request to withdraw or retract a submitted resignation shall be subject to
    Company review. The Company reserves the discretion to approve or deny such
    request based on business requirements and operational considerations.

    4.2.1 Involuntary
    An employee who fails to comply with Company policies, procedures, and
    processes shall be subject to appropriate disciplinary action, in accordance with
    the Company’s Code of Conduct, applicable Company policies, and the
    requirements of procedural due process under Philippine labor laws.
    The Company may terminate an employee without payment of separation pay for
    just causes, as provided under Article 297 of the Labor Code of the Philippines
    (formerly Article 282), after observance of the required due process.

    4.3 Employee Clearance Process
    The employee is required to complete the clearance process on their last working
    day or prior to the start of any approved leave taken during the final days of
    employment. The Company shall release the employee’s final pay within thirty (30)

       days from the date the clearance process has been successfully completed,
       subject to compliance with all clearance requirements.
       In the event that the employee fails to comply with the clearance requirements,
       including the return of Company-issued assets or tools of trade that are damaged,
       incomplete, or unreturned, the Company reserves the right to deduct the cost of
       such damage, loss, or non-return, as provided in the employee’s Employment
       Agreement and other pertinent company policies.

       4.4 Employee Accountability
       Upon separation from the Company, the employee is responsible for ensuring that
       all accountabilities are fully cleared to avoid any deductions from their final pay.

       4.4.1 Clearance of Accountabilities
   •   Company Assets / Properties
   •   Government Loans and Reimbursements – The Company shall deduct any
       outstanding balances from the employee’s final pay in compliance with the
       requirements of the Social Security System (SSS) including but not limited to:
           o SSS loans
           o Maternity and Sickness reimbursements
   •   HMO usage, including voluntary dependents
   •   Company funds
       Any unsettled accountabilities and/or unreturned assets shall be subject to further
       evaluation and re-computation of the employee’s final pay. This may result in an
       extension of the final pay release timeline.

5 Policy Administration
       5.1 Employee
       Initiates separation from the Company by formally submitting a resignation through
       the Company’s designated HR system (currently People Assist).
       5.1.1
       Ensures that all attendance-related matters are properly addressed prior to the last
       working day or before the start of any approved leave taken during the final days of
       employment. This includes completing and filing the required attendance records
       and securing approval from the Immediate Superior, or coordinating directly with
       the Immediate Superior to resolve any pending attendance-related concerns.

5.1.2
Ensures that all company-issued assets and accountabilities are cleared on or
before the employee’s last working day, or earlier in cases where leave or time off is
availed prior to separation. * Once all company-issued assets and accountabilities
have been surrendered by the employee, the REWS Department will forward the
Employee Asset Forms to the Talent Services Team.
5.2 Immediate Superior
Reviews the resignation submitted through People Assist and secures leadership
alignment and approval in line with Company guidelines prior to the effective date
of separation.
5.2.1
Ensures that all attendance-related matters of their subordinates are properly
addressed prior to the employee’s last working day or before the start of any
approved leave taken during the final days of employment, including the completion
of required attendance filings and/or coordination with the employee to resolve any
pending concerns.

5.2.2
Validates completion of all turnover and transition deliverables and that the
offboarding form is updated accordingly within seven (7) calendar days.
5.2.3
Also, ensure that all required attrition details are accurately and completely
provided prior to approving the Employee Resignation/Involuntary Separation ticket
in People Assist to avoid delays. Required information includes the Last Working
Day (LWD), termination date, termination reason and type, regrettable or non-
regrettable classification, and rehire eligibility.
To support compliance with termination timelines, managers are expected to
approve resignation tickets within two (2) business days. This ensures timely
submission to Talent Services and prevents delays in termination processing in
UKG.

5.3 Talent Services Associate
Lodges termination in UKG – Voluntary & Involuntary

5.3.1
Closes the Employee Resignation/Involuntary Separation form in People Assist after
lodging the termination in UKG.
5.3.2
Initiates offboarding via People Assist.
5.3.3
Sends offboarding instructions to the separating employee via People Assist;
*Notifications to exit stakeholders will be triggered on the effective date of
termination of the employee.
5.3.4
Notifies the Payroll team to initiate the employee’s final pay computation.
5.3.5
Sends final pay status update notifications to separated employees;
5.3.6
Sends a demand letter to the REWS Team for appropriate action if the separated
employee fails to return all company-issued assets.

5.4 Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP)
Reviews and approves the termination filed by the Talent Services in UKG.
5.4.1
For involuntary separation – Serves termination notice.
5.4.1.1
Initiates Separation in People Assist
5.4.1.2
Reviews and approves the termination filed by the Shared Services Associate in
UKG.

5.5 Desktop Support
Ensures that all Company-issued assets returned by the employee are thoroughly
checked and validated for completeness and acceptable condition in accordance
with Company standards, and that the offboarding form is updated accordingly
within seven (7) calendar days, reckoned from whichever comes first: (a) the date
the employee returns all Company-issued assets, or (b) the effective date of
separation.
5.5.1
Indicates the appropriate amount in the offboarding form submitted through People
Assist for any damaged or unreturned assets to support accurate clearance
validation and final pay deductions.

5.6 Finance Department
Validates uncleared accountabilities;
5.6.1
Computes the applicable deductions from the employee’s final pay in accordance
with Company policies and applicable regulations, and updates the offboarding
form within seven (7) calendar days, reckoned from whichever comes first: (a) the
date the employee returns all Company-issued assets, or (b) the effective date of
separation.
5.6.2
Requests the disbursement of the employee’s final pay upon endorsement by
Payroll and after the separated employee has duly signed either a Quitclaim and
Release or, in cases where the employee declines to sign a quitclaim, an
Acknowledgment of Receipt of Final Pay.

5.7 Payroll
Processes the employee’s final pay and applies approved deductions for any
uncleared accountabilities based on validated and endorsed offboarding results
within seven (7) calendar days, reckoned from whichever comes first: (a) the date
the employee returns all Company-issued assets, or (b) the effective date of
separation.
5.7.1
Sends the final pay computation and quitclaim to the separated employee for
completion;

5.7.2
Endorses to Finance for final pay release after the quitclaim has been duly signed by
the separated employee; Retain records for compliance and reference;
5.7.3
Releases the Certificate of Completion (COC) and BIR Form 2316 once the final pay
has been credited to the separated employee’s bank account.

The RealPage Human Resources (HR) Department is responsible for the
administration of this policy, including ensuring compliance to release the final pay
in 30 days and initiating appropriate disciplinary action for non-compliance.
