                  REALPAGE PHILIPPINES – FLEXIBLE WORK – POLICY

DOCUMENT METADATA

Document Title: RealPage Philippines – Flexible Work – Policy
Source Title: RealPage Philippines Flexible Work Policy
Document Type: Policy
Description: Philippines-specific supplement to the RealPage Global Flexible Work Policy
defining requirements and parameters for hybrid work, fully remote work, in-office
exceptions, and related employee responsibilities.
Owner: Human Resources
Audience: All employees of RealPage (Philippines), Inc.
Country/Jurisdiction: Philippines
Legal Entity: RealPage (Philippines), Inc.
System of Record: UKG People Articles / designated HRIS policy repository
Version Number: 1.1
Classification: Internal Use
Document Status: Final
Effective Date: August 4, 2025
Last Review Date: July 1, 2025
Approval Date: July 1, 2025
Approver: Peter Paul Ramolete
Next Review Date: August 4, 2027
Reason for Change: Corrected Annex C: List of Provinces, Cities and Municipalities “Far”
from RealPage Offices.
Version 1.1 Change Date: 08/04/2025

I.     Policy Statement

This RealPage Philippines Flexible Work Policy is a supplement to the RealPage Global
Flexible Work Policy to ensure that RealPage (Philippines), Inc. (“Company”) defines and
sets out the local parameters to implement in the Philippines the global hybrid and remote
working policy discretion.

II.    Application

This Policy applies to all employees of RealPage (Philippines), Inc. without regard to
position, tenure, and status of employment.

III.   Hybrid and Remote Work

          1. An employee who works at home or at an alternative location, whether as
          part of (a) hybrid working or (b) as a fully remote employee, has the following
          responsibilities:

                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                 Internal Use

   a.      The employee must work in a safe and secure location, generally
   his/her residence, that will not expose his/her person or the company
   property and information to any harm or danger.
   b.      The employee must ensure that the chosen location for remote work
   is equipped with appropriate, stable, usable, and secure internet
   connection. The employee must comply with the appropriate internet speed
   (i.e., mbps) required by their respective business units or functions and with
   reliable back-up provisions for power, internet connection, and other
   systems and equipment enablement.
   c.      It is the employee’s responsibility to ensure that their home or
   alternative work location is conducive to productive work. This includes
   maintaining a quiet environment free from disruptive background noise such
   as but not limited to machineries, vehicles, animals, or other sources that
   may interfere with virtual meetings, calls, or focused work. The company
   reserves the right to reassess the remote work arrangement if the work
   environment is found to be consistently disruptive or unsuitable for
   professional duties.
   d.      It remains the duty of the employee while in a remote working location
   to continuously comply with, and to be bound by, all the Company policies,
   procedures, rules, and regulations such as those pertaining to information
   security, data privacy, confidentiality, and other matters pertaining to the
   performance and delivery of work.
   e.      The employee must immediately inform, at the earliest opportunity,
   his/her immediate supervisor regarding any unstable or loss of internet
   connection or any event that diminishes or interrupts his/her capability to
   perform or deliver any work or to communicate with any leaders or co-
   employees, clients or customers; and thereafter, should such situation
   persist, for the employee to immediately report in the office or a suitable
   alternative location in a manner that will prevent any further work
   interruption or disturbance. Unproductive hours/days may be compensated
   only when appropriate paid time off were used, following the process of
   request and approval for utilizing accrued PTO credits (see RealPage
   Philippines Paid Time Off Policy). The failure by the employee to make this
   immediate notification or to do the immediate work onsite as a mode to
   recover from the unproductive time or work disruption shall be deemed as
   deviation from standard operating procedure which are subject to proper
   investigation and due process.
   f.      All costs arising from or connected to remote working shall be the
   responsibility of the employee.

2. Any opportunity given by the Company to render Hybrid or Remote Work in
this or in other policies is a privilege that the Company may alter or completely

                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                             Internal Use

          revoke, and it is not a right. As such, the employee must responsibly exercise
          the privilege by ensuring that his/her Remote Work situation or environment is
          fully compatible with the requirements of the business.
          An employee who, while in a remote work, fails to maintain the desired working
          environment to support the business (e.g., does not have a reliable internet
          service/connection or power, noise that is disruptive in the conduct of work, or
          does not have a quiet professional environment, etc.) must immediately report
          for work in the office or alternative suitable location for the rest of his/her shift
          and in his/her subsequent scheduled shifts until he/she could sufficiently prove
          that he/she has restored his/her remote working condition in a manner that is
          deemed suitable to support the business.

          3. Employees who cannot be in the office or suitable alternative location within
          two (2) hours from the work interruption shall be marked as absent, unless the
          leader and the HR Department has determined that half-day work credit is
          justified. The employee who was marked as absent must show proof that the
          work interruption was beyond his/her control and/or not anticipated; otherwise,
          he/she will also be liable for unauthorized absence.

          4. Subject to validation process as indicated in Annex A of this policy,
          employees whose address are far from RealPage offices prior to June 10, 2025
          on UKG. For the avoidance of doubt, “far” refers to cities or municipalities that
          are:
                        i.  Outside Greater Metro Manila or at the outskirts Greater Metro
Manila. (See Annex C for the list.)
                        ii. Outside of Metro Cebu or at the outskirts Greater Metro Cebu.
(See Annex C for the list.)

Employees applying for remote work will be assessed based on business needs and role
requirements, such as the level of collaboration, need for onsite supervision, and
performance or productivity standards. The employee’s declared address and signed
Commitment Form will also undergo strict validation (see Annex A for details). All criteria
must be met for approval, and management’s decision is final.
While relocating is a right of an employee, doing so does not grant eligibility for full remote
work.

          5. All other employees who do not qualify for Fully Remote Work as stated in
          III.4 above shall render Hybrid Work unless this policy and/or any other official
          instructions provide otherwise.

          6. All hybrid employees are encouraged to reside within a reasonable
          commuting distance of their assigned RealPage office location. This is to help
          ensure that their time and energy are focused on meaningful work, rather than

                                   For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                 Internal Use

being depleted by long or strenuous commutes. To this end, candidates
considered for roles in any of the offices of the company shall be asked to
declare their addresses as part of the application process.

7. All Hybrid Work setup envisioned above is limited by the following
parameters:

   a.      Employees may be asked to report in their respective assigned office
   locations for two (2) to eight (8) days within a month depending on the need
   of their respective departments, groups, team, business units or functions or
   their company roles and positions. The frequency and/or specific days of
   Remote Work shall be decided by the HR Head and the Managing Director in
   consultation with the respective heads of the concerned departments,
   groups, team, business units or functions. The frequency of “two (2) to eight
   (8) days” within a month to do in-office work is an indicative period or
   frequency based on current business needs, and that the Company hereby
   reserves the right to modify the same or to add more days.
   b.      A newly-hired employee shall, during the Probationary Period of their
   employment and unless otherwise specified by leaders’ instructions or on
   the employment contract, be on Hybrid Work setup with preference for more
   work-in-office days, considering the need of the employee to undergo
   training, to familiarize themselves with the workplace, the business and
   integration with their teams, as well as to provide an environment for proper
   assessment and evaluation in line with the purposes of probationary
   employment.

8. To give employees flexibility where absolutely needed, the Company offers
up to six (6) In-Office Exception days per calendar year. The employee must
apply for remote work a week prior to the date of intended use, except where the
employee can provide justifiable and/or emergency circumstances which may
warrant its immediate application; provided, that the manager has the
prerogative to approve or reject such request based on the merit of each
application, taking into consideration business exigencies and the need to
satisfy business requirements relative to cause submitted for immediate use of
In-Office Exception Credits. See the process for application and approval of
InOffice Exception credits in Annex B.

9. Employees are entitled to one complimentary meal on their designated
inoffice days. This meal is provided at the company’s discretion and is not
considered a contractual right or employee benefit. The company reserves the
right to modify or discontinue this offering at any time without prior notice.

                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

          10. The Company reserves the right to order an employee to report FULLY IN THE
          OFFICE on scheduled working days, for a reasonable period of time, based on,
          but not limited to, the following reasons: training, official events, employee
          monitoring, performance improvement, other official needs, or when serious
          considerations make it appear that in-office days may be more productive and
          beneficial to the employee and/or the company. For example:

              a.      If an employee is eligible for and signs up for a training program that is
              only available in-person on-site, the employee shall be required to come to
              the office to avail of such training. This shall be the same arrangement for an
              employee on full remote work arrangement.

              b.      If an employee is identified as needing additional in-person
              supervision, coaching, or support to address performance challenges and
              meet individual or team objectives, they may be required to report to the
              office on days beyond their regular in-office schedule.

          11. The company reserves the right to a shift in scheduling and/or setup
          paradigm relative to office and/or remote work of employees as part of
          Company’s prerogatives under law and regulation. This policy does not in any
          way create, conceptualize, nor accrue in favor of any employee a right to
          entitlement, demand, claim, or invocation to any working setup, including
          remote work, hybrid work, office work, or any other working arrangement or
          setup.

An employee may only avail of the Remote Work Setup within this policy with Remote Work
done in the Philippines. Except for company-arranged business travels, when an employee
intends to travel abroad, he/she must use leave credits, and should not render remote
work. Reasonable incidental work during personal travels may be allowed.

IV.    Repeal of Previous Policies

Any other Company policy, procedure, rule, or practice which is inconsistent with this
policy is hereby repealed and superseded by this policy.

V. DOCUMENT HISTORY

ANNEX A: Full Remote Work Arrangement: Process Flow

Step 1: System-Based Eligibility Identification
HR reviews employee records to identify those whose current address in the company’s
system is in a place that requires air or sea travel to reach the office prior to the effectivity
date of this policy.

Step 2: BU/Function Head Recommendation and Immediate Manager Validation
       2.1. Employee’s BU or Function Head provides a written recommendation.
Recommendation must confirm:
                      •   Suitability of the role for remote work
                      •   Employee’s reliability and independence
                      •   Employee’s performance level is “Meeting Expectations”

2.2. Employee’s immediate manager provides validation that the address declared by
the employee is true and correct.

Step 3: Notify employees who are eligible and recommended by their BU for remote work
arrangement.

Eligible employees are notified that they are eligible to apply for full remote work, as well as
the instructions and requirements for application.

Step 4: Employee Expression of Interest
Eligible employee submits a request to apply for full remote work via the designated HR
platform.

Employee submits two (2) valid proofs of address with the employee’s legal name in it,
such as:
                      •   a recent proof of billing
                      •   valid government ID
                      •   barangay certificate
                      •   leasing/rental agreement

The employee is also required to submit a notarized Commitment Form upon application
for remote work.

The company reserves the right to seek for other equivalent and/or supporting documents.

Step 5: Immediate Manager Validation
Employee’s immediate manager provides validation that the address declared by the
employee is true and correct.

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

Step 6: Documentation Verification
The HRBP of the employee validates the documents submitted. They validate the
consistency of the address on official company records and that indicated in the proof of
address and notarized commitment form, and checks the authenticity of the documents
received.

Any invalid documents and/or inconsistency may result to rejection of the application.

The system sends an update to the employee on the status of the application. It informs
the employee if it is in progress for final approval or denied as evidence provided do not
meet requirements.

Step 7: Final Review and Decision
HR Head and Senior Managing Director jointly review:
               •     Eligibility criteria
               •     Documentation
               •     Performance rating
               •     BU/Function Head recommendation
If approved → HR issues a Full Remote Work Agreement
If declined → HR communicates the reason to the employee

Step 8: Agreement and Onboarding
Employee is informed by HR regarding the result of the application for remote work and
copies in the immediate manager of the employee in the said notice.
HR updates the employee’s work arrangement in the system
IT and Facilities teams are notified for any support needs

                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

ANNEX B: In-Office Exception Process Flow

Step 1: Allotment of In-Office Exception Days
         •     Each employee is allotted 6 In-Office Exception (IOE) days per calendar year,
         distributed pro-rata based on their date of joining.
         •     Unconsumed WIO credit does not carry-over the following year. All
         employees reset to the total days offered per year on January 01 yearly.
         •     These days are front-loaded and made available in the system.

Step 2: Employee Submits IOE Request
         •     Employee logs into the system and applies for the In-Office Exception prior
         to the intended date of use.
         •     Employee specifies the date(s) and reason for the request.

Step 3: Manager Review and Approval
        •    The employee’s manager receives a notification of the request.
        •    Manager reviews the request and approves or declines it via the system.

Step 4: Confirmation and Logging
        •     Once approved, the IOE day is deducted from the employee’s available
         balance.
        •     The employee receives a confirmation notification.

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

hr_return_to_work_order_procedure_philip.text:
Internal Use

               HR – Return to Work Order – Procedure V3.0 – Philippines

Document Metadata:
  • Document Type: Procedure
  • Owner: HR Employee Relations – Philippines
  • Audience: HR Business Partners, People Leaders (Philippines)
  • Country: Philippines
  • System of Record: SharePoint – HR Philippines Document Library
  • Version Number: 3.0
  • Effective Date: July 1, 2026
  • Approval Date: June 2, 2026
  • Approver: Ivy De Borja, VP - HR Employee Relations
  • Last Review Date: April 24, 2026
  • Next Review Date: April 24, 2027
  • Document Status: Final
  • Classification: Internal Use

1. Purpose
This document defines the standard process for issuing Return to Work Orders (RTWO) and
managing No Call No Show (NCNS) cases in compliance with company policy and
Philippine labor requirements.

2. Scope
This procedure applies to all employees of RealPage Philippines and covers the end-to-end
process for handling NCNS incidents, including issuance of RTWO, Notice to Explain (NTE),
and Notice of Decision (NOD).

3. Roles and Responsibilities
    HR Business Partner (HRBP)
       • Drafts and issues RTWO, NTE, and NOD
       • Ensures documentation is complete and stored in the system of record
    VP HR Employee Relations / HR Head
       • Reviews and approves Notice of Decision
           Approves termination decisions where applicable
    Immediate Supervisor / Manager
       • Reports NCNS incidents promptly to HR
       • Confirms employee return to work status

4. Definitions
    • No Call No Show (NCNS): Absence without proper notice as defined in the
       Attendance Policy
    • Return to Work Order (RTWO): Formal directive requiring employee to report back
       to work

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

   •   Notice to Explain (NTE): Document requesting employee explanation for alleged
       violation
   •   Notice of Decision (NOD): Final decision following due process
   •   Termination Letter: Formal notice of employment termination

5. Process Overview (Day 1–Day 41)
    Day 1 – NCNS Occurrence and Reporting
       • Immediate Supervisor identifies No Call No Show (NCNS)
       • Immediate Supervisor reports NCNS to HRBP via prescribed form or email on
           the same day
    Day 2 – Initial Action / First RTWO Decision Point
       • If employee reports to work:
           o Serve Notice to Explain (NTE) for 1 day NCNS
       • If employee remains absent:
           o HRBP drafts Return to Work Order (RTWO) with NTE (1st issuance)
           o Send RTWO via all required channels:
                    ➢ Docusign (personal email)
                    ➢ Work email and personal email
                    ➢ Courier
                    ➢ Registered mail to last known address
           o Upload RTWO and NTE to system of record
    Day 3–4 – Minimum Delivery Window (Courier)
       • Employee is expected to receive RTWO via courier
    Day 4 – Expected Return
       • Employee is expected to report to Immediate Supervisor
       • Supervisor must notify HRBP if employee returns
    Day 4–8 – Monitoring Period
       • HRBP monitors employee status (returned vs still NCNS)
       • Supervisor provides updates to HRBP
    Day 8 – Maximum Delivery Window (Courier)
       • Lapse of 5 calendar days from 1st attempt to deliver
    Day 9 – Employee Response Deadline
       • Employee expected to respond to NTE

   Scenario 1: Employee Remains on No Call No Show Status Despite Notice
   Day 9: Final RTWO (Escalation)
          o HRBP drafts 2nd RTWO with NTE (2nd Issuance)
          o Issue via:
                 ➢ Docusign
                 ➢ Email (work and personal)
                 ➢ Courier
                 ➢ Registered mail

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                     Internal Use

Day 10–11 – Delivery Window (Courier)
   • Employee is expected to receive RTWO via courier
Day 11 – Expected Return
   • Employee is expected to report to Immediate Supervisor
   • Supervisor must notify HRBP if employee returns
Day 11–15 – Final Monitoring Period
   • HRBP monitors employee status (returned vs still NCNS)
   • Supervisor provides updates to HRBP
Day 15 – Maximum Delivery Window (Courier)
   • Lapse of 5 calendar days from 1st attempt to deliver
Day 16 – Employee Response Deadline
   • Employee expected to respond to NTE
Day 17–18 – Decision Path and Final Decision Drafting
   • HRBP and Deliberation Committee:
      o Review all documentation (RTWO, NTEs, responses, attendance records)
      o Ensure due process compliance
      o Draft Final Notice of Decision
Day 19–20 – Final Approval
   • VP, HR Employee Relations reviews and approves Final Notice of Decision
Day 21 – Final Notice of Decision Issuance
   • Serve Final NOD (including termination if applicable):
      ➢ Docusign
      ➢ Email (work and personal)
      ➢ Courier
      ➢ Registered mail
   • Upload all final documents to system of record
   • Close case with complete documentation
                          --END PROCESS FOR SCENARIO I--

Scenario 2: Employee Responded to the Company’s Notice
Day 9 – Initial Hearing
       o HRBP schedules and conducts hearing
Day 10–11 – Decision Drafting
   • HRBP drafts NOD based on:
       o Employee explanation, and
       o Administrative Hearing (if attended by the employee)
       o Alignment with Immediate Supervisor / Manager with decision
Day 12 – First Notice of Decision Issuance
   • Serve NOD:
       o In person if employee returned
       o Otherwise via Docusign, email, courier, and registered mail
Day 13–17 – Delivery and Return Expectation
   • Employee expected to receive documents via courier

                           For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                         Internal Use

      •  Employee expected to report to Immediate Supervisor
      •  Supervisor confirms whether employee has returned
   Day 18 – Maximum Delivery Window (Courier)
      • Lapse of 5 calendar days from 1st attempt to deliver
   Day 19 – Final RTWO (Escalation)
      • HRBP drafts 2nd RTWO with NTE (2nd Issuance)
         o Issue via:
                  ➢ Docusign
                  ➢ Email (work and personal)
                  ➢ Courier
                  ➢ Registered mail
   Day 20–24 – Delivery and Return Expectation
      • Employee is expected to receive the 2nd RTWO with NTE via courier
      • Employee expected to report to Immediate Supervisor
      • Supervisor confirms whether employee has returned
   Day 25 – Maximum Delivery Window (Courier)
      • Lapse of 5 calendar days from 1st attempt to deliver
   Day 26 – Final Hearing or Decision Path
      • If employee requests hearing:
         o Conduct administrative hearing
      • If no response:
         o Proceed to final decision drafting
   Day 27–38 – Case Deliberation and Final Decision Drafting
      • HRBP and Deliberation Committee:
         o Review all documentation (RTWO, NTEs, responses, attendance records)
         o Ensure due process compliance
         o Draft Final Notice of Decision
   Day 39–40 – Final Approval
      • VP, HR Employee Relations reviews and approves Final Notice of Decision
   Day 41 – Final Notice of Decision Issuance
      • Serve Final NOD (including termination if applicable):
      o Docusign
      o Email (work and personal)
      o Courier
      o Registered mail
      • Upload all final documents to system of record
      • Close case with complete documentation
                              --END PROCESS FOR SCENARIO 2--

6. Detailed Process Guidelines
    1. All NCNS incidents must be reported on the first day of occurrence
    2. HRBP determines appropriate disciplinary action based on Code of Conduct
    3. All communications must be documented and stored in the system of record

                               For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

      4. Timeframes are indicative and may vary depending on case circumstances
      5. Employee responses must be formally recorded

7. Documentation and Storage
    • All RTWO, NTE, and NOD documents must be stored in the employee’s record in the
      system of record
    • A single authoritative version must be maintained
    • Documents must not be stored in personal drives or email as final copies

8. References
    • Code of Conduct
    • Attendance Policy
    • Philippine Labor Code (Article 297)

9. Version History
Version            Date                           Owner           Description
1.0                2019-05-24                     HR BP           Initial version
2.0                2024-07-26                     HR BP           Process updates and
                                                                  communication channels
3.0                 2026-04-24                    HR BP           Timeline updates and
                                                                  RTWO enhancements

10. Notes
    • This document must be reviewed annually
    • Any exceptions must be approved by HR Compliance

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

HR – Smoke-Free Workplace – Policy

Document Code: HR-POL 12
Document Type: Policy
Description: Establishes requirements for maintaining a smoke-free workplace on
RealPage premises, at company-sponsored activities, and in company-owned, leased, or
company-paid vehicles.
Owner: Human Resource Business Partner
Audience: RealPage employees and all persons on company premises
Country/Jurisdiction: Philippines
System of Record: UKG People Articles
Version Number: 1.1
Last Review Date: May 1, 2024
Effective Date: June 1, 2024
Approval Date: June 1, 2024
Approver: Ivy de Borja
Classification: Internal Use
Document Status: Final
Next Review Date: August 14, 2027
Reason for Change: Expanded the policy to include company-paid transportation/vehicles
and clarified that e-cigarettes include vaping.

I. POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTTIVES

It is the policy of RealPage to prohibit smoking on all company premises in order to provide
and maintain a safe and healthy work environment for all employees.

II. ELIGIBILITY

The policy applies to all RealPage employees and all persons in company premises, at all
times.

III. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

   1. REWS – Works with the building admin & Government body in reinforcing policy on
      Smoke-free workplace.

   2. HR – Creates awareness and remind employees on the Smoke-free workplace

IV. GUIDELINES

   1. The smoke-free workplace policy applies to all persons in:

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

a. All areas of company buildings;

b. All company-sponsored events.

c. All company-sponsored off-site conferences and meetings. This includes video
conference meetings.

d. All vehicles owned or leased and/or paid by the company

    2. Smoking is permitted only in locations that have designated smoking areas outside
       of the building.

    3. Employees who violate the smoking policy will be subject to disciplinary action
       stated in the Company’s Code of Conduct. In case the Building Administrator
       imposes a fine for violating the no smoking policy of the building, the erring
       employee shall reimburse the company for the same amount of penalty incurred.

    4. Smoking includes the use of tobacco, e-cigarettes (also known as vaping).

               Total Rewards – Corporate Clinic – Guidelines and Procedures –

               Guidelines and procedures governing the operation of the RealPage
               Philippines corporate clinic, including medical consultation,
Description

               emergency room conduction, and accident reporting processes.

Audience

1. Purpose

Having a corporate clinic at RealPage Philippines, Inc. serves as a valuable resource for
employees in the Philippines. By providing convenient access to healthcare services within
the workplace, the company aims to promote employee health and well-being, leading to
increased productivity and morale.

This document contains the corporate clinic processes and procedures intended to
support preventive care services and early interventions, help maintain a safe and healthy
workplace, and support adherence to applicable Occupational Safety and Health
Standards requirements based on the OSH Law (DOLE-BWC).

This document serves as a guide to medical staff regarding the standard operating
procedures applicable to Clinic Management services.

The contents of this document are not definitive and should be supplemented by
applicable guidelines that may be issued by relevant government agencies from time to
time.

2. Scope

The provisions of this document apply to:

   •   All employees of RealPage Philippines, Inc.

   •   All clinic staff provided by the company’s vendor partner, whether permanent or
       reliever.

3. Definitions

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

Employee

Refers to all personnel of RealPage Philippines, Inc.

Local Operations Leaders

The employee’s Supervisor, Manager, and Director based in the Philippines.

Occupational Health Nurse (OH Nurse)

A nurse duly licensed to practice their profession in the Philippines and possessing all
additional qualifications required under Rule 1964.01 of the Occupational Safety and
Health Standards.

Occupational Health Doctor (OH Doctor)

A physician duly licensed to practice their profession in the Philippines and possessing all
additional qualifications required under Rule 1964.01 of the Occupational Safety and
Health Standards.

Medical Certificate

A document issued by an attending physician that attests to the result of a medical
examination of a patient. It may serve as documentation that an employee is unfit for work
or as evidence of a health condition.

The certificate must be validated by the corporate clinic doctors where validation is
required under the process described in this document.

Fit to Work Evaluation

An objective examination of an employee’s health to determine whether the employee is fit
to return to work.

A fit-to-work clearance is issued by the attending physician following the evaluation and
must be submitted to and validated by the clinic doctors in accordance with the applicable
company process.

Health Case Management (HCM) Tracker

A census of employees who visit or call the corporate clinic for medical consultation.

4. General Guidelines and Procedures

A. Medical Consultation

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

   1. The employee visits the corporate clinic.

   2. The OH Nurse greets and receives the employee.

   3. The OH Nurse conducts an initial assessment and properly records the information
      in the patient medical record.

   4. The OH Nurse identifies whether the employee needs to be recorded in the Health
      Case Management (HCM) Tracker.

   5. If the OH Doctor is on duty, the OH Nurse refers the employee to the OH Doctor for
      consultation.

   6. If the OH Doctor is off duty, the OH Nurse refers the employee to another corporate
      clinic for consultation.

   7. The OH Doctor provides an assessment, diagnosis, and appropriate medical advice
      and determines the final disposition.

Possible dispositions include:

   •   Return to workstation

   •   Medicine dispensing

   •   Clinic rest

   •   Send home

   •   Emergency Room (ER) conduction

Note: In the absence of the OH Doctor, the OH Nurse may provide management and
intervention within the OH Nurse’s scope of practice.

A.1 Return to Workstation

The employee returns to the workstation following the medical consultation when
medically appropriate.

A.2 Medicine Dispensing

   1. The OH Doctor prescribes the medicine.

   2. The OH Nurse dispenses the appropriate medication or medication prescribed by
      the OH Doctor.

   3. The employee records the transaction in the medicine dispensing log sheet.

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

A.3 Clinic Rest

   1. The OH Doctor recommends clinic rest.

   2. The OH Nurse obtains the employee’s emergency contact details.

   3. The OH Nurse allows the employee to rest in the clinic based on the OH Doctor’s
      recommendation, but not to exceed one hour.

   4. The OH Nurse sends an email notification to the employee’s Local Operations
      Leaders.

   5. If the employee’s condition improves after clinic rest, the employee is asked to
      return to the workstation.

   6. If the employee’s condition does not improve, the OH Doctor provides the final
      disposition, such as Send Home or ER Conduction.

   7. The OH Nurse informs the employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

Note: Time spent by employees during clinic rest is considered unpaid if it exceeds the
employee’s meal breaks.

A.4 Send Home

   1. The OH Doctor provides further advice and prescribes medication, if applicable.

   2. The OH Nurse gives further instructions to the employee.

   3. The OH Nurse informs the employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

   4. The employee signs the waiver/release form.

   5. Upon arrival at the residence or hospital, the employee submits the signed waiver
      form by email to the Corporate Nurse.

   6. The employee is sent home and is required to present a medical certificate upon
      return to work.

   7. If the employee was seen by an OH Doctor, whether by telehealth or onsite, the OH
      Doctor may issue the medical certificate for a simple or non-complex case, subject
      to the attending physician’s assessment.

   8. If the case is complex and the employee is referred to a specialist, the specialist
      issues the medical certificate.

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

Note: If there is no OH Nurse or OH Doctor in the corporate clinic, an OH Nurse or OH
Doctor in another corporate clinic may make the recommendation to the Local Operations
Leader.

A.5 Emergency Room Conduction Process

Non-Life-Threatening Cases

   1. The OH Nurse informs the employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

   2. The OH Nurse obtains the employee’s emergency contact details.

   3. The OH Nurse informs the Security team for assistance.

   4. The employee is transported to the nearest medical facility through an appropriate
      private conduction method, such as a company/private vehicle or Transportation
      Network Vehicle Service (TNVS).

   5. The OH Nurse accompanies the employee.

   6. Security notifies the Local Operations Leaders regarding the conduction.

   7. The OH Nurse leaves a notice at the clinic indicating OUT FOR ER CONDUCTION.

   8. The OH Nurse may wait for the employee’s relative before leaving the medical
      facility if another medical staff member is available to manage the corporate clinic.

   9. The OH Nurse submits the ER conduction report to the Local Operations Leaders
      within the shift.

   10. The OH Nurse follows up on the employee’s health status within 24 hours following
       conduction.

Life-Threatening Cases

   1. The OH Nurse informs the employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

   2. The OH Nurse obtains the employee’s emergency contact details.

   3. The OH Nurse endorses the employee to the nearest medical facility and contacts
      the accredited ambulance provider, private vehicle, or TNVS as appropriate.

   4. The OH Nurse informs the Security team regarding the ambulance conduction.

   5. The employee is transported by ambulance, private vehicle, or TNVS.

   6. The OH Doctor accompanies the employee to the medical facility. If the OH Doctor
      is unavailable, the OH Nurse accompanies the employee.

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

   7. The OH Doctor or OH Nurse waits for the employee’s relative before leaving the
      medical facility.

   8. The OH Nurse submits the ER conduction report to the Local Operations Leaders
      within the shift.

   9. The OH Nurse follows up on the employee’s health status within 24 hours following
      conduction.

Note: If the OH Nurse is the only medical staff member managing the corporate clinic at
the time of conduction, the OH Nurse informs the onsite first aiders so they may assist with
situations requiring immediate attention.

B. Teleconsultation Process

   1. The employee calls the clinic.

   2. The OH Nurse greets the employee and accommodates the call.

   3. The OH Nurse conducts an initial assessment and properly records the information
      in the patient medical record.

   4. The OH Nurse determines whether the employee needs to be recorded in the Health
      Case Management (HCM) Tracker.

   5. If the OH Doctor is on duty, the OH Nurse refers the employee for consultation.

   6. If the OH Doctor is off duty, the OH Nurse refers the employee to another corporate
      clinic for consultation.

   7. The OH Doctor provides an assessment, diagnosis, and appropriate medical advice.

   8. The OH Doctor sends email documentation to the OH Nurse.

   9. The OH Nurse forwards the documentation to the employee.

Note: In the absence of an OH Doctor, the OH Nurse may provide management and
intervention within the OH Nurse’s scope of practice.

C. Fit to Work Evaluation

Fit to Work Evaluation is intended to help determine whether employees returning from
illness or injury are fit to resume work.

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

   1. The employee visits the corporate clinic.

   2. The OH Nurse greets and receives the employee.

   3. The OH Nurse conducts an initial assessment and properly records the information
      in the patient medical record.

   4. The OH Nurse determines whether the employee should be recorded in the Health
      Case Management (HCM) Tracker.

   5. If the OH Doctor is on duty, the OH Nurse refers the employee for consultation.

   6. If the OH Doctor is off duty, the OH Nurse may provide management and
      intervention within the OH Nurse’s scope of practice.

   7. An employee determined to be fit to work is allowed to return to the workstation.

   8. An employee determined not to be fit to work is sent home.

   9. The OH Nurse informs the employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

Note: In the absence of the OH Doctor, the OH Nurse may schedule a teleconsultation
with an OH Doctor from another worksite. The teleconsulting doctor assesses and
manages the patient accordingly.

Upon the employee’s return from sick leave, the employee consults the onsite OH Doctor.
Following the evaluation, the onsite OH Doctor issues the fit-to-work determination as
applicable.

The teleconsulting and onsite OH Doctors coordinate internally regarding the employee’s
case.

If the employee was referred to a specialist, the specialist issues the fit-to-work certificate.

Important: If a specific return-to-work date is not indicated on the initial medical
certificate, the employee should have a follow-up consultation with the attending
physician, whether an external physician or Corporate Doctor depending on the case, and
obtain a separate fit-to-work clearance.

D. Medical Certificate Validation

Medical Certificate Validation is intended to support the authenticity and accuracy of
employee health documentation and maintain a healthy, safe, and efficient workplace.

                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

Not all medical certificates require validation. Only certificates issued by non-HMO-
accredited doctors are subject to the validation process described below.

   1. The employee submits a medical certificate to the clinic for validation.

   2. The OH Nurse acknowledges receipt of the medical certificate within 24 hours.

   3. The OH Doctor, or OH Nurse under the supervision of the OH Doctor, validates the
      medical certificate.

   4. Minimum turnaround time is within the shift, while maximum turnaround time is one
      to three days.

   5. In addition to validating the medical certificate, the OH Doctor reviews the attending
      physician’s recommendations in the context of RealPage’s business operations and
      recommends the most appropriate course of action.

   6. The OH Nurse sends the results of the medical certificate validation to the
      employee’s Local Operations Leaders.

   7. The validation result includes the details of the person from the doctor’s clinic who
      confirmed or denied the medical certificate.

   8. The OH Nurse reviews the medical certificate for validity or erroneous details.

Note: An employee may return to work and remain productive while validation of the
medical certificate is ongoing, provided the case is non-communicable or non-contagious.

RealPage reserves the right to request a copy of laboratory tests and medications.

Important: Medical certificates from doctors who do not have a physical clinic and are not
part of a teleconsultation platform must include a copy of BIR 2303 and a sample blank
official receipt indicating that the doctor’s home address is their business address.

E. Accident Reporting Process

   1. The employee visits the clinic for consultation and reports the accident or injury.

   2. The OH Nurse greets and receives the employee.

   3. The OH Nurse completes the Incident Report Form.

   4. The OH Nurse reports the accident or injury to Security, OSH, HRBP, OSH Chair, and
      Site Leader.

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

   5. HRBP submits the required report to DOLE.

Note: The Medical Consultation Process applies to clinic visits related to accidents
requiring first-aid treatment.

Accident/Incident Reporting should occur within 24–48 hours.

5. Templates

The following supporting materials are associated with this controlled procedure:

Description        administration of Paid Time Off (PTO) for employees of RealPage
                   Philippines Inc.

Reason for         Updated to align with the Global HR Document Management Policy and
Change             revised PTO accrual and carry-over provisions.

I. Policy Statement, Purpose, and Scope

RealPage Philippines Inc. (“Company”) provides Paid Time Off (PTO) to support employee
well-being, work-life balance, and business continuity. PTO allows eligible employees to
take paid leave for vacation, illness, personal matters, and qualifying dependent care while
maintaining consistent business operations.

The purpose of this Policy is to establish the eligibility requirements, accrual methodology,
usage guidelines, carry-over provisions, cash conversion rules, and administrative
responsibilities governing Paid Time Off.

This Policy applies to all eligible employees.

II. Eligibility

Employees begin accruing Paid Time Off on their date of hire.

Employees become eligible to use accrued PTO beginning on their third (3rd) month of
employment.

Employees on an unpaid leave of absence for fifteen (15) consecutive calendar days do not
accrue PTO during the unpaid leave period, except during maternity leave.

III. Responsibilities

Employee Responsibilities

Employees are responsible for:

    •   Submitting PTO requests through the Company’s official timekeeping system.

    •   Obtaining manager approval before taking planned leave.

    •   Submitting requests ideally at least fourteen (14) calendar days before the intended
        PTO date, whenever reasonably possible.

    •   Providing supporting documentation when required under this Policy.

                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

Manager Responsibilities

Managers are responsible for:

   •   Reviewing PTO requests promptly.

   •   Approving or declining requests based on operational requirements and this Policy.

   •   Ensuring leave requests are reviewed and approved in a timely manner within the
       official timekeeping system.

Payroll Responsibilities

Payroll is responsible for processing payment of approved PTO that has been properly
submitted and approved through the official Company timekeeping system in accordance
with established payroll processing schedules.

IV. Guidelines

A. PTO Accrual

Paid Time Off is accrued and credited on a semi-monthly basis according to the
employee’s completed years of service.

Years of Service   Semi-monthly Accrual      Annual Accrual

Less than 5 years 0.835 days                 20 days

5 years and above 1.25 days                  30 days

Accrual Posting: Middle and end of each month.

B. PTO Usage

Paid Time Off may be used in increments of one-half (0.5) day or one (1) full day and may be
taken at the employee’s discretion, subject to this Policy.

C. Medical Documentation

A Medical Certificate or Physician’s Statement is required when:

   •   An employee is absent due to illness for two (2) or more consecutive workdays; or

   •   An employee is absent because of a contagious illness.

The Company reserves the right to request additional medical documentation when
appropriate.

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

D. PTO Loan

Employees who have insufficient accrued PTO due to illness may receive up to two (2) PTO
loan days through October of each calendar year.

Borrowed PTO will automatically be deducted from future PTO accruals until fully repaid.

V. PTO Carry-Over and Cash Conversion

A. Carry-Over

At the end of each calendar year, Payroll will calculate each employee’s unused PTO
balance.

Employees may carry forward unused PTO into the following calendar year subject to the
limits below.

Years of Service   Maximum Carry-Over

Less than 5 years 5 days

5 years and above 10 days

Carried-over PTO must be used no later than June 30 of the following calendar year.

Unused carried-over PTO remaining after June 30 will be forfeited.

B. Cash Conversion

Unused PTO exceeding the allowable carry-over limit will be converted to cash subject to
the following limits.

Years of Service   Maximum Cash Conversion

Less than 5 years 10 days

5 years and above 15 days

Cash conversion is subject to applicable tax withholdings.

Unused PTO that is not converted to cash or carried over in accordance with this Policy will
be forfeited. Any carried-over PTO must be used by June 30 of the following year; otherwise,
it will be forfeited.

C. Separation from Employment

                                For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                          Internal Use

Upon separation from employment, earned and unused PTO will be paid in accordance
with applicable law and Company policy as part of the employee’s final pay, subject to
applicable payroll deductions and statutory requirements.

I. Overview and Objective

The SSS maternity benefit is a government-mandated benefit intended to protect and
promote the rights and welfare of working women. The benefit provides eligible female
employees with leave to support recovery, health and wellness, and maternal
responsibilities.

This procedure defines the internal process for administering the SSS maternity benefit
within RealPage Philippines Inc.

II. Scope

This procedure describes the end-to-end internal process for female employees and
responsible stakeholders when an employee applies for and receives the SSS maternity
benefit.

It applies to RealPage Philippines female employees and Total Rewards, HR, Finance, and
Payroll stakeholders involved in maternity-benefit administration.

III. Roles and Responsibilities

1. Employee

The employee is responsible for:

   •   Notifying the employer of her pregnancy and expected date of childbirth.

   •   Providing the forms and supporting documentation required by SSS and the
       employer.

   •   Completing applicable maternity-benefit documentation.

2. Total Rewards Team

The Total Rewards Team is responsible for:

   •   Receiving and validating required forms and supporting documents.

   •   Completing the maternity notification process.

   •   Reporting the maternity notification through the SSS system.

   •   Computing the SSS benefit due to the employee.

   •   Preparing and submitting the required Request for Payment and supporting
       documents.

   •   Coordinating with Finance & Payroll for processing of the benefit.

   •   Submitting applicable documentation to SSS for reimbursement.

3. Total Rewards Leader

The Total Rewards leader is responsible for reviewing and approving the Request for
Payment associated with maternity-benefit processing.

4. Finance & Payroll Team

The Finance and Payroll Team are responsible for processing the advance payment of the
SSS maternity benefit and applicable salary differential respectively after receiving the
endorsed and approved documentation from Total Rewards Team.

VI. Guidelines

1. Pregnancy Notification

Upon confirmation of pregnancy, the employee shall inform the employer of the pregnancy
and expected date of childbirth.

2. Eligibility

To be eligible for the benefit, the employee should have at least three monthly
contributions within the 12-month period immediately preceding the semester of
childbirth, miscarriage, or emergency termination of pregnancy.

3. Maternity Leave Benefit

The maternity benefit is a paid leave benefit with full pay for the following durations:

    •   One hundred five (105) days for live childbirth, regardless of type of delivery.

    •   An additional fifteen (15) days of paid leave if the employee qualifies as a solo
        parent.

    •   Sixty (60) days of paid leave for miscarriage and emergency termination of
        pregnancy, including stillbirth.

    •   An additional thirty (30) days of unpaid leave may be availed where the employee
        has notified the employer and managers within a reasonable period or at least 45
        days before the end of the maternity leave originally filed.

    •   The employee may file for maternity leave as early as 45 days before the expected
        date of delivery.

4. Full Pay and Salary Differential

Full pay refers to the remuneration or earnings paid by an employer to a worker for services
rendered on normal working days and hours.

                                   For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

The existing procedure defines the calculation as:

Full Pay = SSS Benefit + Employer Salary Differential

The SSS portion is computed based on the employee's average daily salary credit.

The existing procedure also states that the salary differential is non-taxable and that
applicable statutory contributions shall be deducted.

5. Allocation of Maternity Leave

The employee may allocate up to seven (7) days of the maternity benefit to the child's
father, whether or not the father is married to the employee, or alternate caregiver

In the event of the death, absence, or incapacity of the child's father, the employee may
allocate the applicable leave to an alternate caregiver identified in the existing procedure
as:

   •   A relative within the fourth degree of consanguinity; or

   •   The employee's current partner, regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity,
       who shares the same household.

6. SSS Reimbursement

After completion of post maternity documents, the employer must submit the required
documents to SSS for processing of the maternity-benefit reimbursement.

I. Policy Statement and Objective

This policy defines the eligibility, coverage, requirements, and procedures for employees
availing of the Wellness Reimbursement benefit.

II. Eligibility

All full-time, regular employees are eligible to avail of this benefit.

Employees must be eligible at the time qualified expenses are incurred, applied for, and
processed. Qualified expenses must be incurred within the applicable calendar year, from
January 1 through December 31 of the same year.

This benefit is exclusive to RealPage employees.

III. Definition of Terms

1. Leave of Absence

For purposes of this policy, the reason for the leave of absence should not be maternity- or
medical-related. Examples listed in the existing policy include COVID-related
circumstances, further education, relocation, inability to work in the office, or inability to
work from home.

IV. Guidelines

1. Benefit Amount

Reimbursement is available up to a maximum of Php 5,000.00 per calendar year, based
on the employee being in regular status at the beginning of the calendar year.

For new hires who become regular employees during the calendar year, the benefit is
calculated on a pro-rated basis from the employee's regularization date:

Php 5,000 ÷ 12 months = Php 416.66 per month

                                   For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

Php 416.66 × remaining number of months in the reimbursable year from the date of
regularization

For eligible employees who have utilized the wellness fund and separate from the company
during the calendar year, the benefit is calculated on a pro-rated basis based on the
separation date. Any overpayment will be recovered through final pay:

Introduction
As organizations navigate the complexities of talent acquisition and retention, internal mobility has become
a key strategy for building a resilient and adaptable workforce. In an industry where agility is essential,
having a structured and documented internal mobility approach is crucial for fostering a dynamic and
engaged employee base.

At RealPage, we are proud to have a global team of talented employees who collaborate to support our
customers and drive business growth. To sustain this momentum and help employees achieve their career
goals, we actively promote and support internal mobility, which is the internal transfer of an employee into a
different role and/or location within the company and includes both vertical and lateral movement.
Leveraging the talent already within our organization allows employees to advance, reskill, and explore new
growth opportunities, fostering a more diverse workforce at all levels.

Together, we can ensure both company-wide success and personal career development.

This document outlines RealPage’s approach to internal mobility, including guiding principles and recommended
steps for all stakeholders to follow.

Benefits of Internal Mobility
The benefits of internal mobility extend far beyond simply filling vacant positions, positively impacting not
only individual employees but also team dynamics, organizational culture and the bottom line. Below are key
advantages that make internal mobility a cornerstone of successful talent management strategies.

Drives Employee Engagement
A demonstrated investment in employee growth and development significantly boosts employee
engagement. When organizations prioritize internal mobility, employees feel valued and motivated, seeing
clear pathways for both upward and lateral career progression within the company. This sense of possibility
and personal growth keeps employees intellectually stimulated, leading to higher levels of engagement and
productivity.

Retains Top Talent
Research shows that 70% of employees would explore opportunities within their current organization
before looking externally. By developing job skills within our organization and providing opportunities for
mobility, we can achieve higher retention rates and reduce employee turnover.

Fosters Inclusion and Diversity
Internal mobility fosters inclusion and diversity by providing employees from all backgrounds the
opportunity to advance, reskill, and explore new roles within the organization. This approach ensures that a
wide range of perspectives, experiences and skills are represented across various levels, contributing to a
more inclusive and equitable workforce.

Boosts Productivity
On average, it takes 28 weeks for a new employee to reach full productivity in a mid-level role. Internal
mobility allows us to easily identify our existing employees, who already know our business and are ready to
grow their careers.

Saves Time and Money
The cost to replace an employee can be as high as 50% to 60% of their salary with overall losses to the
company ranging from 90% to 200%. Two of the biggest benefits of an internal mobility strategy are cost
savings and the ability to operate more efficiently — especially during a time when many organizations are
operating with leaner teams after scaling down in response to economic challenges.

Definitions
RealPage supports internal mobility – the internal transfer of an employee into a different role and/or
location within the company. The following definitions are intended to clarify role changes that are
considered internal mobility.

                                                  Internal Use

Roles in the Internal Mobility Process
Employee
• Self-reflect on your career goals. Ask HR for Development resources to facilitate your career planning.
• Discuss your areas of interests with your current manager. You do not need to wait for a specific
   opportunity to open a conversation with the managers and colleagues in the areas you are interested in.

• Research available opportunities by navigating to our Employee Internal Career Portal:
     • https://employees-realpagepms.icims.com/
     • In the top right corner, click Employee Login and login (using your RealPage Single-Sign On (SSO)

      • Tip: Chrome browser is preferred

• When you identify an opportunity that you are interested in or you wish to pursue, you are required to
   inform your current manager as a courtesy. This communication is not a request for permission, as all
   employees at RealPage have the autonomy to explore any internal roles in which they are interested. If
   you need assistance preparing for this conversation, HR is available to support you.
• Involve a RealPage recruiter for support during the interview process or your HRBP for additional
   assistance.
• If selected for the role, work with your current manager on developing a transition plan and share your
   ideas on potential internal successors for the role you are leaving vacant.

• Consult with both your current and hiring manager before communicating any organizational changes.

                                                  Internal Use

Current Manager
• Respond to your employee’s interest in another role with a “One RealPage” mindset. Remember:
    RealPage actively supports employees’ career development and will provide them with career
    opportunities to help them achieve their goals while enabling RealPage to retain top talent.

• Understand the internal mobility process and align with your HRBP for support throughout the process.
• Ensure your management team and functional leader are aware of any internal talent movement.
• Provide accurate, balanced feedback on performance and potential.

If an internal candidate is selected:
Ensure all goals/notes are updated in the HRIS system prior to the transition.

• Discuss and align on the transition period with the hiring manager. Do not put the employee in the
    middle of this discussion.

• Create a transition plan, in alignment with the employee, that enables success for the entire team.
• Once the current employee has accepted a new role, begin working on the plan to best utilize the
    headcount for the role being vacated.

If an internal candidate is not selected:

• Confirm that the employee’s current role is secured for them and reaffirm your commitment to their
    professional development.
•   Facilitate frequent professional development conversations with the employee.
•   Ensure the employee understands that internal opportunities are encouraged by supporting a
    development plan based on career aspirations and aligning them to current and future roles.

                                                   Internal Use

HR Business Partner
• Be a proactive career advocate.
• Provide advisory support to the employee and manager throughout the process.
• Ensure that all parties are acting with a “One RealPage” mindset and in full support of enabling internal
   career mobility for RealPagers.

• Ensure performance feedback is reviewed and considered.
• Provide compensation recommendations, if applicable.
• Support organizational transition plans and collaborate with functional and regional HRBPs as needed.
   Transition time should be consistent with the employee’s contractual notice period, if any, unless
   otherwise agreed between the employee, current, and hiring managers. Please note: Contractual notice
   periods can vary by country.

Recruiter
• With the knowledge of the HRBPs and managers, proactively seek internal candidates for open
   positions.

• Make internal candidate sourcing and recruiting the priority in generating candidate pools for open
   positions.

• Ensure the employee has informed their current manager when they express interest in a role.
• Notify the HRBP of internal candidates.
• Work with the hiring manager to define a fair and inclusive selection process.
• Provide support for the employee and management teams throughout the process. If there is any
   indication of resistance to the "One RealPage" mindset, or for enabling internal mobility, inform the
   HRBP.

• Stay closely aligned with the HRBP, hiring and current managers throughout the process.
• Screen all internal candidates to assess capabilities, skill set, and career goals.
• Manage internal interview schedules and obtain feedback from the interview team, ensuring that the
   process is inclusive and unbiased.

• Work with the HRBP to confirm timing of the compensation adjustment for the selected internal
   candidate as it might not be automatically after the move, but subject to eligibility criteria and budget
   approval process.

                                                    Internal Use

Hiring Manager
• Involve the employee’s current manager before approaching an employee on another team within the
   organization.

• Seek feedback on performance and potential from multiple sources before making a decision.

If internal candidate is selected:

• Work with your recruiter to confirm the job level, title and compensation before discussing these topics
   with the employee.

• Negotiate the transition period with the current manager. Transition time should be consistent with the
   employee’s contractual notice period, if any, unless otherwise agreed between the employee, current,
   and hiring managers. Please note: Contractual notice periods can vary by country. If you have any
   questions or need further clarification, please consult your HRBP.

If internal candidate is not selected:

• Provide transparent feedback on why the internal candidate was not selected and any suggestions on
   what they can work on to improve their chance of success next time.

• If appropriate, provide feedback to the current manager on possible development opportunities to help
   support the employee’s career growth.

We look forward to nurturing and developing our internal talent and fostering a culture where every employee
has the opportunity to grow, thrive and achieve their full potential while delivering our business goals. For any
questions, please contact the HR Team.

Introduction
To get the most from this handbook, keep the following in mind: Other than the Dispute Resolution Policy,
which sets forth the manner in which you and the Company agree to address workplace issues, it contains
only general information and guidelines and is not intended to be comprehensive or to address all the possible
applications of, or exceptions to, the general policies and procedures described. For that reason, if you have any
questions concerning eligibility for a particular benefit or the applicability of a policy or practice, you should
direct your specific questions to Human Resources.

Except for the Dispute Resolution Policy, which is a binding contract between you and the Company, nothing
in this handbook is intended to constitute a guarantee of employment or contract for employment (express or
implied) for any specified period of time. Either RealPage or the employee may end this relationship at any time
with or without cause, notice, or reason. No manager, supervisor, or representative other than RealPage’s chief
executive officer or the chief financial officer has the authority to enter into any written agreement guaranteeing
you employment for any specific period of time or to make any written or oral promises, agreements, or
commitments contrary to this policy. Further, any employment agreement entered into by the chief executive
officer or chief financial officer will not be enforceable unless it is in writing.

The procedures, practices, policies and benefits described here may be modified or discontinued from time to
time. RealPage will adhere to these policies except to the extent that they conflict with federal, state or local
laws. Applicable laws will take precedence in these cases.

If an employee is accused of violating any provision of the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, any other
rules of conduct, or the Employee Handbook, RealPage will take the appropriate corrective action, up to and
including termination based on the facts of the situation.

You may also be subject to policies and rules other than those described in this handbook to meet business
requirements. Official policy documents give detailed descriptions of some subjects described in this handbook.

RealPage Purpose Statement and Core Values
A strong corporate culture is built on shared purpose and values and is essential to our long-term success. Our
Purpose Statement is why we exist and what we do. At RealPage we:

                   Inspire Amazing Experiences. Deliver Exceptional Value.

Inspire is a powerful word that highlights the role we and our solutions play in our ecosystem. We Inspire Amazing
Experiences for our customers and their employees, as well as prospects and residents. We Deliver Exceptional
Value for everyone who interacts with and relies on our solutions.

We will succeed at achieving our purpose through our Core Values of Excellence, Character, Ownership
and Teamwork:

            EXCELLENCE                                                    OWNERSHIP

     Commit to Excellence                                         Own It
     1. Focus on customer success.                                1. Hold ourselves and one another accountable.

     2. Drive innovation and thought leadership.                  2. Follow through on commitments.

                                                                  4. Celebrate the joy in the journey.

                                                                                                         7

Why are core values important?
Core values are the building blocks of organizational culture, and they provide a platform for each of us as
employees to anchor to that Company culture.

Core values help shape the Company culture in everything we do, and they provide a common language across
the organization. They define how we show up to one another internally, and how we want to be understood
externally.

Core values help guide our decision making, inform our actions and emphasize what is important to the business
as the organization continues to evolve and improve.

It takes each and every one of us to lean in and live these values for them to become embedded into the culture
here at RealPage.
