                                                                                                                                  Learning & Development

What are the benefits of using My Pathway?
▪ Practicality - the learning recommendations are targeted to your unique development needs.
▪ Self-paced learning – you can complete the courses anytime, anywhere, at your speed.
▪ Efficiency – the courses range from 15 – 30 minutes.
▪ Variety of topics – the platform has 34 micro-courses, 14 podcasts and 18 blogposts that target competencies to manage people, manage
  work and manage change.
▪ Soft skill development for all RealPage employees

Who can use My Pathway?

▪ New and upcoming RealPage leaders
▪ Employees can use My Pathway to stretch, grow, or prepare for future leadership roles
▪ Leaders and the HR team can take advantage of the learning courses as it applies to their roles and team situations – coaching, conflict
  management, emotional intelligence, building trust, etc.

How do I use My Pathway?
Upon logging on to My Pathway, you be asked to complete a 15-minute self-assessment. Immediately after completing the assessment, you will
get a two-part report – Your Personality and Your Skills.

Legal Compliance Courses in RealPage University
Complete all “Assigned” legal compliance courses within your first 30 days in RealPage University.

Click here to log on to RealPage University. Once logged in, you can find the courses under your
“Assigned” tasks on the home page. Note: Only complete the courses assigned to you.

For first-time users or if you are experiencing RPU access issues, click here.

HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)
Overview: The HIPAA Policies & Procedures course reviews the privacy of information as HIPAA
mandates. This includes protected health information (PHI), electronic PHI (ePHI), and personally
identifiable information (PII).

Security Awareness
Overview: Protecting RealPage’s information and information systems is our responsibility. This
course is designed to provide you with the critical information you need to detect threats to
information security and the means to protect against those threats. You will learn about security
essentials including but not limited to phishing techniques, secure password management, safe web
browsing, mobile and physical security, and secure remote working.

Anti-Corruption
Overview: Anti-Corruption Policies & Procedures reviews the RealPage anti-corruption policy. It also
discusses highlights of the U.S. Federal Corruption Practices Act and the UK Bribery Act.

Anti-Harassment
Overview: Anti-Harassment Policies & Procedures covers anti-harassment laws and the
RealPage anti-harassment policy and focuses on preventing and addressing sexual
harassment in the workplace. Learn about the definition of sexual harassment, the RealPage
anti-harassment policy, and employee obligations and reporting procedures.

For Philippine Employees Only: Occupational Safety and Health (6 modules)
Overview: The first session provides an introduction and overview of the OSH. In session two, the
General Concepts & Terminologies in OSH will be discussed. Session three equips us with the Basic
Safety Rules & Measurement for Workplace Hazards while session four teaches us the Application of
Hazards Identification, Risk Assessment & Control. Session five orients us on Workplace Emergency
Preparedness, and finally, session six tells us the mandatory Compliances on the Administrative OSH
Requirements of the Department of Labor & Employment.

For India Employees Only: Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH)
Overview: This online training helps you understand your role in creating a safe and respectful
workplace. This training addresses the elements of handling and prevention of unacceptable behavior.
It also covers basic topics like 'What is sexual harassment?' and various actions that may be
categorized as sexual harassment.

Required New Hire Orientation Sessions
Note: These sessions are required for all new hires. In some cases, the
onboarding team will reach out to you for a separate session.

RealPage’s New Hire Orientation is a crucial step in your journey with us, as it provides an
overview of our company's history, the products and services we offer, and company goals.
New Hire Orientation helps you to understand our company culture, core values, and best
practices for security awareness, which are integral to your successful onboarding with
RealPage.

New Hire Orientation (NHO) is divided into two sessions: Global and Local (Except India)

The global NHO session will focus on topics relevant to all RealPage employees, regardless of
their role or location, while the local NHO session will cover country-specific items such as HR
policies and company benefits, among others.

The schedule for both NHO sessions is generally as follows and is offered every other week:

▪ Global – Tuesday, 9 a.m. CT

▪ Local – Thursday
      – US – 9 a.m. CT
      – PH – 7 p.m. PHT

▪ India Orientation (In-person Session)

       – Third Wednesday of the month, 11:30 a.m. – 3:30 p.m. IST

The schedules above are subject to change depending on company events and country-specific
holidays. Please ensure you accept and attend all NHO sessions.

If you did not receive an invitation for any of these sessions, email: newhireonboarding@realpage.com.

New Hire Onboarding Buddy Assignment

Important: This is required for ALL new hires. Make sure to complete this process before
your new employee’s start date.

What is an Onboarding Buddy?
An Onboarding Buddy is a colleague who partners
with a new teammate during their first 90 days of
employment to offer advice, guidance, and support
to help them successfully acclimate to their new
role. As a buddy, they also act as a key point of
contact to our new joiners throughout the
onboarding process to provide insights into
RealPage’s culture, norms, product, procedures,
and policies.

Click here to learn more about the onboarding
buddy’s responsibilities.

What is your role as the New Hire’s Manager?
It is your responsibility to select the Onboarding Buddy for your new hire. When identifying
the Onboarding Buddy, they must meet the following criteria:

       ▪ Be an employee with strong performance.
       ▪ Must have great people skills.
       ▪ Must be a good representative of RealPage's Core Values: Excellence, Character,
         Ownership, and Teamwork.

Once identified, do the following:

1. Submit a Salesforce ticket. Click here for the how-to guide.
2. Schedule a meeting with the onboarding buddy and cover expectations for your new
   hire. Click here for the Onboarding Buddy Guide.

To learn more about your role as a new hire manager, click here.

This toolkit provides new hires with a checklist outlining tasks and

Our employees are at the center of everything we do at
RealPage, and it is through employee actions, feedback
and insights that we can continue to improve as an
organization. Employee Voice is our platform that
provides us with real-time insights through quarterly
pulse surveys, enabling us to be more agile and
responsive.

Click here to learn more.

To support a smooth onboarding experience, new hires have access to country-specific
resources tailored to their location. These resources provide essential information on
local policies, benefits, workplace guidelines, and support services, helping them quickly
adapt to their roles.

Visit the Onboarding SharePoint to view the resources relevant to your new hire.

Performance Management
Performance management is a continuous process of setting goals, assessing progress, and
providing ongoing feedback to ensure RealPage employees meet organizational objectives
and reach their full potential. It involves aligning individual performance with company
goals, fostering employee development, and enhancing productivity through regular
communication and evaluation.

Click here to learn more.

RealStars Quarterly Recognition Program
RealStars is a quarterly recognition program that celebrates teammates who demonstrate
outstanding performance and drive impactful business outcomes for RealPage. As a leader,
you can nominate a team or individual who has exemplified the following:

▪ Set the standard for extraordinary performance and deliver exceptional impact.
▪ Drive significant positive business outcomes for RealPage.
▪ Exhibit our Core Values.
▪ Uphold our Purpose Statement: Inspire Amazing Experiences. Deliver Exceptional
  Value.

RealStars winners will be announced during our global Town Halls. Click here to view the
winners.

making_performance_goals_smart_ddi.title: Making Performance Goals SMART (DDI)
making_performance_goals_smart_ddi.text:
Setting SMART Goals to Manage Performance                               ►

                                              Making Performance Goals SMART

Criteria for Well-Written Goals
For a performance goal to be well written and effective, it needs to meet certain criteria. The
acronym SMART is a good way to outline this criteria.

SMART stands for:

•   Specific—defines specific results to be achieved.
•   Measurable—defines quantity, cost, or quality metrics to determine progress.
•   Attainable—allows the goal to be challenging, yet the person can still ensure results.
•   Relevant—supports the achievement of team or organizational goals.
•   Time bound—specifies a due date, time frame, or frequency rate.

Tips for Writing SMART Goals
•   Start each goal with an action verb (for example, Increase, Complete, Attain).
•   Define quantity, cost, timeliness, and/or quality as well as any due dates or time frames.
•   Avoid writing “all or nothing” goals. For example, “Train everyone in the department on the new
    software system by the end of the third quarter” is a goal that’s either met or it’s not. Instead,
    provide flexibility to make the goal more attainable, such as a range: “Train 95–100 percent of
    the department . . .”
•   Don’t mistake tasks or activities for performance goals. For example, “Polling service
    representatives to find out if they are seeing certain trends in product usage” is an activity that
    may be one of many tasks to be completed to achieve a performance goal.
•   Make sure each goal is observable. If you are the direct report, the results of your efforts need to
    be evident to you and others who will provide feedback on performance.
•   Limit the number of goals to between one and three for each major output of the job to make
    the overall performance plan realistic. You always can add or modify as needed.
•   If you are the direct report, ask yourself: Does this goal benefit me, the team, and the
    organization? If you are the leader, ask the direct report: Does this goal benefit you, our team,
    and the organization? If not, consider rewriting it.

                                                                            Internal Use

Overview & Guidelines

As we continue to embody our Core Values to Inspire Amazing Experiences, Deliver Exceptional Values, your Learning & Development
team has created and prepared this Team Building and Icebreaker Activity Resource Guide for you to engage, connect, and get to
know your team members while enhancing skills and competencies.

This resource guide contains 20 team building and/or ice-breaking activities along with instructions for each of them. This resource
guide is also available on the UKG Home Page under “Teambuilding Resources.”

Team Building and Icebreaker Activities Definition

Team Building Activities: Team-building activities are games, meetings, activities or events designed to motivate members of a group to get to
know, bond and build respect for one another. Team building activities focus on making a group become more cohesive.

Icebreaker Activities: Icebreakers are quick activities designed to help employees get to know each other and usually involve sharing names and
other background information.

Guidelines
• Identify if the team would need a team building or an icebreaker activity based on the definition given above.
• Review the table and the list of activities on the next slide to decide which would address your team’s needs.
• Schedule the activities during work hours.
• If you plan to conduct the activity face-to-face, make sure to prepare a venue, as needed, ahead of time.
• Read the activity details and prepare the activity materials in advance.
• Before facilitating an activity, explain the intent for conducting it. Encourage collaboration, not competition.
• If you have any questions or support needed, please reach out to your respective HR Business Partners.

My N.A.M.E
Overview: An activity in which participants introduce themselves
by presenting their first names as acronyms
Competency/Skill Target: Team Engagement
Time to Complete: 10 to 15 minutes
Meeting Type: Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:

▪ Give the group 5 minutes to think of interesting facts about
  themselves that correspond to the letters of their first name.
▪ Have each participant share his or her acronym.
▪ For example… “Hi, I’m Logan. L is for Led Zepplin, one of my
  favorite rock groups. O is for Ohio, which is where I live. G is
  for German, the only foreign language I know. A is for Aunt
  Wendee, my favorite relative. And N is for Nice, because I am
  a nice guy!”

Sweet Stories
Overview: An activity in which participants share a story about
themselves based on the color of the candy they have in their hands.
Competency/Skill Target: Trust, Building Relationships
Time to Complete: 15 to 20 minutes
Material/s needed: Colored M&Ms, Starburst or jellybeans
Meeting Type: Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Team Building or Icebreaker

 Instructions:
▪ Take turns sharing with the group a story based on the following code:
▪ Blue candy: A time at work when you felt very proud.
▪ Green candy: A boss you respected and why.
▪ Yellow candy: A reason you are proud to belong to this organization.
▪ Brown candy: A work experience that stands out to you.
▪ Orange candy: A time at work when a project or task didn’t go as
    planned.
▪ Red candy: A funny thing that happened to you at work.
▪ Each participant will be given 2 minutes to share their stories.

The Compliment Circle

Overview: To foster a culture of appreciation by encouraging team
members to provide positive feedback for each other
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Communication, Feedback
Time to Complete: 15 minutes
Material/s needed: Pens and Post-it Notes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
Team members will spend 10 minutes writing compliments for each team
member.
▪ This activity is good for groups of 4-8 people.
▪ Each team member will take turns being the compliment receiver.
  Each team member will share the compliment written for the
  compliment receiver.
▪ The compliment receiver cannot respond to the compliments other
  than to say, “thank you”.
▪ Compliments can be one word or 1-2 sentences.

Building a Storyline
Overview: Team members will complete a story by completing
another person’s sentence. Through this activity, participants can
enhance their listening skills and collaboration.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Listening
Time to Complete: 15 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
▪ Arrange participants in a circle or create sequence who would
    go after each other.
▪ One team member starts narrating a story but stops with an
    incomplete sentence.
▪ For example, “Jane was on her way to the office. She stopped
    at the local coffee shop to…”
▪ The next person finishes the sentence and adds another
    incomplete sentence.
▪ This goes on until the final person in the circle does the same.

Draw, Partner
Overview: Partners will draw a picture using only the other’s instructions. Through this
activity, team members can learn to give clear instructions, ask follow-up questions and
decipher directions with little outside information.
Competency/Skill Target: Listening, Asking probing questions
Time to Complete: 15 minutes
Materials needed: Photos - click here
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or virtual
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
Split the group into pairs. Instruct each pair to stand with their backs to each other
▪ Give one partner a pen and paper, and the other a drawing/photo.
▪ Direct the partner with the drawing to describe the picture to the other partner, who will
    draw the object.
▪ Each pair will be given 3 minutes to complete their drawing
▪ Reveal the artwork and gauge the accuracy. What would have made the instructions
    clearer? What would the communicator have done differently, if anything?
▪ Direct partners to switch roles and repeat the activity with a new picture.

Office Trivia
Overview: To test team members on how well they know the
company, their leaders, etc.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Business Acumen
Time to Complete: 15 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:
▪ Come up with 10-20 trivia questions about your workplace and
    test your team's knowledge.
▪ Sample questions may include:
     o What are our core values?
     o How many people are in our company?
     o How many people are in our department?
     o How many windows are there in the entire office?
     o What month of the year is most common for birthdays among
         our employees?
     o How many executives can you name?

Competency/Skill Target: Team Engagement, Creative Thinking,
Decision-making
Time to Complete: 10 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker

▪ Have each participant share three statements about
   themselves, 2 facts (truths) and one lie.
▪ Team members must guess which statement is the lie.

Scavenger Hunt
Overview: Scavenger hunts can be great for a team to get to know more about the chosen topic,
requiring them to identify things around the office. Employees work together as a team and
explore the office.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Problem Solving, Critical Thinking
Time to Complete: 15 minutes
Material/s needed: Mobile phones
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
▪    Set up questions for employees to uncover X number of facts or artifacts
▪    Divide players into small teams and define a starting location
▪    Each team is given a starting clue or challenge to complete
▪    Employees will have to find items hidden around a predefined location or complete certain
     challenges.
▪    Make it each team's mission to find and photograph everything on that list within a certain time
     limit
▪    The first team to complete each item on the list wins
▪    Be creative with the items, challenges, and riddles you include in your scavenger hunt. When
     thinking of challenges, consider key skills you would like to develop within your workforce.

The Marshmallow Activity

Overview: The objective of this activity is for groups to see who can build the tallest, freestanding structure using uncooked spaghetti
and marshmallows. This activity requires collaboration from participants in a short time frame. It can reveal lessons about the nature of
collaboration, teamwork, etc.

Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Problem Solving, Critical Thinking, Change Management
Time to complete: 20 minutes
Material/s needed:
▪ Package of uncooked spaghetti noodles per team (not thin)
▪ 1 bag of marshmallows per team (large is okay)
▪ Measuring tape
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face
Category: Team Building
Instructions:
▪     This activity is best for larger groups.
        o     Teams can be 3-8 people.
▪ Hand out the package of spaghetti and marshmallows to each table and give these instructions:
        o     Build the tallest freestanding structure using only the items that were handed out.
        o     Set timer for 10 minutes.
        o     Start timer – Go!
▪     Measure towers at the end
▪     Declare a winner based on the tallest structure
▪     Debrief the activity. Suggested questions:
                 - What general observations did you notice as you were building the tower?
                 - What strengths emerged as you helped to build the tower?
                 - Who within your group stood out? Why?
                 - What kind of communication was going on?
                 - Did anyone take charge? How? What did they do?
                 - Was anyone left out?
                 - If you could redo the exercise, what would you do differently?
▪     Additional variations to this activity may include:
        o     Provide an additional resource mid-way through building the tower. Example: Scotch tape.
        o     Rotate team members mid-way through building this tower. This can represent team members leaving, adding new team
              members, and/or change management.

New Leader Assimilation
Overview: This activity includes a list of questions that a team can
ask to get to know a new leader.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Communication, Leadership
Style and Expectations
Time to complete: 1-2 hours, depending on the size of the team
and number of questions.
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker
Instructions:
▪     1-2 months into a new leader assignment, a facilitator asks for
      questions from the leader’s direct reports – both personally and
      professionally. These can be asked for and collected in advance or
      flip-charted in person. Note: the new leader is not included as a
      participant for this part.
▪     The leader then comes in to answer questions provided by the
      facilitator that were “anonymously” posed to get to know the
      leader and the leader’s style.

Best Piece of Advice
Overview: This activity is for team members to get to know each
other by sharing their best piece of advice and why is important
to them.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Communication
Time to complete: 10-15 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-face or Virtual
Category: Team Building or Icebreaker
Instructions:

▪     Ask each participant to think about the best piece of advice
      you have been given.
▪     Participants take turns sharing advice, why it is important to
      them and how they have applied it.
▪     Flipchart advice for the team.

10 in Common

Overview: This activity is for team members to get to know each other
better by finding unique commonalities. This is most impactful for teams
with a lot of new people or for groups that don’t interact/work with
each other often.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Communication, Building
Relationships
Time to Complete: 20 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker or Team Building

Instructions:
▪ Break group into teams, mix teams by work group/role type.
▪ Task each team to come up with 10 things they have in common
    (exclude “we are human,” “we all work at RealPage,” etc).
▪ Bring the teams back together and ask each team to share how
    many things they found in common and their top 3 unique
    commonalities.

 Personal Artifact

 Overview: The objective of this activity is for team members to
 gain further understanding of what someone finds meaningful.
 This works best for groups of 10 – 25 people.
 Competency/Skill Target: Building Relationships
 Time to Complete: 15 minutes
 Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
 Category: Ice Breaker

 Instructions:

 ▪     Ask each person in the group to pick an item they currently
       have with them and explain what significance or memory it
       holds for them. People can use something they are wearing,
       anything in their pockets/purse, a notebook, water bottle, etc.
 ▪     If time allows the group can ask 2-3 questions about each

Team Jigsaw Puzzle

Overview: Team members will work together to complete a puzzle in
the allotted time but will have to find and barter for their missing
pieces.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Communication, Problem
Solving, Negotiation
Time to Complete: 25 – 30 minutes
Material/s needed: Puzzles (100 pieces)
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
▪    Before the game begins take a few pieces of each puzzle and put them
     in a different puzzle box
▪    Divide group into same-sized teams and give each team a different
     jigsaw puzzle with the same number of pieces (recommend 100 pieces).
▪    The goal is to finish a completed puzzle first – they will work collectively
     to figure out how to convince other teams to give up the pieces they
     need. They can barter, merge/change teams, donate minutes, or come
     up with creative problem-solving methods.

Wolf/Chicken/Grain Riddle
Overview: Teams work together to solve a riddle (within a given timeframe) and explain their
reasoning to the larger group. Works best for a smaller group – no more than 20 people.
Competency/Skill Target: Critical Thinking, Problem Solving
Time to Complete: 20 minutes (10 to solve riddle, 10 to present/discuss)
Meeting Type: Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:
▪    Divide group into teams of 3 – 5 people.
▪    Give the group the riddle: “A farmer is traveling with a wolf, chicken, and bag of grains
     comes to a river they need to cross. The boat only has room for the farmer and 1 other.
     The farmer can’t leave the wolf alone with the chicken and he can’t leave the chicken alone
     with the grain. How can he get them all across the river safely?”
▪    Teams have 10 minutes to figure out their solution.
▪    Ask each team to present their solution to the group and what method they used to solve
     the riddle.
       o Points to consider: did one person take charge? Did anyone draw/map out the
           solution? Did they come to a consensus? Who was familiar with the riddle and
           remembered it from previous experience?
▪    Answer to riddle:
       o The farmer takes the chicken over first. He brings the wolf second and comes back
           with the chicken. He drops off the chicken and takes the grain to the other side with
           the wolf. The farmer makes one last trip to retrieve the chicken.

Desert Island Intelligences

Overview: Based on Gardner’s Theory of Multiple Intelligences, this game asks your team to vote people off a deserted
island based on how useful they believe different skillsets/interests would be for survival.
Competency/Skill Target: Communication, Persuasion, Critical Thinking
Time to Complete: 1 hour
Meeting Type: Face-to-face or Virtual
Category: Team Building

Instructions:
▪    Ask 8 team members to represent one of the eight intelligences (for larger groups you can have 2-3 people represent
     each one) the remaining group members will be the voting audience. The eight intelligences include:
       o Visual-spatial
       o Linguistic-verbal
       o Interpersonal
       o Intrapersonal
       o Logical-mathematical
       o Musical
       o Body-kinesthetic
       o Naturalistic
▪    Provide each of the eight people/teams information on their assigned intelligence.
▪    Give each intelligence team 5 minutes to prepare their argument.
▪    Each intelligence team will present their argument as to how they can help further society on the island and ensure
     survival for the larger group.
▪    The voting group will listen to each argument/presentation and must come to a consensus on what order to eliminate
     the intelligences in, to ensure survival and prosperity for their new island community.
▪    Allow for debate and discussion across the group.

A Shrinking Vessel

Overview: This activity will help avoid having a teammate fall off the circle and work together to figure
out how to keep everyone within the shrinking boundaries.
Competency/Skill Target: Teamwork, Critical Thinking and Problem Solving
Time to Complete: 15- 20 minutes
Materials Needed: A rope
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face
Category: Team Building

Instructions:

▪    Using the rope, make a shape on the floor where everyone can fit into.
▪    Then gradually shrink the space by reducing the size of the shape, so the team will have to think fast
     and work together to keep everyone within the shrinking boundaries.

Office Bingo

Overview: In this activity, the facilitator reads out loud the statements one by one on the bingo
card shared with team members, and then them cross off, or not, their square.
Competency/Skill Target: Team Engagement, Integrity, and Decision-making
Time to Complete: 25-30 minutes
Materials Needed: Bingo Card Print out
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or Virtual
Category: Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:
▪ Generate and email the bingo cards just before the meeting.
▪ Players need to download or hand over print out of Bingo cards during meeting.
▪ One by one, call out the statements on the virtual bingo card. Each time a statement is called
    out, if the team member recognizes it, they must cross it off their virtual bingo card.
▪ Let each virtual team member have the opportunity to share their experiences, jokes, and
    stories about the topic on the bingo card. This will get team have a good laugh and connect.
▪ The bingo winner is the first person who successfully crosses off an entire column, row or
    diagonal line.
▪ Motivate the team with funny dares, example the loser will have to sing a song in the next
    team meeting.
▪ See sample of the Office Bingo card on the side.

Guess Who

Overview: Looking at images, team members need to guess their teammates who submitted those images.
Competency/Skill Target: Team Engagement, Building Relationships and Observational Skills
Time to Complete: 15-20 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or virtual
Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:

▪    Have your team members send a photo of their home offices.
▪    Share the image on screen and then have everyone do the guess work.
▪    Keep the game going with photos of everyone's coffee mugs, desktop backgrounds, or the view outside
     their window, favorite quote, their lunch that day etc.
▪    The one who guesses all the images right will win.

Scattergories

Overview: The game is for team members to write down the least common words they can think of
starting with a specific letter in certain categories presented on screen in order to win points.
Competency/Skill Target: Vocabulary, Time Management and Social Skills
Time to Complete: 15-20 minutes
Meeting Type : Face-to-Face or virtual
Category: Icebreaker

Instructions:

▪    Split the team into two evenly sized groups (if playing in-person), for virtual individual
     participation.
▪    Facilitator will open the following website and share their screen:
     https://swellgarfo.com/scattergories
▪    Set time between 60 – 120 seconds and set category up to 10.
▪    Click on the reset button and then click play.
▪    Using the letter and categories provided, players write down the least common words they can
     think of - 1 word per category.
▪    Facilitator keeps a tally of points for each team.
▪    The person with the highest points wins.

   Leader's Guide to Open Dialogue

PURPOSE

As the business landscape continuously transforms, leaders
must understand the challenges faced within their team and
across the organization.

By fostering open dialogue leaders can ensure teams are
aligned and can navigate these changes effectively.

This guide aims to provide steps to help your team reflect,
revitalize, and renew their commitment to their role, the
team and RealPage.

     2                                                                     ©2024 RealPage Inc.

                                              Proprietary & Confidential

CHANGE IS THE ONLY CONSTANT
Leadership is the key to change success! Our actions determine if employees feel that change is happening to them or if they are a part of the
change effort.

reduces understanding and increases anxiety or anger.

STEPS TO BUILD SUCCESSFUL TWO-WAY CONVERSATIONS
MANAGERS MUST UNDERSTAND HOW CHANGE WILL AFFECT THEIR TEAM, HAVE HONEST CONVERSATIONS
TO ENABLE EMPLOYEE OWNERSHIP, SUPPORT AND DISCUSS HOW EMPLOYEES PLAN TO IMPLEMENT
CHANGE.

      5                                                                                     ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                           Proprietary & Confidential

1. PREPARE THE CONVERSATION
 Set the Agenda

 ➢ Define Objectives
       o Clearly outline the goals of the meeting
 ➢ Prepare Key Points:
       o Focus on the change and its impact

 Choose a Comfortable Setting (in-person/remote)

 ➢ Neutral Environment:
        o Select a location that is comfortable and neutral
 ➢ Inclusive Communication:
        o Ensure the setting promotes open dialogue
        o In-person - seat participants in a circle to assure a sense of equal participation
        o Remote - request for cameras to be on but don't request repeatedly or make
           mandatory

 Invite Participants

 ➢ Inform the Team:
        o Clearly Communicate the meeting's purpose
        o Schedule a 60-90 mins meeting
        o 8-12 participants per group (if possible)
 ➢ Encourage Preparation:
        o Allow team members time to gather their thought and questions

    6                                                                                                             ©2024 RealPage Inc.

                                                                                     Proprietary & Confidential

1. PREPARE THE CONVERSATION (CONT'D)
 USE THESE QUESTIONS TO ENSURE YOU UNDERSTAND YOUR OWN EMOTIONAL REACTION TO THE CHANGE AND HOW THE
 CHANGE WILL AFFECT THE WAY YOUR DIRECT REPORTS GET THEIR WORK DONE.

 Process your own emotional reaction to how you will be affected.
 ➢ What was my initial reaction to the change? Did I feel anxious, frustrated, or excited?
 ➢ What was most the productive thing I did to work through these emotions?
 ➢ What can I learn from my reaction that might apply to how I communicate with my direct reports or how I approach the
   conversation? What tips would I give them?
 ➢ What should I do differently compared to how the change was communicated to me or how I have communicated changes in the
   past?
 ➢ Are there any peers or leaders whose approach to communicating change I admire? How can I imitate them?
 Ensure you understand the implications of the change for your team.

 ➢ Why does the organization have to change and what will success look like?
 ➢ How does this affect my direct reports and their needs and tasks?
 ➢ Does it affect all of them in the same way?
 ➢ When will they be affected, and when do they need to make the changes?
 ➢ How do my direct reports’ behaviors and decisions have to change because of this change? How dramatic will this change feel to them?
 ➢ What do I think are the obstacles and risks of implementing this change? What might they think?
 ➢ Is this change news to them, or are they likely to have heard about it already?
 ➢ Is there a perception of fatigue related to this or other changes? How relevant and how urgent is this information for them?
 ➢ Are there other priorities that I need my direct reports to focus on? How should they balance these with the new demands placed on
   them?
 ➢ Do I have enough information to help my direct reports think creatively about how to support the change? Can I address areas
   of uncertainty that lack sufficient information?
    7                                                                                               ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                  Proprietary & Confidential

 2. OPEN THE CONVERSATION
Opening is done by the designated senior leader and should include the following:
  ➢ A warm welcome and an expression of appreciation for their participation
  ➢ Clear explanation as to why the session is being held and how it is being viewed by the organization (e.g., the description of what led to
    the session and that this is one of an ongoing series of conversations).
  ➢ An explanation of the aim for the session , which should include:
       o Provide a forum for employees to be heard
       o Create a shared understanding of the issues and the impact
       o Further opportunities for employees to be a part of the solution
       o Make sure that everyone knows that they are not only not alone and have support
        o Share description on how the input from this session will be used (i.e., themes and concepts only—no individual attribution)

        o Introduce the moderator/note-taker

  ➢ Recording the session is highly discouraged

Ground rules are a list of terms that participants agree to follow, and the facilitator agrees to uphold during the
session.
  ➢ Commit to making this a safe space for honest expression
  ➢ Share responsibility for including all voices in the conversation
  ➢ Refrain from attributing any comments to a specific individual(s) after the session is over
  ➢ Be honest but constructive—no “bashing” others
  ➢ Be concise to allow others to fully participate
  ➢ Limit distractions and avoid multitasking during the session

        8                                                                                                          ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                      Proprietary & Confidential

 3. DURING THE CONVERSATION
Get employees involved in the conversation.
  ➢ Ask them to speak up: indicate that you have information to share but want to spend most of the time getting their reactions
    and/or ideas.
  ➢ Lead with their interests: Focus early discussions on issues that directly impact the employees.
  ➢ Ask open-ended questions: For example, "What could we be doing better?" or "What are we doing that works well?"
  ➢ Make it safe: Show genuine interest in different perspectives; avoid a critical or dismissive posture.
  ➢ Forge connections: Point out links or contrasts between employee opinions; aim to cultivate a “network effect” rather than a series
    of direct exchanges with you.

Be a good listener
  ➢ Listen, then gather more facts and details: For example, “Tell me more about that,” or “Keep going, I’m following you.”
  ➢ Listen, then validate their challenges: For example, “It sounds like our current plan could make it hard for the team to stay ahead of
    deadlines.”
  ➢ Listen, then clarify meanings: For example, “I hear you saying you are frustrated with the lack of transparency—is that right?”
  ➢ Listen, then encourage elaboration: For example, “Why do you think this problem is so hard to eliminate?”
  ➢ Listen, then invite discovery: For example, “What could we do to make things better?”

Express Empathy and Address Feelings
  ➢ Empathize: "I understand that this change might be diﬃcult for many of you."
  ➢ Normalize Feelings: "It’s normal to feel uncertain or anxious during times like these."
  ➢ Invite Sharing of Feelings: "How are you feeling about the recent changes?”
  ➢ Affirm Emotions: "Your feelings are completely valid and understandable."

      9                                                                                                           ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                    Proprietary & Confidential

3. DURING THE CONVERSATION

Discuss Challenges
  ➢ Identify Challenges: “What challenges are you currently facing due to this change?”
  ➢ Identify Challenges: “What resources or support do you need to feel more comfortable with the changes?”
  ➢ Identify Challenges: “What speciﬁc tools or training would help you adapt to the new environment?”

Offer Support
  ➢ Reassure Team: "We are all in this together, and we will get through this by supporting one another.“
  ➢ Reassure Team: "We are a resilient team, and with everyone’s effort, we can make a successful transition forward."
  ➢ Offer Support: ”We value your contributions and are here to provide resources and support you need.”
  ➢ Offer Support: “Let’s work together to find solutions and make this transition as smooth as possible.”
  ➢ What can I learn from managers in other parts of the organization as to how their teams are implementing the change?
  ➢ How can my team help other teams in making the change?

Foster Open Communication and Collaboration
  ➢ Encourage Open Dialogue: "Please feel free to share any thoughts or ideas you have."
  ➢ Encourage Open Dialogue: “How can we improve our communication during this transition?”
  ➢ Promote Inclusivity: "Everyone’s input is valuable, and we want to hear from all of you."
  ➢ Promote Inclusivity: “What can we do to ensure everyone feels included and valued during this time?”

    10                                                                                                       ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                  Proprietary & Confidential

 3. DURING THE CONVERSATION
Admit uncertainty and the potential implications, where appropriate.
  ➢ Am I acknowledging in clear language a reduction in the workforce, team transfers, impact on benefits, or job security?
  ➢ Am I acknowledging the personal stress of adjusting to new conditions? Am I acknowledging if my direct reports will need to build
    new capabilities?
  ➢ Do I articulate the outcome I expect from this change, and do I admit where I don’t have the answers? Do I articulate what my direct
    reports should and shouldn’t do and where they are free to experiment?
  ➢ Do I admit when I don’t have answers to their questions, and do I know where to find them or can I help my direct reports find them?

Ask questions that stimulate employees to think strategically about how they will be affected and can
contribute to the change.
  ➢ Why is this change important to the organization? Why is it important to our team?
  ➢ How does this change align with your own personal goals? How about with the goals of your teammates? How do you plan to
    contribute to making the change a success?
  ➢ What do you need to know to understand the goal? Who might have the answers? How can we measure if our goals were
    achieved in the short term? In the long term? What will be hard about executing this change?
  ➢ Which of our processes might need to be updated? Which other changes could result from this change? What needs to be
    adjusted in your work or the work of your peers and managers?
  ➢ Has the team or someone else experienced a similar change in the past that we can learn from? Who do you need to work with
    that you don’t already?

      11                                                                                                        ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                   Proprietary & Confidential

 4. FOCUS ON THE FUTURE
USE THE QUESTIONS BELOW TO CHECK IN REGULARLY WITH YOUR DIRECT REPORTS ON HOW THEY ARE MAKING
CHANGES.

Shift Focus to the Future
  ➢ Forward Thinking: "Let’s look ahead and see how we can move forward."
  ➢ Forward Thinking: "“What opportunities do you see arising from these changes?”
  ➢ Uniﬁed Goals: "Together, we can achieve our goals in this new environment."
  ➢ Unified Goals: “How can we work together to achieve our goals moving forward?”

Advise and discuss employees’ plans for implementing the change.
  ➢ Review how your direct reports plan to implement the change using the questions below.
  ➢ Have my direct reports overlooked any activities or new behaviors they should be pursuing? Have they identified appropriate
    success measures that indicate adoption of the new behaviors? At the higher level, do team members share the same objectives
    and behaviors?
  ➢ Are different direct reports learning from each other regarding how they plan to implement the change? Have team members
    identified the same obstacles to change?
  ➢ What can I learn from managers in other parts of the organization as to how their teams are implementing the change?
  ➢ How can my team help other teams in making the change?

Have continuous conversations to identify obstacles and support implementation.
  ➢ It is hard to predict what change will look like in practice, so support your direct reports throughout implementation.
  ➢ Are new projects or initiatives I have assigned supporting or interfering with a direct report’s change objectives or priorities?
  ➢ Are there any obstacles we did not foresee that I can help overcome, or that I should communicate up?
  ➢ Am I keeping my direct reports updated on changing organizational priorities?

      12                                                                                                            ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                     Proprietary & Confidential

5. WRAP-UP/CLOSING

Summarize
  ➢ Recap Discussion: Highlight the main challenges and proposed solutions.
  ➢ Outline Next Steps: Detail the support resources available and immediate next steps.
  ➢ Consider sharing an anonymous survey to gather additional feedback.

Express Appreciation
  ➢ Thank Team: "Thank you all for your openness and valuable input today.“
  ➢ Thank Team: Consider sending a written thank you note to the team.
  ➢ Reinforce Communication: Emphasize the importance of ongoing communication and support.

Follow-up
  ➢ Schedule Ongoing Conversations: Arrange a follow-up session to review progress and address further concerns.
  ➢ Offer Ongoing Support: Ensure a clear plan for continued support and communication.

     13                                                                                                   ©2024 RealPage Inc.
                                                 Proprietary & Confidential

6. TIPS TO STAY ON TRACK
KEEPING A CONVERSATION GOING IS NOT JUST ABOUT TALKING—IT'S ABOUT LISTENING, UNDERSTANDING, AND CONNECTING ON A DEEPER LEVEL.

          Reaffirm the Agenda/Key Topics
01        Regularly refer back to the agenda to remind of the planned topics. This helps anchor the discussion
          and realign to the intended focus.

          Use a Parking Lot
02        A parking lot is a tool that helps you capture and defer any issues or questions that are not relevant or
          urgent for the current discussion.

          Implement Time Management
03        Use a timer/assign time limit to each topic. Gently remind participants when it’s time to move on to
          ensure everyone has an opportunity to share feedback.

          Keep Additional Topics Handy
04        Prepare a few potential conversation topics that will interest the participants you’re talking to ahead of
          time. This will help if the conversation lags and you need keep the conversation going.

          Ask Open–Ended Questions
05        Instead of yes-or-no questions, ask open-ended questions that invite the other person to share more
          information and expand on their thoughts.

     14                                                                                                                     ©2024 RealPage Inc.

                                                                                           Proprietary & Confidential

QUESTIONS OR SUPPORT?

Email Us: HRBP@RealPage.com or contact your assigned HRBP

Team Building and Icebreakers

Thank You!

Contractor Onboarding Process

     1.   The Hiring Manager (HM) sends the completed Onboarding Request Form to the
          Contingent Worker mailbox.

Before onboarding any contractor, ensure that a Purchase Order (PO) has been provided. For U.S.-based contractors, verify
that a background check has been completed. If no background check is in place, initiate the background check in Sterling and
wait for the results before proceeding with onboarding.

     2. Send the onboarding (OB) form to the contractor through DocuSign using the HRSC login or send
        it from the CW mailbox using this email template.

 Use the PowerForm link below for bulk onboarding requests. This is more efficient than DocuSign, as it eliminates the need
 to manually enter each contractor's name and email address:
 https://na2.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=d6587f0a-5b0d-40c8-b8a5-
 691777206413&env=na2&acct=fd8275f7-664a-46d4-9490-fed753571c66&v=2

     3. For contractors under the Non-Payroll company (e.g., US, Outside COC, and FACT), select Add
        Employee (Hire/Rehire) under My Employees in Administration.

     4. For contractors under PH and IND, select Add US/Canadian/International Employee under My
        Employees in Administration.

   5. A new window will open for ID verification. Confirm the ID number, then select the appropriate
      company from the dropdown menu:

            ➢ US, Outside COC, and FACT: Non-Payroll
            ➢ PH: RP PH
            ➢ IND: RP IND

onboarding types.

1. In the Start tab, select Non-Payroll and complete the required fields. Use a dummy SSN (999-99-9999) for
contractors outside COC; use the SSN from the OB form for U.S. contractors.

2. In the Personal tab, use Quick Address Search for U.S. addresses. For addresses outside the U.S., select
Override Smart Tax Address, enter the address manually, and choose Foreign National as the State/Province.
Complete all required fields, including Alternate Email Address, Date of Birth, Gender, PO Number, and End
Date.

       Tip: Most business units require a PO. If no PO is provided, confirm with the Hiring Manager (HM)
       whether a PO is required, as some business units (e.g., WhiteSky) may not require one.

3. Under the Dates tab, enter the Hire Date based on the request form. The remaining fields will populate
automatically.

4. Under the Jobs/Payroll tab, complete all required fields using the onboarding spreadsheet. Only fields
with provided data are required.

Job Information

   ➢ Supervisor
   ➢ Job: Always select CONTRACT – SUPPLEMENTAL LABOR
   ➢ Alternate Job Title: If blank in the spreadsheet, leave the field unchanged.
   ➢ Location: If the location is not available in the dropdown, select 27 – R-NONPayroll.
   ➢ Cost Center: Use the value provided in the spreadsheet.
   ➢ Division, Business Unit, and Department: Copy the values from the Hiring Manager's
     hierarchy/details.
   ➢ Equipment: Based on the request form, use either of the following codes:
                  ▪ No computer – NC
                  ▪ Windows PC/Laptop –WIN
                  ▪ Cloud Access – CP
                  ▪ Mac PC/Laptop – MAC

Payroll Information

   ➢ Pay rate: refer to the contractor request form. If no pay rate is provided, use the default rates below.

     RP PH and IND
   ➢ For Employee Type: select CON – Contractor/Consultant
   ➢ Full/Part time: Always Full time
   ➢ For other fields, either refer to the request form or select the only option from the dropdown.

5.   Do not change anything and skip the Direct Deposit tab until Summary tab by clicking Next. Review all the
     information on this page and click Save. This will now create the CW’s UKG profile including their EID.

onboarding in UKG using the default details below. Complete the remaining onboarding steps following
the standard Non-Payroll (NP) onboarding process and populate all required fields.

   Contractor Form for job details. Follow the NP process for all remaining fields and onboarding steps.

           Common Issue: Contractor Cannot Be Found in Salesforce

           If the contractor was recently onboarded:

               •    Contact User Access (UserAccess@RealPage.com) and the SailPoint Support Team
                    (SailPointSupport@RealPage.com) for assistance.

                    investigation.

below. Inform them that the profile has been created and that the CW will receive a separate email from

customized as needed. However, ensure that all key details and reminders are included.

          deadlines.

      •   To terminate a contractor/consultant, email ContingentWorker@realpage.com.

Common Issue: Contractor Access Revoked Due to Missed Extension

If a contractor's access is revoked because the extension was not submitted on time, advise the
Hiring Manager that they are responsible for requesting access reactivation.

A. If the contractor is still active in UKG:

    1. Update the contractor's end date in UKG.

       SailPoint Support (SailPointSupport@RealPage.com) to request access reactivation.

       the end date.

    2. Once the contractor is active in UKG, have the Hiring Manager contact User Access and

extension update by HRSC.

Talent Services | Process Documentation Library

TALENT SERVICES PROCESS GUIDE
UKG Termination Approval Reminder Process
Monitoring daily pending termination alerts and reminding UKG Termination Approvers

 Process boundary: Talent Services monitors the daily alert and sends reminders. The HRBP / UKG
 Termination Approver owns the approval action in UKG.

1. Purpose

The purpose of this process is to remind UKG Termination Approvers of pending termination tasks in their UKG inbox
to ensure timely approval and processing of employee separations. Timely approval helps ensure that separating
employees are appropriately processed in UKG and that system access is removed in accordance with the
employee’s separation.

2. Scope

This process applies to termination requests that are pending approval in UKG and require action from the
designated HR Business Partner (HRBP) or termination approver.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

 Role                      Responsibilities                                           Ownership boundary
 Talent Services           Review the daily pending termination alert in the HRSC     Does not approve the
                           mailbox; identify pending approvals; send reminder         termination in UKG.
                           emails to the appropriate UKG Termination Approver /
                           HRBP; follow up according to the established reminder
                           process.
 HRBP / UKG                Review pending termination tasks in the UKG inbox;         Owns the approval action
 Termination               approve the termination in a timely manner; ensure the     and downstream
 Approver                  termination is properly processed so system access         termination processing.
                           can be removed as applicable.
 HRIS                      Send the daily pending termination alert to the HRSC       Reporting source; not the
                           mailbox.                                                   approval owner.

4. Process Overview

 Stage                Talent Services action                                        Outcome
 1. Alert             Receive the daily pending termination alert from HRIS in     Visibility into pending UKG
 received             the HRSC mailbox.                                            approvals.
 2. Review            Identify employee, request, approver / HRBP, status and      Clear reminder population.
                      relevant details.
 3. Reminder          Email the assigned UKG Termination Approver / HRBP           Approver is notified.
                      and request timely approval.

                                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only    UKG Termination Approval Reminder Process

                                                            Internal Use
Talent Services | Process Documentation Library

 Stage                Talent Services action                                       Outcome
 4. Approval          HRBP reviews and approves the task in UKG.                   Termination can continue.
 5.                   Termination process continues, including system              Separation processing
 Continuation         access removal as applicable.                                proceeds.

5. Detailed Step-by-Step Process

Step 1 - Receive the daily pending termination alert

   1. Access the HRSC mailbox and locate the daily pending termination alert from HRIS.
   2. Confirm the alert provides visibility into termination requests that remain pending approval in UKG.

 Control point: Use the daily alert as the starting point for identifying pending termination approvals.

Step 2 - Review pending terminations

   3. Review the alert and identify each termination request that is still pending approval.
   4. Capture or confirm the employee name, termination request, assigned UKG Termination Approver / HRBP,
       pending status, and any other relevant information in the alert.

Step 3 - Send the reminder

   5. Send an email reminder to the assigned UKG Termination Approver / HRBP.
   6. Identify the employee or termination request requiring action.
   7. Advise the approver that the termination is pending in their UKG inbox.
   8. Request that the termination be reviewed and approved as soon as possible.
   9. Reinforce that timely approval prevents delays in the separation process and system access removal.

Step 4 - HRBP approves the termination in UKG

   10.The HRBP / UKG Termination Approver reviews the pending task in their UKG inbox.
   11.The approver approves the termination request in UKG.
   12.Once approved, the termination request proceeds through the appropriate termination process, including
       system access removal as applicable.

 Ownership boundary: Talent Services monitors and reminds; the HRBP / UKG Termination Approver
 owns approval in UKG.

6. Process Flow

Use the following visual map as the quick-reference view of the end-to-end process:

                                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only    UKG Termination Approval Reminder Process

                                                            Internal Use
Talent Services | Process Documentation Library

                                    Figure 1. UKG Termination Approval Reminder Process

7. Key Control

 Key control: Timely approval of termination requests is critical. Pending approvals may delay the
 employee separation process and the timely removal of system access.

   • Talent Services reviews the daily pending termination alert consistently.
   • Talent Services reminds the appropriate UKG Termination Approver / HRBP promptly.
   • The HRBP / UKG Termination Approver owns the approval action in UKG.
   • The termination process continues after approval, including system access removal as applicable.

8. Completion Criteria

 Scenario                                 Process result
 Pending termination identified           Reminder is sent to the assigned UKG Termination Approver / HRBP.
 Termination approved in UKG              Request proceeds through the appropriate termination process.
 Approval remains pending                 Continue the established reminder / follow-up process and maintain
                                          clear ownership with the designated approver.

                                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only   UKG Termination Approval Reminder Process

offboarding_process_in_ukg_revised.text:
Internal Use

                                  Offboarding Process in People Assist

This document outlines the standard offboarding process in UKG (People Assist) for voluntary and
involuntary separation following manager approval. It defines the responsibilities of HR Shared Services
(HRSC) in processing employee terminations, initiating the digital clearance process, and coordinating
workflow activities through completion of the offboarding process.

1. Resignation Ticket Initiation
    • Employee submits a resignation request via HR Help – for voluntary
    • HRBP submits termination request via HR Help – for involuntary
    • Ticket will be received by HRSC once manager approved the ticket – for voluntary
    • For involuntary, the ticket will not be routed to the manager for approval. Instead, the HRBP will
        complete the “Manager Only” section.

Access UKG Pro > People Assist > Request Manager > All Requests > Employee Resignation
Form/Involuntary Separation Form

2. Ticket Facilitation – Once you have confirmed that the ticket is under your bucket, please click Manage
Request so that ownership of the ticket will be assigned to you.

Once the information in the “Manager Only” section has been completed, process the employee
termination in UKG. Return to the ticket and update the request status to “Support Request Closed”. Then
change the status from Closed to “Archived” to ensure all submitted documents are saved in the employee’s
folder within Document Manager.

    •    Add the following comment in the ticket before closing the ticket:

“This has been facilitated in UKG. Offboarding instructions will be sent to your email address shortly.

We will now proceed with closing this ticket.
Should you have any additional or follow-up questions, please feel free to reopen this ticket or submit a new one, and
we will be happy to assist you.”

                                          For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                  Internal Use

Note: For involuntary cases, the ticket will not be routed to the manager for approval. Instead, the HRBP will
complete the “Manager Only” section.

For voluntary cases, the ticket will be routed to the manager for approval. In cases where the “Manager
only” field contains missing or incomplete information, advise the Manager to update and complete the
required details before proceeding.

Employee Termination in UKG
Process Owner: HR Shared Services
System: UKG Pro
Trigger: Approved resignation request with manager-provided details

    •   Access Employee Profile
        • Log in to UKG Pro
        • Search for and open the employees’ UKG Profile
    •   Navigate to Termination Section
        • Go to Personal
        • Select Termination Info
    •   Click Terminate Employee

                                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                 Internal Use

        •  Enter Termination Details
        •  Complete the required fields based on the manager’s information provided in the ticket:
           ✓ Last Working Date
           ✓ Termination Date
           ✓ Termination Reason
           ✓ Regrettable / Non-Regrettable (as confirmed by the manager)
    •   Review and Submit
        • Review all entered details for accuracy
        • Submit the termination in UKG

Important Note:
Employee terminations must be processed in UKG immediately upon receipt of an approved resignation
request. Delays should be avoided to maintain compliance and data accuracy.

A late termination occurs when the resignation is entered after the effective termination date and may
result in compliance exceptions or audit findings.

The Termination Date should not be the same as the Last Working Date. The Termination Date must be the
day immediately following the employee's Last Working Date. For example, if the Last Working Date is June
15, the Termination Date should be June 16.

                                      For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                              Internal Use

3. Digital Clearance Process Setup
Prerequisite:
    • Employee resignation form ticket is closed and Termination has been lodged in UKG
HRSC Actions:
    ➢ Navigate to:
         UKG > My Team > People Assist > Digital Process Manager > Select New Process
    ➢ Complete the process details:
              o Process Template: PH Employee Offboarding
              o Process Name: Add at the beginning the Employee’s name
              o Limit to Employees Within Scope: Talent Services
              o Employee Name
              o Due Date: 30days from Separation Date

   ➢   Click Create Process
   ➢   Click Publish

                                    For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                               Internal Use

4. Publish Digital Clearance
HRSC Actions:
    ➢ Publish the clearance process to initiate departmental signoffs
    ➢ Ensure the Publication Date matches the clearance initiation date
    ➢ Click Publish now
Departments Involved:
    • IT
    • Payroll
    • Finance
    • Operations

                                     For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                 Internal Use

5. Task Completion & Workflow Progression
HRSC Actions:
     ➢ Complete assigned HRSC tasks in sequence
     ➢ First required task:
         Enter Termination in UKG
     ➢ Mark the task as Complete once finished
System Behavior:
     • Upon completion, remaining tasks automatically route to the next assigned users (e.g., IT, Payroll,
         Finance, Ops)

Retraction process:

Confirm Approval
   • Confirm with the employee's manager that the resignation retraction has been approved.
   • Copy the assigned HR Business Partner in the email communication for visibility.
Cancel Termination in UKG
   • Submit a request to the HRIS team to cancel the employee's termination transaction in UKG.
Cancel Digital Manager Clearance
   • Cancel the employee's clearance process in Digital Manager to prevent further offboarding
        activities.
Update Salary Holding Tracker
   • Remove the employee's name from the Salary Holding Tracker to ensure they are no longer included
        in salary hold monitoring

                                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                 Internal Use

Clearance Step:

   1.   UKG Termination Lodged
        Mark this task as Complete to confirm that HRSC has successfully processed and lodged the
        employee’s termination in UKG.
   2.   Review and Acknowledge PHI Offboarding Instructions
        The employee review and acknowledge receipt of the PHI Offboarding Instructions sent to their
        work email address. If the separation is involuntary, offboarding instructions should be sent to the
        employee manually, as they will no longer have access to their work email address to receive
        automated communications.
   3.   Departmental Sign-Offs (to be completed within 7 days from the employee's separation date)
             o IT Offboarding Sign-Off – Completed by the IT team once the employee has returned all
                 company-issued equipment within the required 7day return period.
             o Finance Offboarding Sign-Off – Completed by the Finance team upon verification of all
                 applicable financial clearances.
             o Manager Offboarding Sign-Off – Completed by the employee's manager. If the manager's
                 sign-off has not been provided within 7 days from separation, the clearance process may
                 still be endorsed to Payroll for final pay computation, provided that both IT and Finance
                 sign-offs have been completed.
   4.   For Final Pay Computation
        HRSC will endorse the clearance to Payroll for final pay computation once the required
        departmental sign-offs have been completed. IT and Finance sign-offs are mandatory. If only the
        Manager Offboarding Sign-Off remains pending, the clearance may still proceed to Payroll, as the
        manager sign-off is considered optional for final pay processing.
   5.   First Final Pay Status Update
        HRSC must notify the separated employee that their final pay has been endorsed to Payroll for
        processing, provided that the IT team has confirmed through their notes that all company assets
        have been returned. Mark this task as Complete once the notification has been sent.
   6.   Second Final Pay Status Update
        HRSC must provide a follow-up update to the employee on the 10th day after the first final pay
        status update has been sent, provided that Payroll has not yet sent the final pay computation. Mark
        this task as Complete once the notification has been sent.
   7.   Final Pay Computation Finalized – Employee Notified
        The Payroll team is responsible for notifying the employee once the final pay computation has been
        completed.
   8.   Final Pay Disbursed
        The Finance team must complete this task once the employee's final pay has been successfully
        disbursed to their designated bank account.

Additional Steps for Unreturned Company Assets
The following steps apply only when the employee has not returned company-issued equipment within the
prescribed return period:

   1.   Reminder to Return Equipment
        HRSC must send a reminder to the employee regarding any outstanding company assets. This task

Please ensure that the salary of separating employees is placed on hold in the next applicable payroll cutoff.

                                 PH Onboarding Process Guide (Talent Services)

Overview

This guide provides a step-by-step overview for initiating and managing the onboarding process
within RecruitIQ.

Talent Acquisition will move the candidate to “Start Offer” so the offer letter can be created.

The onboarding process in RecruitIQ will be initiated after the onboarding discussion with the candidate has
been completed.

Link: Onboarding simplied Process Map

Step-by-Step Workflow:

    1.   The TA team messages the OB team to request an onboarding discussion. The request is usually
         submitted through the GC. The TA team forwards the meeting link to the candidate. Conduct the
         discussion and send the pre-employment reminder email to the candidate. Sample Email - PRE-
         EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS RealPage Inc..msg

    2.   Endorse the candidate for PEME via email using the appropriate branch contact details provided
         below. Sample Email - PEME Endorsement

    3.   Process Candidate in RecruitIQ.

         Move the candidate to “Pre-Hire Screening PH” so the candidate receives the background-check
         form link through AppTrac. Confirm that the package type is entered in the job details. If it is missing,
         contact the TA team for an update. Then move the candidate to “Start Onboarding” so the candidate
         receives the ICIMS link to upload requirements and acknowledge the iforms.

         RecruitIQ navigation:

    •    Select the candidate’s name to begin the onboarding process.

                                         For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                            Internal Use

•   Click Advance, then choose “Pre-hire screening PHI”.

                                  For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                 Internal Use

Note: Before moving the candidate to Pre-hire screening, confirm that the package type is entered in the
job details. If it is missing, contact the TA team for an update.

    •   Click Advance again, then choose “Start Onboarding” - This will give the candidate access to the
        iCIMS onboarding portal, where they can complete their required onboarding tasks, such as

                                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                           Internal Use

    uploading their government numbers and acknowledging required forms, including the Code of
    Conduct.

•   A pop-up window will appear prompting you to complete the following steps:
        ➢ New Hire:
           o In the Notifications section, always select “Do not Send Rejection Notice”
           o In the Actions section, verify that all options (checked by default) are correct:
               ✓ Move Job Folder to “Closed” under the Action section.
               ✓ Move candidate to Folder “Current Employee”
               ✓ Ensure that the “Start Date" matches the “Internal Req Job Start Date". The Start
                  Date is used to determine task due dates and system integrations.
           o Click OK to continue.

                                 For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                    Internal Use

➢   Submit to Workflow and Add tasks
    o Select the appropriate New Hire Category or the Onboarding Packet based on their
       location. The default onboarding tasks will automatically populate based on the selected
       category.
    o Click Submit to continue.

                          For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                Internal Use

            o   On the Add Task process, the required iForms will be automatically selected based on the
                submitted New Hire Category/Onboarding Packet .
            o   When using the "Add Task" process, you still have the opportunity to review and confirm the
                iForms that will be sent to the candidate based on the selected New Hire Category.
            o   From this section, you can:
                ✓ Add additional iForms if needed.
                ✓ Delete any iForms that were included by default but should not be sent to the candidate.

This step ensures that only the appropriate onboarding forms are assigned, helping maintain accuracy and
relevance in the onboarding process.

Note: Please ensure that the PH PII Form has been sent to the candidate as part of the onboarding
requirements.

                                      For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                   Internal Use

➢   Email
    o Click Send to email the Onboard Welcome Letter to the candidate. This provides access
       to the New Hire Portal where they can complete onboarding tasks.

                         For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                             Internal Use

•   Once the welcome email has been sent to the candidate, you will be automatically routed to
    the Employee tab. In this section, please ensure the following fields are accurately completed:
        ➢ Device Choice - Check the CM file to confirm the asset assigned by Talent Acquisition (TA).

    Note: The Device Choice may automatically change once the candidate receives the iCIMS link.
    During the completion of their information, candidates are required to select their preferred device;

Then click “Save”

 Process summary

   At a glance
   Talent Acquisition endorses the candidate to Talent Services for the onboarding discussion.  Key    decision
  1. Is the          points

                                    US Onboarding Process Guide (Talent Services)

Overview

This guide outlines the step-by-step process for initiating and managing onboarding in the system once a candidate is
ready to be hired.

Talent Acquisition will move candidates to "Pre-Hire Screening Initiated-US" once the candidate has accepted their offer
letter.

Talent Services is responsible for processing the onboarding of all candidates listed under the "Pre-Hire Screening
Initiated-US" folder.

Step-by-Step Process

Recruiters will notify Talent Services Team via MS Teams Direct Message or through the Group Chat) for Internal
Candidates to be processed.

Note: Onboarding Team to monitor the Pre-hire screening folder as well as the US onboarding GC.

SLA: Talent Services will process the onboarding within three (3) hours upon receipt of the candidate endorsement from
the TA team.

    1.   Locating the Candidate (Two Ways)

    1A.
    •   On iCIMS Landing Page, navigate to the "Pre-Hire Screening Initiated-US" folder

    •    Click the ‘Dropdown’ icon near the Business Unit to search for Candidate’s Requisition ID or Name

                                           For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                  Internal Use

1B.
•   On iCIMS Landing Page, search for the candidate by using the Requisition ID or Name
•   Choose ‘Requisition’ (recommended) if searching the candidate using Requisition ID; choose ‘Person’ if searching
    for the candidate using Name

•    Go to ‘Candidates’ Tab, and always click the ‘Dropdown’ icon near ‘Offer Management’ or ‘Pre-Hire Screening
     Initiated – US’ to locate the correct candidate then click the name of the candidate to start the onboarding
     process

2.   Candidate’s Information

•    Under ‘Overview’ Tab, copy the Candidate’s Email Address under Contact Info, and the Recruiter’s Name

                                       For RealPage Internal Use Only

•    Go to ‘Offer’ Tab, download or view the Signed Offer Letter.

•    Offer Letter is the sole basis for checking the candidate’s information and keeping the US New Hire Tracker up
     to date, information such as:
          o Job Title
          o Reporting To
          o Start Date
          o Orientation Date

               o    Jennifer Honea

communicated, updated, and accurately reflected in UKG prior to the employee’s start date.

2. Background Check Monitoring

a. Background Check Review

ada_faqs.title: ADA FAQs
ada_faqs.text:
ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act)
                    Frequently Asked Questions

1. What Is a Reasonable Accommodation? A reasonable accommodation is an
   adjustment or change that helps you perform the essential functions of your job or
   access the workplace.
2. What is the Interactive Process? The interactive process is a collaborative
   conversation between you, Human Resources, and Unum to determine an effective
   accommodation. This process includes reviewing your request, discussing job
   responsibilities, exploring accommodation options and making adjustments if
   needed over time. If an accommodation is not effective, you may request a review or
   modification.
3. Do I have to say “ADA” to request help? No. Any request for workplace support
   related to a medical condition may trigger the ADA process.
4. How long does the process take? Timelines vary based on documentation and
   complexity, but requests are reviewed as promptly as possible.
5. Can my accommodation be denied? Some requests may not be reasonable or
   feasible, but alternative options will be explored whenever possible.
6. Will requesting an accommodation affect my job? No. Retaliation is prohibited
