loa_information.text:
RealPage Leave of Absence
                                             How to Apply for Leave of Absence
Please contact Unum to apply for FMLA, Parental Leave and/or Short Term Disability (STD) by visiting portal.unum.com
or by calling 1-866-868-6737. Have your physician’s name, phone number, and fax number available. Be sure to stay in
contact with Unum during your leave and update them of any changes to your status. Unum MUST be contacted when
you officially start your leave to activate your claim.
                                                                 FMLA
FMLA entitles eligible employees to take unpaid, job and benefit-protected leave for specified family and medical
reasons. Eligible employees are entitled to twelve work weeks of leave in a rolling 12-month period for:
    •    The birth of a child or placement of a child with the employee for adoption or foster care,
    •    The care for a child, spouse, or parent who has a serious health condition,
    •    A serious health condition that makes the employee unable to work, and
    •    Reasons related to a family member’s service in the military, including
              o    Qualifying exigency leave – leave for certain reasons related to a family member’s foreign deployment, and
              o    Military caregiver leave – leave when a family member is a current servicemember or recent veteran with a
                   serious injury or illness.
*All time off for the reasons listed above must be certified by our third-party administrator, Unum. It is your responsibility to ensure
Unum gets the certification required to approve the claim.
                                                       Short Term Disability
Short Term Disability (STD) provides you with 60% of your salary if your leave of absence is related to your own personal
medical needs. If you are applying for maternity leave, the benefit is equal to 100% of your salary.
The first week of medical leave is paid via RealPage payroll with available PTO/unused sick time up to state requirements.
Once your disability claim has been approved by Unum, STD benefits will begin on the 8th day of your leave (or upon
exhaustion of required state paid sick time). Weekly disability checks from Unum will be sent to your home address on
file unless you enroll in Direct Deposit through Unum.
* CA, MA, NJ, NY, CT, RI, DC, CO, OR and WA employees- a portion of paid leave benefits are paid by the state. Please log onto
your corresponding state family/medical leave website to start your state claim.
Massachusetts/New York: Contact Unum to coordinate your leave.
New Jersey Residents: Contact Unum to coordinate your disability claim. Family leave claims should be started at
https://nj.gov/labor/myleavebenefits/.
                                          Short Term Disability Tax Withholdings
Disability benefits are currently considered taxable income for Social Security (FICA) Tax, Federal Income Tax (FIT) and,
in some cases, State Tax purposes. FICA taxes are mandatory and are automatically deducted from disability income
benefits issued during the 6 calendar months immediately following the month in which you last worked. The tax
regulations require withholding of FIT at 25% of the taxable portion of your benefit. This FIT deduction is reflected in
your benefit check. To change the FIT percentage withholding for your STD benefits, notify your STD Claim
Representative with Unum.
                                                            Paid Time Off
40 hours of PTO/unused sick time up to state requirements will be applied to your first week of medical leave if you have
the hours available. *First week of maternity leave is paid at 100% directly through Unum.

                                                         Benefit Premiums
While you are out on leave of absence, RealPage will continue to pay the employee and employer portion of your benefit
premiums. Upon return, missed premiums will be collected by doubling deductions until you are caught up.

paid_parental_leave_policy.title: Paid Parental Leave Policy
paid_parental_leave_policy.text:
Internal Use

Paid Parental Leave Policy
Employees are eligible to take a leave of absence from work due to the birth, adoption or placement of a child
under the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended (ADA). The Paid
Parental Leave Policy works in conjunction with FMLA, ADA and state regulations to provide employees with paid
time off in the 12-month period following the birth or placement of a child. The purpose of parental leave is to
enable the employee to care for and bond with a newborn, newly adopted or newly placed child. Paid Parental
Leave is independent of, and in addition to, the six (6) weeks of Pregnancy Leave available to birthing parents
immediately following childbirth, as discussed further below. This policy applies to births, adoptions or
placements that occurred on or after January 1, 2023.

Please also refer to the Family and Medical Leave (FMLA) and Leave of Absence Policy section of the Employee
Handbook for further information regarding employee benefits under FMLA, ADA, and Short Term Disability (STD).

Parental Leave
RealPage, Inc. will provide all full-time, regular employees, up to six weeks of paid leave compensated at 100% of
their weekly rate of base pay during the 12-month period immediately following the birth of an employee’s child
or the placement of a child with an employee in connection with adoption or foster care. Paid Parental Leave will
run concurrently with any other state leave benefits and will not result in over 100% of your weekly base pay.
Parental leave can be taken in no less than 14 calendar day increments. Advanced noticed is required for parental
leave taken in increments and is subject to manager approval based on business needs.

State Paid Leave

RealPage Parental Leave runs concurrently with state Paid Family and Medical Leave. RealPage Parental Leave
payments will be paid as a supplement to the state provided benefits for the first six weeks of leave. The
supplemental payments are paid through our Third-Party Administrator, Unum. Please contact
leaves@realpage.com for more information.

Requesting Parental Leave
RealPage Benefits, in partnership with Unum, is the administrator of the Leave of Absence process. To initiate a
parental leave, contact leaves@realpage.com or Unum at https://portal.unum.com/. Additional instructions for
filing a leave can be found via the Benefits SharePoint site. Employees must provide at least 30 days’ notice of
the requested leave (or as much notice as practicable if the leave is not foreseeable).

Eligibility
All regular, full-time teammates in the U.S who are scheduled to work 30 or more standard hours per week
are eligible 3 months after date of hire.

Employees must meet the following criteria:

    •    Be a full-time, regular employee at the time leave begins (temporary and part-time employees are not
         eligible for this benefit).
    •    Be a parent of a newly born or newly adopted child or a foster child who has been newly placed in
         employee’s home (in either case, the child must be age 17 or younger).
              o The adoption of a stepchild is excluded from this policy.

Eligible employees will receive a maximum of six weeks of Parental Leave for the birth, adoption or placement of
a child/children. A multiple birth, adoption or placement occurs (e.g., the birth of twins or adoption of siblings)
will not increase the total amount of Parental Leave granted for that event. In addition, in no case will an

                                           For RealPage Internal Use Only

                                                    Internal Use

employee receive more than six weeks of Parental Leave in a rolling 12-month period, regardless of whether more
than one birth, adoption or foster care placement event occurs within that 12-month time frame.

When both parents are RealPage employees who meet eligibility guidelines, each parent is entitled to six weeks of
Parental Leave.

Additional information:
     •   Employees must take Parental Leave in no less than 14 calendar day increments.
     •   Employees must use all Parental Leave during the 12-months following the event or any remaining time
         will be forfeited.
     •   Upon separation of the individual’s employment, the employee will not be paid for any unused Parental
         Leave for which they were eligible.

Coordination with Other Policies:
Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA)

     •   Parental Leave taken under this policy will run concurrently with leave under FMLA.
     •   The leave will be counted toward the 12 weeks of available FMLA leave per 12-month period.
     •   All other requirements and provisions under the FMLA will apply.
     •   An employee who takes Parental Leave who does not qualify for FMLA leave will be granted the same
         level of job protection as if the employee were on FMLA-qualifying leave.

Pregnancy Leave
     •   Full-time, regular employees who give birth to a child are entitled to six (6) weeks of Pregnancy Leave,
         which runs concurrently with FMLA, immediately following childbirth. To be eligible for Pregnancy
         Leave, an employee must meet the requirements to receive short-term disability payments under
         RealPage’s STD policy and provide appropriate verification and documentation to RealPage and the
         company’s third-party STD carrier.
     •   Employees who are eligible for Pregnancy Leave will receive 100% of their weekly base pay for six (6)
         weeks regardless of birth type. The first week of Pregnancy Leave will be compensated by RealPage;
         beginning the second week of Pregnancy Leave, employees will be compensated through STD.

     •   Paid Parental Leave may begin at the conclusion of Pregnancy Leave and will be offset by any additional
         state provided benefits. In no event will compensation for employees on Pregnancy Leave or Paid
         Parental Leave exceed 100% of weekly base pay.
     •   STD payments will be made at 100% of weekly base pay for six weeks regardless of birth type.

Employee Benefits While on Leave

     •   The company will maintain all benefits for employees during Parental Leave period just as if they were
         taking PTO.
     •   Missed benefit premiums will be collected by taking double deductions upon return until the premiums
         are recouped.
     •   Scheduled holidays will not extend the total Parental Leave entitlement.

                                          For RealPage Internal Use Only

          Internal Use

                           RealPage, Inc. 401(k) Retirement Plan
                             SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION

                                                ARTICLE 1
                                              INTRODUCTION

RealPage, Inc. has adopted the RealPage, Inc. 401(k) Retirement Plan (the “Plan”) to help its employees
save for retirement. If you are an employee of RealPage, Inc., you may be entitled to participate in the Plan,
provided you satisfy the conditions for participation as described in this Summary Plan Description (“SPD”).
In addition, if you are an employee of any of the following Employers, you also may be entitled to participate
in the RealPage, Inc. 401(k) Retirement Plan.

       A.L. Wizard LLC
       Active Building, LLC
       NovelPay LLC
       DepositIQ and RentersIQ Insurance Agency
       RP Newco XXVII LLC
       LeaseStar LLC
       Level One LLC
       My Building LLC

       Property Photos.com LLC

       RealPage Vendor Compliance LLC
       LeaseLabs LLC
       RP Newco V LLC
       RP Newco XV LLC
       Windsor Compliance LLC

This SPD is designed to help you understand the retirement benefits provided under the Plan and your rights
and obligations with respect to the Plan. This SPD contains a summary of the major features of the Plan,
including the conditions you must satisfy to participate under the Plan, the amount of benefits you are entitled
to as a Plan participant, when you may receive distributions from the Plan, and other valuable information
you should know to understand your Plan benefits. We encourage you to read this SPD and contact the Plan
Administrator if you have any questions regarding your rights and obligations under the Plan. (See Article 2
below for the name and address of the Plan Administrator.)

This SPD does not replace the formal Plan document, which contains all of the legal and technical
requirements applicable to the Plan. However, this SPD does attempt to explain the Plan language in a non-
technical manner that will help you understand your retirement benefits. If the non-technical language under
this SPD and the technical, legal language under the Plan document conflict, the Plan document always
governs. If you have any questions regarding the provisions contained in this SPD or if you wish to receive a
copy of the legal Plan document, please contact the Plan Administrator.

The Plan document may be amended or modified due to changes in law, to comply with pronouncements by
the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or Department of Labor (DOL), or due to other circumstances. If the Plan
is amended or modified in a way that changes the provisions under this SPD, you will be notified of such
changes.

    The Plan Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day administration and operation of the Plan. For

Plan Year:

    Many of the provisions of the Plan are applied on the basis of the Plan Year. For this purpose, the Plan
    Year is the calendar year running from January 1 – December 31.

Plan Compensation:

    In applying the contribution formulas under the Plan (as described in Article 5 below), your contributions
    may be determined based on Plan Compensation earned during the Plan Year. However, in determining
    Plan Compensation, no amount will be taken into account to the extent such compensation exceeds the
    compensation dollar limit set forth under IRS rules. For 2025, the compensation dollar limit is $350,000
    ($360,000 in 2026). Thus, for Plan Years beginning in 2025, no contribution may be made under the
    Plan with respect to Plan Compensation above $350,000 ($360,000 in 2026). For subsequent plan
    years, the compensation dollar limit may be adjusted for cost-of-living increases. Note that the
    compensation dollar limit described above does not apply to Salary Deferrals contributed to the Plan.

    For purposes of determining Plan Compensation, your total taxable wages or salary is taken into account
    including any Salary Deferrals you make to this 401(k) plan and any pre-tax salary reduction
    contributions you may make under any other plans we may maintain, which may include any pre-tax
    contributions you make under a medical reimbursement plan or “cafeteria” plan. Plan Compensation also
    generally includes compensation for services that is paid after termination of employment, as long as
    such amounts are paid by the end of the year or within 2½ months following termination of employment,

            Any wages or salary you receive from a “related employer,” unless that “related employer”

            Continuation payments to disabled Participants paid after severance of employment

             achievers award (ACWRD), referral bonuses (17), on-call pay (OCALL). Further, inclusions to
             plan compensation include the following: maternity (MAT40) and parental leave (PAT80), award
             (A) and award overtime (AOT), quarterly award (QPR) and quarterly award overtime (QPROT),
             event pay (EVENT), lieu of notice (L), retention bonus (RETBN), trail commission (TCOM), MIP
             and PIP bonuses (MIPPIP), bonus (B), commission (C), and commission overtime (COT).

    Period for determining Plan Compensation. For purposes of determining Plan Compensation, only
    compensation you earn while you are a participant in the Plan will be taken into account. Thus, any
    compensation you earn while you are not eligible to participate in the Plan will not be considered in
    determining Plan Compensation.

    You will reach Normal Retirement Age under the Plan when you turn age 65.

                                              ARTICLE 3
                                         DESCRIPTION OF PLAN

Type of Plan. This Plan is a special type of retirement plan commonly referred to as a 401(k) plan. Under
the Plan, you may elect to have a portion of your salary deposited directly into a 401(k) account on your
behalf. This pre-tax contribution is called a “Salary Deferral.” As a pre-tax contribution, you do not have to
pay any income tax while your Salary Deferrals are held in the Plan, and any earnings on your Salary
Deferrals are not taxed while they stay in the Plan.

You also may choose to make contributions to the Plan on an after-tax basis, by designating your Salary
Deferrals as Roth Deferrals. While you are taxed on a Roth Deferral in the year you contribute to the Plan,
you will not be taxed on the contribution or earnings attributable to Roth Deferrals under the Plan when you
elect to withdraw your Roth amounts from the Plan, as long as your withdrawal is a qualified distribution. See
the discussion of Roth Deferrals under Article 5 below.

In addition to your own Salary Deferrals, if you satisfy the eligibility conditions described in Article 4 below,
you may be eligible to receive an additional Employer Contribution under the Plan. If you are eligible to
receive an Employer Contribution, we will deposit such contribution directly into the Plan on your behalf. Like
the pre-tax Salary Deferrals discussed above, any Employer Contribution we make to the Plan on your
behalf and any earnings on such amounts will not be subject to income tax as long as those amounts stay in
the Plan. You will not be taxed on your Employer Contributions generally until you withdraw such amounts
from the Plan. Article 5 below describes the Employer Contributions authorized under the Plan.

This Plan is a defined contribution plan, which is intended to qualify under Section 401(a) of the Internal
Revenue Code. As a defined contribution plan, it is not covered under Title IV of ERISA and, therefore,
benefits are not insured by the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation.

Pre-Tax Salary Deferrals. If you make Salary Deferrals to the Plan, you will not have to pay income taxes
on such amounts or on any earnings until you withdraw those amounts from the Plan.

Consider the following examples:

   If you earn $30,000 a year, are in the 12% tax bracket, are eligible to participate in the Plan and you
    elect to save 3% (or $900) of your salary under the 401(k) Plan this year, you would save $108 in
    Federal income taxes (12% of $900 = $108).

   If you earn $30,000 a year, are in the 12% tax bracket, are eligible to participate in the Plan, and you
    elect to save 5% (or $1,500) of your salary under the 401(k) Plan this year, you would save $180 in
    Federal income taxes (12% of $1,500 = $180).

   If you earn $42,000 a year, are in the 22% tax bracket, are eligible to participate in the Plan and you
    elect to save 5% (or $2,100) of your salary under the 401(k) Plan this year, you would save $462 in
    Federal income taxes (22% of $2,100 = $462).

As you can see, the more you are able to put away in the Plan and the higher your tax bracket, the greater
your tax savings will be. In addition, if the amount of your Salary Deferrals grows due to investment earnings,
you will not have to pay any Federal income taxes on those earnings until such time as you withdraw those
amounts from the Plan.

                                              Top Heavy Benefits

A plan that primarily benefits key employees is called a top heavy plan. For this purpose, key employees are
defined as certain owners of an employer and officers with a specified level of compensation. A plan is
generally a top heavy plan when more than 60% of all account balances under the plan are attributable to
key employees. The Plan Administrator will determine each year whether the plan is a top heavy plan.

If the Plan becomes top heavy in any Plan Year, non-key employees who are eligible to receive a top heavy
contribution under the Plan generally will receive a minimum contribution equal to the lesser of 3% of Plan
Compensation or the highest percentage provided to any key employee (as defined in the Plan). This
minimum contribution may be different if the Employer maintains another qualified plan. For this purpose,
any Employer Contributions and Matching Contributions may be taken into account in determining whether
the top heavy rules are satisfied. In applying the top heavy rules, any eligible non-key employee who is
employed at the end of the year is entitled to the top heavy minimum, regardless how many hours the
employee works during the year.

    (4)     You need the distribution to prevent your eviction or to prevent foreclosure on your mortgage. The

            federally-declared disaster. Your principal residence or principal place of employment at the time
            of the disaster must be located in a federally-declared disaster area designated for individual
            assistance.

Participant rights. As a participant in the Plan, you are entitled to certain rights and protections under the
Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). ERISA provides that all Plan participants shall
be entitled to:

       Examine, without charge, at the Plan Administrator’s office, all documents governing the Plan,
        including insurance contracts and collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and a copy of the
        latest annual report (Form 5500 series) filed by the Plan Administrator with the U.S. Department of
        Labor.
       Obtain copies of documents governing the operation of the Plan, including insurance contracts and
        collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and copies of the latest annual report (Form 5500
        series) and updated SPD, upon written request to the Plan Administrator. The Plan Administrator
        may assess a reasonable charge for the copies.
       Receive a summary of the Plan’s annual financial report. The Plan Administrator is required by law to
        provide each participant with a copy of this summary annual report.
       Obtain a statement telling you whether you have a right to receive benefits under the Plan and, if so,
        what your current benefits are. You must request this statement in writing and you may only request
        this statement once a year. The Plan Administrator will provide the statement free of charge.
       File a claim for benefits.

Prudent Actions by Plan Fiduciaries. In addition to creating rights for Plan participants, ERISA imposes
duties upon the people who are responsible for the operation of the Plan. These people, called “fiduciaries,”
have a duty to operate the Plan prudently and in the best interests of you, other Plan participants and
beneficiaries. You may not be fired or otherwise discriminated against in any way solely to prevent you from
obtaining a Plan benefit or exercising your rights under ERISA.

Enforcement of Rights. If you have a claim for benefits under the Plan that is denied or ignored, in whole or
in part, you have a right to know why this was done, to obtain copies of documents relating to the decision
without charge, and to appeal any denial, all within certain time schedules. Under ERISA, there are steps
you can take to enforce the above rights. For example, if you request a copy of Plan documents or the latest
annual report from the Plan and do not receive the requested documents within 30 days, you may file suit in
a federal court. In such a case, the court may require the Plan Administrator to provide the documents and
pay you up to $110 a day until you receive the documents, unless the documents were not sent because of
reasons beyond the control of the Plan Administrator. If you have a claim for benefits which is denied or
ignored, in whole or in part, you may file suit in a state or Federal court. In addition, if you disagree with the
Plan’s decision or lack thereof concerning the qualified status of a domestic relations order that affects the
payment of benefits under the Plan, you may file suit in federal court. If the Plan’s fiduciaries misuse the
Plan’s money, or if you are discriminated against for asserting your rights, you may seek assistance from the
U.S. Department of Labor, or you may file suit in a federal court. The court will decide who should pay court
costs and legal fees. If you are successful, the court may order the person you have sued to pay these costs
and fees. If you lose, the court may order you to pay these costs and fees, for example, if it finds your claim
is frivolous.

Assistance with Questions. If you have any questions about the Plan or this SPD, you should contact the
Plan Administrator. If you have any questions about your rights under ERISA, or if you need assistance in
obtaining documents from the Plan Administrator, you should contact the nearest office of the Employee
Benefits Security Administration, U.S. Department of Labor, listed in your telephone directory or the Division
of Technical Assistance and Inquiries, Employee Benefits Security Administration, U.S. Department of Labor,
200 Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, D.C. 20210. You may also obtain certain publications about
your rights and responsibilities under ERISA by calling the publications hotline of the Employee Benefits
Security Administration.

Claim for Benefits. Benefits will normally be payable under the Plan without the need for a formal claim.
However, if you feel you are entitled to benefits under the Plan that have not been paid, you may submit to
the Plan Administrator a written claim for benefits. Your request for Plan benefits will be considered a claim
for Plan benefits, and it will be subject to a full and fair review. The Plan Administrator will evaluate your
claim (including all relevant documents and records you submit to support your claim) to determine if benefits
are payable to you under the terms of the Plan. The Plan Administrator may solicit additional information
from you, if necessary, to evaluate the claim.

If the Plan Administrator determines the claim is valid, then you will receive a statement describing the
amount of benefit, the method or methods of payment, the timing of distributions and other information
relevant to the payment of the benefit.

If the Plan Administrator denies all or any portion of your claim, you (and your authorized representative, if
applicable) will receive within a reasonable period of time (not to exceed 90 days after receipt of the claim
form), a written or electronic notice setting forth the reasons for the denial (including references to the
specific provisions of the Plan on which the decision is based), a description of any additional information
needed to perfect your claim, and the steps you must take to submit the claim for review. If the Plan
Administrator determines that special circumstances require an extension of time for processing your claim, it
may extend the 90-day period described in the prior sentence to 180 days, provided the Plan Administrator
provides you with written notice of the extension and prior to the expiration of the original 90-day period. The
extension notice will indicate the special circumstances requiring an extension of time and the date by which
the Plan Administrator expects to render its decision.

If the Plan Administrator denies your claim, you will have 60 days from the date you receive notice of the
denial of your claim to appeal the adverse decision of the Plan Administrator. You may submit to the Plan
Administrator written comments, documents, records and other information relating to your claim for benefits.
You will be provided, upon request and free of charge, reasonable access to, and copies of, all documents,
records and other information relevant to the claim. The Plan Administrator’s review of the claim and of its
denial of the claim shall take into account all comments, documents, records and other information relating to
the claim, without regard to whether these materials were submitted or considered by the Plan Administrator
in its initial decision on the claim.

If the Plan Administrator denies your claim for benefits after appeal, you will receive within a reasonable
period of time (not to exceed 60 days after receipt of the appeal), a written or electronic notice setting forth
the reasons for the denial (including references to the specific provisions of the Plan on which the decision is
based), and a description of your right to bring an action under ERISA Section 502(a). If the Plan
Administrator determines that special circumstances require an extension of time for processing your appeal,
it may extend the 60-day period described in the prior sentence to 120 days, provided the Plan Administrator
provides you with written notice of the extension and prior to the expiration of the original 60-day period. The
extension notice will indicate the special circumstances requiring an extension of time and the date by which
the Plan Administrator expects to render its decision. If the Plan Administrator denies your claim for benefits
upon review, in whole or in part, you may file suit in a state or Federal court.

If the Plan Administrator makes a final written determination denying your claim for benefits, you may
commence legal or equitable action with respect to the denied claim upon completion of the claims
procedures outlined under the Plan. Any legal or equitable action must be commenced no later than the
earlier of 180 days following the date of the final determination or three years following the proof of loss. If
you fail to commence legal or equitable action with respect to a denied claim within the above timeframe, you
will be deemed to have accepted the Plan Administrator’s final decision with respect to the claim for benefits.

    Such health care professional will not be an individual (or a subordinate of such individual) who was
    consulted in connection with the initial adverse benefit determination.

    If the Plan obtained advice from medical or vocational experts in connection with a claimant’s adverse
    benefit determination (without regard to whether the advice was relied upon in making the benefit
    determination), such experts will be identified.

    The Plan Administrator shall notify the claimant of the Plan’s benefit determination on review within a
    reasonable period of time, but not later than 45 days after receipt of the claimant’s request for review by
    the Plan, unless the Plan Administrator determines that special circumstances (such as the need to hold
    a hearing) require an extension of time for processing the claim. If the Plan Administrator determines that
    an extension of time for processing is required, written notice of the extension shall be furnished to the
    claimant prior to the termination of the initial 45-day period. The extension notice will indicate the special

    circumstances requiring an extension of time and the date by which the Plan expects to render the
    determination on review.

    Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination on Review. The Plan Administrator will provide a claimant
    with written or electronic notification (written in a culturally and linguistically appropriate and
    understandable manner) of any “adverse benefit determination.” The notice of adverse benefit
    determination on review will set forth:
       The specific reason or reasons for the adverse determination;
       Reference to the specific Plan provisions on which the determination is based;
       That the claimant is entitled to receive, upon request and free of charge, reasonable access to, and
        copies of, all documents, records, and other information relevant to the claimant's claim for benefits;
       A description of any voluntary appeal procedures offered by the Plan and the claimant's right to
        obtain the information about such procedures;
       A description of the claimant's right to bring an action under ERISA §502(a) (including a description
        of any applicable contractual limitation period that applies to the claimant’s right to bring such an
        action);
       A discussion of the decision, including an explanation of the basis for disagreeing with or not
        following:
           The views presented by the claimant to the Plan of health care professionals treating the
            claimant and vocational professionals who evaluated the claimant;
           The views of medical or vocational experts whose advice was obtained on behalf of the Plan in
            connection with a claimant's adverse benefit determination, without regard to whether the advice
            was relied upon in making the benefit determination; and
           A disability determination regarding the claimant presented by the claimant to the Plan made by
            the Social Security Administration;
       If the adverse benefit determination is based on a medical necessity or experimental treatment or
        similar exclusion or limit, an explanation of the scientific or clinical judgment for the determination,
        applying the terms of the Plan to the claimant's medical circumstances, or, alternatively, a statement
        that such explanation will be provided free of charge upon request; and
       The specific internal rules, guidelines, protocols, standards or other similar criteria of the Plan relied
        upon in making the adverse determination or, alternatively, a statement that such rules, guidelines,
        protocols, standards or other similar criteria of the Plan do not exist.

    The Plan Administrator will assist in language translation of a notice of adverse benefit determination on
    review, if necessary. Translation assistance can include recommending translation services, providing
    verbal assistance and providing the notice in a non-English language upon request.

add_or_change_direct_deposit_accounts_ca.title: Add or Change Direct Deposit Accounts - Canada
add_or_change_direct_deposit_accounts_ca.text:
Add or Change Direct Deposit Accounts - Canada
Provides step-by-step instructions on how to add or change your Canadian direct deposit
accounts.

 UKG Pro

Add or Change Direct Deposit Accounts - Canada

Direct deposit account types
You can create three types of direct deposit accounts: available balance, flat amount, or
percent amount.

Percent amount
Percentage amount accounts receive a percentage of the net pay to the designated
direct deposit account.

All percentages are rounded to the nearest hundredth. For example, 90.99% is rounded
up to 91%. 99.4% is the greatest percentage allowed.

As a best practice, create an available balance account along with a percentage account
to capture the entire amount.

  Note You can create either flat amount or percent amount accounts, but you cannot create a
  combination of both flat and percent accounts.

Flat amount
A ﬂat dollar amount of the net pay is sent to a flat amount direct deposit account.

Depending on your conﬁguration, the system may process partial amounts for ﬂat
amount accounts in two diﬀerent ways:

    By default, if there are not enough funds to cover the ﬂat amount, then no funds will
    be sent to flat amount account. Instead, all partial funds are sent to the available
    balance account.

    If the system is conﬁgured to allow partial dollar amounts, the following message is
    displayed: "Accounts with an active status and an amount are displayed in the order
    they will be funded." In this case, when a deposit is less than the dollar amount
    designated for the flat amount account, the partial amount is deposited. The system
    funds the accounts in the priority order listed on the screen until the pay is
    exhausted.

  Note You can create either flat amount or percent amount accounts, but you cannot create a
  combinate of both flat and percent accounts.

Available balance
After other direct deposit account rules have been applied, the remaining net pay is sent
to the designated available balance account.

As a best practice, when only one account for 100% of the amount is required, create a
single available balance account.

You cannot have multiple available balance accounts regardless of the status (active or
inactive). To add a new available balance account, you must ﬁrst archive the existing
available balance account. Archiving the account will remove the account but save the
historical data.

Add or change direct deposit accounts
Add or change direct deposit accounts on the Direct Deposit Detail page.

    Navigation: Menu > Myself > Pay > Direct deposit
    Navigation: Menu > My team > Team overview > Team overview > select an
    employee > Pay > Direct deposit
    Navigation: Menu > Administration > Employee overview > Employee overview >
    select an employee > Pay > Direct Deposit

  1. From the Direct Deposit Summary page, complete one of the following:
         To add a direct deposit account, select Add.
         To change direct deposit account information, select an account from the list.

  2. From the Direct Deposit Detail page, enter a description, if available.

  3. Enter a bank name, if needed.

  4. Enter a branch number and a banking institution number.

  5. Enter an account number.

  6. Select a status of Active or Inactive for the account.

  7. In the Amount section, complete one of the following:
          To specify a specific dollar amount, select the Flat Amount radio button and
          enter the dollar amount without a dollar sign.
          To specify a specific percentage, select the Percent Amount radio button and
          enter the percentage without a percent sign.
          To specify the available balance, select the Available Balance radio button.

  8. In the Order field, enter a number between 01 and 98 to denote priority order in
     which your flat amount and percent amount accounts will be funded until the pay is
     exhausted. Available balance accounts are automatically assigned an order of 99.

  9. Select Save.

 10. Select Submit. The Direct Deposit Summary page appears with the new account.

Create multiple direct deposit accounts
You can add multiple direct deposit accounts if the accounts receive a flat amount or a
percentage of the pay.

When you set up multiple accounts, as a best practice, create an available balance type
to account for any to account for any remaining amount and to allow for rounding.

Refer to the table below for an example scenario.

 Account Type                                        Amount

 Percentage Account 1                                80%

 Percentage Account 2                                10%

 Available Balance Account                           Any remaining amount

  Note You cannot have multiple Available Balance accounts regardless of the status (active or
  inactive). To add a new Available Balance account, you must first archive the existing Available
  Balance account. Archiving the account will remove the account but save the historical data.

  Tip To deposit all of your net pay into one account, the recommended best practice is to create
  a single Available Balance account.

Archive direct deposit accounts
When you archive a direct deposit account, the system saves the historical data.

    Navigation: Menu > Myself > Pay > Direct deposit
    Navigation: Menu > My team > Team overview > Team overview > select an
    employee > Pay > Direct deposit
    Navigation: Menu > Administration > Employee overview > Employee overview >
    select an employee > Pay > Direct Deposit

  1. From the Direct Deposit Summary page, select the check box next to the Account.

  2. Select the Archive button.

  3. Select OK in the confirmation dialog box.
     Archived appears in the Status column.

         Note You cannot reactivate an archived account. However, you can select the account link
         to review the account details in the Direct Deposit Detail page. Using the information
         displayed on that page, you can reenter the account with an Active status, if needed.

update_your_canada_personal_tax_credits_.text:
Update Your Canada Personal Tax Credits and Source
Deductions Returns
Provides step-by-step instructions on how to update your federal and provincial Personal Tax
Credits Return and Source Deductions Return.

 UKG Pro

Update Your Canada Personal Tax Credits and
Source Deductions Returns

Canada Tax Credits and Deductions
The federal and provincial Personal Tax Credits Return forms certify the tax credits you
claim for your tax withholding elections.

The Canada Federal government uses Form TD1, Personal Tax Credits Return, and each of
the following provinces and territories have their own version of Form TD1: Alberta, British
Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Northwest
Territories, Nunavut, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Saskatchewan, and Yukon.

The province of Quebec uses Form TP-1015.3-V, Source Deductions Return (English) or
Formulaire TP-1015.3, Déclaration pour la retenue d'impôt (French).

  Important If you have a change in circumstance that requires an updated Personal Tax Credits
  Return or Source Deductions Return and you do not submit an updated form, you may be
  subject to penalties from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or Revenu Quebec (RQ).

Update Your Canada Federal Personal Tax Credits Return
If your tax status or situation has changed, update your Federal Form TD1, Personal Tax
Credits Return.

Complete this form if one of the following situations applies:

    You have a new employer or payer, and you will receive salary, wages, commissions,
    pensions, employment insurance benefits, or any other remuneration.

    You want to change amounts you previously claimed (for example, the number of
    your eligible dependents has changed).

    You want to claim the deduction for living in a prescribed zone.

    You want to increase the amount of tax deducted at source.

 Note Remember to update your provincial Personal Tax Credits Return or Source Deductions
 Return when you update your Federal Form TD1, if required.

Navigation: Myself > Pay > Income Tax > Things I Can Do > Add/Change Personal Tax
Information

  1. At the Personal Tax Information page, from the Add/Change Personal Tax
     Information section, select the Federal Personal Tax Credits Return (TD1).

 2. In the Non-residents section, indicate whether you are a resident of Canada.
         If you are a resident of Canada, continue to the next section.
         If you are not a resident of Canada, select I am a non-resident of Canada, and
         then indicate your country of permanent residence and whether your world
         income is included in determining your taxable income.

 3. In the More than one employer or payer at the same time section, indicate whether
    you have more than one employer:
         If you do not have more than one employer, continue to the next section.
         If you have more than one employer at the same time and you have already
         claimed personal tax credit amounts on another form, select the checkbox, and
         then continue to the end of the form.

 4. In each section, for Lines 2 - 12, select the section header and enter the required
    details for each credit you are claiming.

 5. In the Total Claim Amount field, confirm that the amount is correct and update your
    previous responses, if required.

 6. If applicable, in the Additional tax to be deducted field, enter an amount to be
    withheld each pay period.

  7. If applicable, in the Deduction for living in a prescribed zone field, enter the
     appropriate deduction amount.

      Note Select the Full Instructions link to view complete details on the prescribed zone
      deduction requirements.

 8. If applicable, select the Total income less than total claim amount option.

      Note If you select this option, the sections for Lines 2 - 12 are unavailable and the Total
      Claim Amount on Line 13 is set to $0.

 9. At the top of the page, select Next.

 10. Review the completed form for accuracy.

         If the form is accurate, select the checkbox to certify the form, and then select
         Sign & Save.
         If you need to update the form, at the top of the page, select Back.

Update Your Provincial Personal Tax Credits Return
If your tax status or situation has changed and you are subject to provincial income tax
(PIT) outside Quebec, update your provincial Form TD1, Personal Tax Credits Return.

Complete this form if one of the following situations applies:

    You have a new employer or payer, and you will receive salary, wages, commissions,
    pensions, employment insurance benefits, or any other remuneration.

    You want to change amounts you previously claimed (for example, the number of
    your eligible dependents has changed).

    You want to increase the amount of tax deducted at source.

  Note Remember to update your Federal Form TD1, Personal Tax Credits Return, when you update
  your provincial personal tax credits, if required.

Navigation: Myself > Pay > Income Tax > Things I Can Do > Add/Change Personal Tax
Information

  1. At the Personal Tax Information page, from the Add/Change Personal Tax
     Information section, select the provincial Personal Tax Credits Return (TD1).

  2. In the Non-residents section, indicate whether you are a resident of Canada.
          If you are a resident of Canada, continue to the next section.
          If you are not a resident of Canada, select I am a non-resident of Canada, and
          then indicate your country of permanent residence and whether your world
          income is included in determining your taxable income.

  3. In the More than one employer or payer at the same time section, indicate whether
     you have more than one employer:
          If you do not have more than one employer, continue to the next section.
          If you have more than one employer at the same time and you have already
          claimed personal tax credit amounts on another form, select the checkbox, and
          then continue to the end of the form.

  4. In each section, for Lines 2 - 9, select the amount field and enter the required details
     for each credit you are claiming.

  5. In the Total Claim Amount field, confirm that the amount is correct and update your
     previous responses, if required.

  6. If applicable, select the Total income less than total claim amount option.

      Note If you select this option, the sections for Lines 2 - 12 are unavailable and the Total
      Claim Amount on Line 13 is set to $0.

  7. At the top of the page, select Next.

  8. Review the completed form for accuracy.
         If the form is accurate, select the checkbox to certify the form, and then select
         Sign & Save.
         If you need to update the form, at the top of the page, select Back.

Update Your Quebec Source Deductions Return
If your tax status or situation has changed and you are subject to provincial income tax
(PIT) in the province of Quebec, update your Federal Form TD1, Personal Tax Credits
Return.

  Note Remember to update your Federal Form TD1, Personal Tax Credits Return, when you update
  your Quebec source deductions, if required.

Navigation: Myself > Pay > Income Tax > Things I Can Do > Add/Change Personal Tax
Information

  1. At the Personal Tax Information page, from the Add/Change Personal Tax
     Information section, select Source Deductions Return (TP-1015.3-V) or
     Déclaration pour la retenue d'impôt (TP-1015.3).

  2. In the More than one employer or payer at the same time section, indicate whether
     you have more than one employer:
          If you do not have more than one employer, continue to the next section.
          If you have more than one employer at the same time and you have already
          claimed personal tax credit amounts on another form, select the checkbox, and
          then continue to the end of the form.

  3. In each section, for Lines 2 - 9, select the section header and enter the required
     details for each deduction you are claiming.

  4. In the Personal tax credits (Line 10) field, confirm that the amount is correct and
     update your previous responses, if required.

  5. If applicable, in the Additional income tax to be withheld field, enter an amount to
     be withheld each pay period.

  6. If applicable, in the Deductions section, enter the appropriate deduction amounts
     for living in a prescribed northern zone or deductible support payments.

         Note Select the Full Instructions link to view complete details on the prescribed northern
         zone deduction requirements.

   7. If applicable, select the I request exemption from withholding income tax option.

  8. At the top of the page, select Next.

  9. Review the completed form for accuracy.
         If the form is accurate, select the checkbox to certify the form, and then select
         Sign & Save.

fa_pol_01_payroll_administration_policy_.title: FA-POL 01 - PAYROLL ADMINISTRATION POLICY (1)
fa_pol_01_payroll_administration_policy_.text:
POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
RealPage commits to provide our employees with the correct pay at the right time. RealPage also ensures that we adhere to tax and labor laws governing compensation and statutory compliance.
This policy aims to communicate how RealPage manages our payroll and follows thru to this commitment.
ELIGIBILITY
This policy applies to all RealPage Employees (Exempt or Non-Exempt, Intern, Part-Time or Full-Time Employee).
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Human Resource Department-Reports the list of New Hires, Separated Employees and Employee Movements. Process the approval of Incentives, Referrals and Medical Reimbursements.
Finance Department- Processes the payroll instruction and submits to payroll vendor. Complies with BIR requirements. Processes the final pay of the separated employees.
Third Party Service Provider- Processes the payroll and submit to RP Philippines for review and approval. Processes final pays for inclusion in the year – end tax annualization.
 DEFINITION OF TERMS
Employee Movement Report (EMR) -Employee Movement Report is an HR report submitted to payroll team every 5th and 20th of the month that contains New Hire Employees, Separated Employees, Employee Change of Status, Employee Data Updates and Payroll Adjustments and Deductions.
Master list- Employee Masterfile that contains Employee data such as, Name of Employee, Date of Birth, Date of Hire, SSS, TIN & PHIC Number, Bank Account Number, Cost Center, Department, Monthly Salaries, Income and Allowances, Address, Position or Designation, Employee Status/Type.
Payroll Instruction Report- A payroll report sent to Third-party processor every 10th and 25th of the month as the basis of the credits, deductions, and payroll inclusion every semi-monthly payroll period.
Payroll Register- Record for a payroll cycle that lists details and breakdown of employee compensation including but not limited to hours worked, gross pay, net pay, deductions, and payroll period covered.
Annualization- Annual process that summarizes and consolidates employees’ compensation income to determine tax due for the employee.
Any excess tax withheld over the “should be” tax due shall be refunded to employees, while the deficiency tax shall be deducted from employees’ future compensation.
BIR FORM 2316- Certificate of Compensation Payment or Income Tax Withheld.  A yearly certificate issued by the employer to employees which declares Withholding Tax on compensation.
ALPHALIST- Alpha List report generates an alphabetical list of employees who have paid tax in line with the Philippine Revenue Regulations. This report also contains information on taxes deducted by employers from their wages. It also includes the computations for tax refund and tax payable at the end of each year. This is submitted to BIR at the end of the year.
BIR 1604CF- Annual Information Return of Income Tax Withheld on Compensation and Final Withholding Taxes filed by a withholding agent who is required to withhold and deduct taxes on compensation paid to employees.
EFPS- Electronic Filing and Payment System. Bureau of Internal Revenue online portal.
GUIDELINES
SEMI – MONTHLY PAYROLL
Calculation of pay shall be based on approved timecards.
Third party service provider processes the semi – monthly payroll and submits to RP Philippines for review and approval.
Seek approval from Country Head and US Head approvers for the reviewed payroll before crediting to the employees’ payroll accounts every payout date.
YEAR – END TAX ANNUALIZATION
HR collates all submitted BIR Form 2316 of newly hired employees and provides copies to Payroll team for Annual Income Tax computation.
Third party service provider computes the annual income and corresponding annual tax at year - end and submits to RP Philippines for review and approval.
RP Philippines files the approved Alpha List and BIR 1604 CF via EFPS on or before January 30th of each year.
PAYROLL DISPUTE
Payroll officers collate all types of disputes received after every payout date for verification.
Valid payroll disputes shall be included in the next payroll period cut off for crediting.
FINAL PAY PROCESSING
All completed clearances forwarded by HR will be processed within Thirty (30) calendar days from termination or separation from employment. Special accommodation to expedite the final pay computation and check releasing can be done with proper request and approval coming from HR department within Seven (7) business days upon receipt of the completed clearance.
Final pays due to employees shall be released after Seven (7) business days upon endorsement to Accounting Team with the signed Quit Claim & Waiver Form issued by HR team.
TIMELINES/PAYMENT SCHEDULE
RealPage follows a semi – monthly payroll processing, Payout schedule is every 15th and 30th of the month. If the 15th and 30th of the month falls on weekend, payroll should be submitted to approvers Three (3) business days before the payout date.

fa_pol_02_final_pay_processing_policy_1.title: FA-POL 02-FINAL PAY PROCESSING POLICY (1)
fa_pol_02_final_pay_processing_policy_1.text:
Document:                          Title:
POLICY                             FINAL PAY PROCESSING POLICY
Document Code:                     Approved By:                                           Effective Date:
FA-POL 02                          Jenny Constantino                                      June 01, 2021

 I.    POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
       This policy aims to pay the accurate amount to an employee who resigns or gets discharged through the last
       day of work including paid time off and deducting accountabilities in compliance with tax and labor laws. To
       establish transparent workflow of final pay processing, the inclusion of remaining income and deductions, and
       to set expectations on the schedule of final paycheck releasing.

 II.   ELIGIBILITY
       This applies to all separated employees: Exempt, Non-Exempt and Interns.

III.   ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
           1. Human Resources Department – Ensure to submit completed clearance in the online tool for final
              pay computation.
           2. Finance Department – Validates and processes the final pay checks/wire transfer of the separated
              employees. Handles Final Pay releasing and Quitclaim.

IV.    GUIDELINES
           1. DEADLINES AND DUE DATES:
                  i. All completed clearances forwarded by HR will be processed within 30 calendar days upon
                     employee separation.
                 ii. Special accommodation to expedite the final pay computation and immediate release of
                     final pay can be done with proper request and approval coming from HR department, re:
                     RIF, Death and with Labor Case.

           2. FINAL PAY INCLUSION:
                  i. Pro-rated 13th Month Pay shall be given based on employees’ tenure for the current year.

                     ii. PTO Conversion for the unused Leave of regular voluntary separated employee. If
                         terminated, no PTO conversion will be credited to employee’s final pay.

                     iii. Attendance adjustments including but not limited to Night Differential, Absences, Tardy,
                          Undertime, Overtime and Language Premium from employee’s last payroll credited shall
                          be included in the final pay.

                     iv. In cases wherein the separated employee has unpaid workdays rendered after the last
                         payroll received, RealPage shall pay the remaining number of days (Basic Pay and
                         Allowances).

                     v. Unpaid benefits before separation such as Wellness Reimbursement, Salary Differential
                        from Maternity Benefits, MIP/PIP and Bonuses shall be part of the final pay computation.

                vi. Year – end tax annualization shall be done to determine if separated employee has a tax
                    refund or tax due. If tax refund, over withheld tax will form part of the final pay. If deficit, total
                    amount shall be deducted from the final pay.

               vii. Miscellaneous income and/or deduction like unreleased incentives and unreturned
                    company accountabilities, unliquidated cash advances shall be included in the final pay
                    computation.

               viii. Deduction of remaining loan balances from SSS and HDMF will be deducted from the
                     employee’s final pay. If the employee opts to settle the loan personally, a notarized affidavit
                     shall be submitted or if deduction shall be transferred to the new employer, the employee
                     shall provide a certification/confirmation from the new employer to waive the deduction on
                     the clearance form. If the amount of Final Pay is not enough to cover the loan balance,
                     available amount will be automatically offset to the loan. Any remaining balance will be
                     communicated to the concerned separated employee.

        3. FINAL PAY RELEASE

                 i. Wire Transfer is scheduled once a week but for manual payment, check releasing is every
                    Tuesday from 2PM to 5PM. If Tuesday falls on a holiday, check releasing will resume on
                    the following week as scheduled.

                ii. The bank account of the separated employee shall be the recipient of the money transfer.
                    Assigning other account numbers do not belong to employee is not allowed. In cases of an
                    employee's death, the final pay due to the separated employee shall be paid to the
                    deceased employee's beneficiary or personal representative.

                iii. Separated employee can authorize someone to claim the final paycheck and certificate of
                     employment given that the separated employee has sent the signed quitclaim before the
                     release and by providing the authorization letter or Special Power of Attorney (SPA) and
                     valid IDs for both separated employee and the authorized representative.

fa_pol_03_timekeeping_policy_1.title: FA-POL 03 - TIMEKEEPING POLICY (1)
fa_pol_03_timekeeping_policy_1.text:
POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
RealPage ensures that all employees are properly compensated for hours of work performed.
The purpose of this policy is to outline the information pertaining to recording, tracking and reporting of employees’ work hours for payroll and benefits calculation.
ELIGIBILITY
This applies to all RealPage Employees.
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Employee - reviews their respective timecards before submitting for approval.
 Non-Exempt Employees – Any individual who has a Job Level of P1 to P04; or may be referred to as Rank-and-File employees.
Exempt Employees – Any individual who has a Job Level of P06 and up or Managers and Up including Officers and Senior Leaders.
Approver– immediate superiors are responsible to approve employee timecards.
Finance Department – processes the approved timecards.
Human Resource Department – implements the Attendance Policies and make sure they are strictly followed.
GUIDELINES
Timekeeping procedure must be in accordance with the RealPage PH Attendance Policy
Employee is responsible to accurately report time worked and submits to the Approver for review and approval for further payroll processing. Submission is on the 3rd day from payout date.
Approvers must ensure that any hours reported by the employee are official business work hours.
Attendance Coverage:
15th payout         		16-30/31 of the previous month
30/31st payout     		1-15th of the current month
Employee and Manager Approvals of timecards are required every pay period.
Timekeeping Definitions
Normal Working Hours. The company operates 24/7, work shift shall consist of Eight (8) work hours a day / Five (5) days a week. Individual managers may set different schedules/shifts for their department and may allow flexible work schedules, and shift schedules to meet the demands of the business. Employee must not exceed Eight (8) hours of work per day, this does not include the One (1) hour lunch break.
Compressed Work Week is considered flexible work schedule where in employees render Eleven (11) hours per day, Four (4) days a week.
Weekly Rest Day. RealPage shall determine and schedule the weekly rest day of employees in compliance with the Labor Code. However, the company shall respect the preference of employees as to their weekly rest day when such preference is based on religious grounds.
Undertime Not Offset by Overtime. RealPage shall comply with the labor code standards, the company will not allow undertime offset by overtime as hourly rate of overtime is higher than the hours missed when an employee works for less than eight hours.
Overtime Pay. Refers to the additional compensation for work performed by employees beyond the prescribed regular hours on a regular day or work rendered in excess of Eight (8) hours during an employee’s rest day/holiday.
Night Differential Pay. Additional compensation given for work rendered between 10:00PM to 6:00AM.
Premium Pay. Additional compensation for work rendered during Regular and Special Holidays and on a Rest Day. RealPage may require a non-exempt employee to work on any holiday but employee shall be paid additional compensation as defined by the Philippine Labor Code.
Time in Lieu (TIL). The company is granting time-in-lieu for work that an exempt employee has rendered during his rest day. Rest day shall refer to Saturday, Sunday or non-working holidays (in the Official Holiday Calendar released by HR every year) Time-in-lieu is granted in place of a rest day/holiday that an exempt employee has failed to avail because he was instead, asked to report and render necessary and indispensable work. Exempt employees who follow US holidays may file for Time-In-Lieu for the difference in the number of days between Philippines and US holidays. (See TIL policy).
 Philippine Holidays - Refers to the “Official Holiday List” published by HR.
US Holidays - Refers to the “Official Holiday List” published by RealPage, Inc.

fa_pol_04_year_end_annualization_process.title: FA-POL 04-YEAR-END ANNUALIZATION PROCESSING POLICY (1)
fa_pol_04_year_end_annualization_process.text:
POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
RealPage strictly complies with the requirement of the Bureau of Internal Revenue in the declaration and reporting of employees’ annual compensation and withholding taxes in a calendar year. This policy aims to provide the guidelines on how to comply to this statutory requirement effectively and efficiently.
ELIGIBILITY
This policy covers all employees’ gross compensation income and withholding taxes on compensation deducted from present and previous employers in a calendar year.
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Human Resource Department – Collates all submitted Form 2316 of newly hired employees and submits to payroll team for annual income tax computation.
Finance Department – reviews the computation of Annual Income and Withholding Taxes done by third party payroll provider. Processes BIR Form 2316 and submits to the BIR along with the Alpha list of Withholding Taxes Computation. Files and submits 1604CF and Alpha list to BIR EFPS website.
Third Party Payroll Vendor – computes annual income and corresponding annual tax and submits to RealPage for review and approval.
DEFINITION OF TERMS
ANNUALIZATION- To summarize and consolidate employees’ compensation income to determine the amount of withholding tax due in a calendar year. Any excess tax withheld over the “should be” tax due shall be refunded to employees, while the deficiency tax shall be deducted from employees’ respective salaries.
BIR FORM 2316 - The BIR Form 2316 is also called the “Certificate of Compensation Payment or Income Tax Withheld”.  A yearly certificate that needs to be issued by the employer to all employees. The employer must indicate the total amount that was paid to the employee and the corresponding taxes withheld during the calendar year.
ALPHALIST - The Alpha List report generates an alphabetical list of employees who have paid tax in line with Philippine Revenue Regulations. This report also contains information on taxes deducted by employers from their employees’ compensation income. It also includes the computations for tax refund and tax payable at the end of the calendar year.
BIR 1604CF - Annual Information Return of Income Tax Withheld on Compensation and Final Withholding Taxes which is filed by a withholding agent who is required to withhold and deduct taxes on compensation that were paid to employees.
DE MINIMIS BENEFITS – Are facilities and privileges of small value and provided by an employer to employees on top of the compensation merely to promote their health, goodwill, contentment, or efficiency. These benefits are exempt from withholding tax on compensation (CWT) and fringe benefits tax (FBT).
CALENDAR YEAR – begins from January 1 to December 31
BIR – Bureau of Internal Revenue
EFPS – Electronic Filing and Payment System
TIMELINES AND DUE DATES
Submission of 2316 from Previous Employer - 	October 1 – December 15
Releasing of Tax Refund - 				January 15
Submission of 1604CF online Filing - 		January 30
Submission of Alpha list - 				January 30
Releasing of BIR 2316 to employees - 		January 30
Submission of BIR 2316 to BIR - 			February 28
GUIDELINES
The current employer who will annualize the employee’s tax due at year – end shall include the employee’s amount of compensation income from previous employer(s) in computing the annualized tax due of the employee.
Employees with an annual compensation income of P250,000.00 and below are exempt from income tax and, consequently, to withholding tax on compensation.
Benefits provided by the employer that exceed the de minimis amount shall be included in the P90,000.00 non – taxable 13th month pay and other bonuses. The amount exceeding the said P90,000.00 non – taxable threshold shall be subject to income tax and consequently, to withholding tax on compensation.
The BIR Form 2316 shall serve as the employee’s annual income tax return if the employee is qualified for substituted filing.

fa_pol_05_13th_month_pay_leave_conversio.title: FA-POL 05-13TH MONTH PAY & LEAVE CONVERSION POLICY
fa_pol_05_13th_month_pay_leave_conversio.text:
POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
This policy aims to pay accurate amount to active and inactive employee in compliance to PD 851 also known as 13th month pay and HR Policy on PTO (Leave).
ELIGIBILITY
This applies to all active & separated employees: Exempt, Non-Exempt and Interns.
 ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Finance Department – Validates and process the 13th month pay of active and separated employees. Update the leave balances and convert the unused leave credits into cash at the end of the year.
GUIDELINES
DEADLINES AND DUE DATES:
13th month pay should be paid to all employees not later than December 24th every year.
 PTO conversion should be paid not later than January 31 of the following year.
CALCULATIONS
The 13th month pay is equivalent to one twelfth (1/12) of an employee’s basic annual salary.
Pro-rated 13th Month Pay shall be given to new hire employee based on tenure for the current year.
13TH month accrual should be based on current employee’s basic pay.
Employees with no LWOP/LOA more than 1 month shall get full 12/12 13th month based on current basic pay.
Employees who filed Maternity/Medical Leave can still get full 13th month accrual.
A deduction of prorated monthly basic pay based on number of days of absences with more than 1 month shall be imposed.
PTO Conversion for the unused PTO credits in a year shall be paid to employees with regular status of employment and total unused leave credits for separated employees. If terminated, no Leave conversion will be credited to employee’s final pay.
PTO credits shall be monetized based on current basic pay.
13th month and PTO conversion shall be subject to withholding tax as prescribed by National Internal Revenue Regulations.
Formula in Converting Monthly Basic Pay to Daily Rate
Daily Rate: Basic Pay x 12/261

fa_pol_07_special_payout_guidelines.title: FA-POL 07- SPECIAL PAYOUT GUIDELINES
fa_pol_07_special_payout_guidelines.text:
POLICY STATEMENT AND OBJECTIVE
This policy aims to define the criteria of special payroll processing outside the regular pay cycle, 15th and 30th of the month.
ELIGIBILITY
This applies to active/in active employees who were not part of the regular pay cycle and covers any payroll adjustments including but not limited to
Retroactive pay adjustments
Bonuses and Incentive
Overtime Corrections
Pay Error corrections
GUIDELINES
Special payroll credits are granted under the following conditions:
1. The error that resulted of NO PAY due to systems failure during the regular pay cycle.
2. Missed in back to work reporting / reinstatement or erroneously reported as inactive.
3. Error in timekeeping that impacted not less than 50% of the total team headcount
4. All payroll adjustments with the conditions not mentioned above will be subject to next applicable regular   pay cycle payout.
APPROVAL PROCESS
1.  All requests must be documented and approved by Ops Leader, HR Head and Payroll Manager
2. Immediate Superior of employee affected must submit a Special Payroll Request Form with Supporting    documents.
3. Request are reviewed for accuracy and compliance before processing
